quiz.mistake: Thinks 180° is obtuse, but it is a straight angle

quiz.q: The corner of a notebook page makes which kind of angle?
quiz.explain: A page corner is a square corner, 90°. That is a right angle.
steps: A page corner is a square corner.
A square corner is a quarter turn = 90°.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up the names right and acute

quiz.q: What kind of angle is 179°?
quiz.explain: 179° is more than 90° and just less than 180°, so it is obtuse.
steps: 179° is less than 180°, so it is not straight.
quiz.mistake: Thinks an angle very close to 180° is straight

quiz.q: At 3 o'clock, what kind of angle do the clock hands make?
quiz.explain: From 12 to 3 is 3 × 30° = 90°, a right angle.
steps: At 3 o'clock, the hands point to 12 and 3: 3 gaps.
quiz.mistake: Forgets that 3 gaps on a clock make a quarter turn

quiz.q: At 1 o'clock, what kind of angle do the clock hands make?
quiz.explain: From 12 to 1 is 30°, which is less than 90°. It is acute.
steps: At 1 o'clock, the hands point to 12 and 1: 1 gap.
30° is less than 90°, so it is acute.
quiz.mistake: Thinks every clock angle is a right angle

quiz.q: At 5 o'clock, the smaller angle between the hands is 150°. What kind of angle is it?
quiz.explain: 150° is between 90° and 180°, so it is obtuse.
steps: 150° is more than 90° and less than 180°.

quiz.q: Harpreet says every angle bigger than 90° is obtuse. Is she right?
options: No, an obtuse angle must also be less than 180°
No, obtuse angles are less than 90°
quiz.explain: Obtuse angles are between 90° and 180°. 180° is a straight angle, so 'bigger than 90°' is not enough.
steps: Obtuse angles are more than 90° AND less than 180°.
180° is straight, and angles like 200° are not obtuse.
So No, an obtuse angle must also be less than 180°.
Answer: No, an obtuse angle must also be less than 180°
quiz.mistake: Forgets the upper limit of 180° for obtuse angles

teach.ask: Gappu asks: 'How do I tell acute, right and obtuse angles apart?'
teach.praise: Super! Smaller than 90 is acute, exactly 90 is right, bigger is obtuse!
teach.nudge: What number do we compare with? What makes an angle acute and what makes it obtuse?

revise.summary: A right angle is 90°, an acute angle is less than 90°, an obtuse angle is between 90° and 180°, and a straight angle is 180°.
focus: Name an angle from its size in degrees
Test angles with a page corner
Name the angle made by clock hands
remember: Right = 90°; acute < 90°; obtuse: more than 90° and less than 180°; straight = 180°
traps: 180° is straight, not obtuse.
179° is still obtuse, not straight.
Bigger than 90° alone is not enough for obtuse.

topics.title: Finding angles in pictures and bodies

learn.hook: Fold a paper fan and open it slowly. Watch it go from sharp to wide — acute to obtuse!
points: A paper fan opened a little makes an acute angle. Opened wide (but not flat) it makes an obtuse angle.
In a house drawing, the walls meet the floor at right angles. The roof top can be acute, and the roof joins the wall at an obtuse angle.
Our legs and arms make angles: legs together make almost no turn, legs in a full split make a straight angle.
To check an angle, compare it with a square corner (right angle).
A five-sided house shape can have 2 right angles, 2 obtuse angles and 1 acute angle.

example.q: A gymnast stretches her legs into a full side split, making a straight line. What angle is between her legs?
steps: Both legs are in one straight line
A straight line is a half turn

learn.reallife: Look at a ladder against a wall, a roof, or the hands of a dancer. Angles are all around us!

games.title: Picture angles
items: A square window has 4 right angles.
Each corner is a square corner.
A paper fan opened just a little shows an obtuse angle.
A gymnast's legs in a full split make a straight angle.
The legs form a straight line.
A five-sided shape can have 2 right angles.
Every roof top is a right angle.
Roof tops can be acute, right or obtuse.

quiz.q: Neha opens her paper fan just a little. What angle does it make?
quiz.explain: A small opening is less than a quarter turn, which is acute.
steps: A small opening is less than a square corner.
Less than a quarter turn is acute.
So the fan makes an acute angle.
quiz.mistake: Thinks any open fan is obtuse

quiz.q: She opens the fan wider, more than a square corner but not flat. What angle now?
quiz.explain: Between a quarter turn and a half turn is obtuse.
steps: Wider than a square corner: more than 90°.

quiz.q: In a house drawing, what angle is made where the wall meets the floor?
quiz.explain: Walls stand straight up from the floor, making a square corner.
steps: Walls stand straight up from the floor.
They make a square corner with the floor.
A square corner is a right angle.
quiz.mistake: Does not compare with a square corner

quiz.q: A drawn roof has a pointed top that is sharper than a square corner. What angle is the top?
quiz.explain: Sharper than a square corner means less than a right angle, so acute.
steps: Sharper than a square corner means less than 90°.
So the roof top is acute.

quiz.q: A gymnast lifts one leg straight up while standing on the other. The legs look like an L. What angle is that?
quiz.explain: An L shape is a square corner, a right angle.
steps: An L shape has a square corner.
So the legs make a right angle.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up right and straight angles

quiz.q: Which body position shows a straight angle?
options: Arms stretched out sideways in one line
Arm bent at the elbow like an L
quiz.explain: Arms stretched out in one line make a straight line, a half turn.
steps: A straight angle is a straight line (half turn).
Bent knees, namaste and an L-shaped elbow are not straight lines.
Arms stretched out sideways in one line make a straight angle.
Answer: Arms stretched out sideways in one line
quiz.mistake: Thinks a bent arm is a straight angle

quiz.q: A five-sided house shape has 2 right angles at the bottom and an acute angle at the top. What are the other 2 angles?
quiz.explain: The roof slopes out from the wall, making angles wider than a square corner: obtuse.
steps: Where the roof meets each wall, it slopes outward.
That angle is wider than a square corner but not flat.
So the other 2 angles are obtuse.
quiz.mistake: Thinks all corners of a house are right angles

quiz.q: Which shape can have 2 right, 2 obtuse and 1 acute angle?
quiz.explain: A pentagon like a house with a pointed roof has this mix. A square and rectangle have only right angles; a triangle has 3 angles.
steps: 2 right + 2 obtuse + 1 acute = 5 angles, so the shape needs 5 corners.
A square and rectangle have 4 right angles; a triangle has 3 angles.
A five-sided house shape has this mix.
quiz.mistake: Does not count the number of corners

teach.ask: Gappu made a paper fan. How do the angles change as I open it more and more?
teach.praise: First acute, then a right angle, then obtuse. My fan is a maths fan!
teach.nudge: What angle do I get with a small opening, and what with a wide one?

revise.summary: We find acute, right, obtuse and straight angles in fans, house drawings and our own bodies by comparing each with a square corner.
focus: Name angles in a paper fan, a house drawing and body poses
Know the angle mix in a five-sided house shape
remember: Walls meet the floor at right angles
A full side split or arms stretched in a line make a straight angle
A five-sided house shape: 2 right, 2 obtuse, 1 acute angle
traps: Pointed does not mean obtuse; a sharp roof top is acute.
Don't think every corner of a house shape is a right angle.

learn.hook: An arrow ends up pointing up after a quarter turn. Where did it start? Think backwards like a detective!
points: We can name a turn as a fraction of a full turn: 1/2, 1/4, 1/8, 3/8, 5/8 …
Fold a paper circle in half, then half again, then half again: you get 8 equal parts. Each is 1/8 of a turn.
2/8 of a turn = 1/4 turn. 4/8 = 1/2 turn. 3/8 is between a quarter and a half turn.
To find where an arrow started, turn it back the same amount the other way.
In degrees: 1/8 turn = 45°, 1/4 turn = 90°, 3/8 turn = 135°, 1/2 turn = 180°.

example.q: An arrow turned 1/4 turn clockwise and now points up (to 12 on a clock). Where did it start?
steps: From 12, a quarter turn anticlockwise goes to 9

learn.reallife: A pizza cut into 8 equal slices shows eighths of a turn around its centre.

quiz.q: An arrow made a 1/2 turn and now points down. Which way did it start?
quiz.explain: A half turn makes it face the opposite way, so it started pointing up.
steps: A half turn makes the arrow point the opposite way.
To go back, turn a half turn again.
Opposite of down is up, so it started pointing up.
quiz.mistake: Thinks a half turn leaves the arrow the same

quiz.q: An arrow made a 1/4 turn clockwise and now points right (to 3). Where did it start?
quiz.explain: Turn back a quarter turn anticlockwise from 3 to reach 12.
steps: To undo a 1/4 turn clockwise, turn 1/4 anticlockwise.
From 3, a quarter turn anticlockwise goes back to 12.
quiz.mistake: Turns back in the same direction

quiz.q: An arrow turned 1/8 turn clockwise and now points to 3 o'clock. Where did it start?
quiz.explain: 1/8 turn is half of a quarter turn. Going back from 3 by half a quarter lands halfway between 12 and 3.
steps: A 1/8 turn is half of a quarter turn.
Half of the way from 3 back to 12 → halfway between 12 and 3.
quiz.mistake: Uses a quarter turn instead of an eighth

quiz.q: How many 1/8 turns make a quarter turn?
quiz.explain: 1/4 = 2/8, so two eighth turns.
steps: Write a quarter turn in eighths: 1/4 = 2/8.
So 2 eighth turns make a quarter turn.

quiz.q: 3/8 of a turn is between which two turns?
options: A quarter turn and a half turn
No turn and a quarter turn
A half turn and a full turn
A full turn and two full turns
quiz.explain: 1/4 = 2/8 and 1/2 = 4/8. 3/8 is between them.
steps: 3/8 is more than 2/8 and less than 4/8.
So 3/8 lies between a quarter turn and a half turn.
Answer: A quarter turn and a half turn
quiz.mistake: Does not change quarters and halves into eighths

quiz.q: Which fraction of a turn is 4/8 the same as?
quiz.explain: 4/8 is half of 8 eighths, so it is a half turn.
steps: 4/8 of a turn is the same as 1/2 turn.

quiz.q: 5/8 of a full turn is how many degrees?
An arrow ends pointing left after a 1/2 turn. Where did it start?
quiz.explain: A half turn reverses the arrow, so it started pointing right.
steps: A half turn reverses the arrow.
Undo it with another half turn from left.
Opposite of left is right, so it started pointing right.

teach.ask: Gappu's arrow points up after a 1/4 turn clockwise. Where was it pointing before? Please teach me!
teach.praise: Turning back a quarter anticlockwise from up gives left. It started pointing left!
teach.nudge: What should I do to undo a turn?

revise.summary: A turn can be named as a fraction of a full turn, like 1/8, 1/4, 3/8 or 1/2. To find where an arrow started, turn it back the same amount the other way.
focus: Name turns as fractions in eighths
Find where an arrow started
Change fractions of a turn to degrees
remember: To undo a turn, turn back the same amount the other way
traps: Don't turn back in the same direction.
Don't use 30° for each eighth; it is 45°.

learn.hook: Guess first, then measure! Your guess gets better every time you check.
points: Make a turn measurer: fold a paper circle into 8 equal parts and open it. Each crease is 1/8 turn.
Estimate the angle first, then place the measurer's centre on the corner and one crease on an arm.
Count the eighths to the other arm. 2 eighths = 1/4 turn (right), less is acute, 3 eighths is obtuse.
We can add turns: 1/2 + 1/4 = 3/4 turn. 1/4 + 1/8 = 3/8 turn.
An equilateral triangle's corner is less than 1/8 + 1/8 turn, so it is acute.
Turns like 1/8 + 1/6 are easy in degrees: 1/8 turn = 45° and 1/6 turn = 60°, so together 105°, an obtuse angle.

example.q: Draw the turn 1/2 + 1/4. How much of a full turn is it?

learn.reallife: Skateboarders talk about a 'one-eighty' — a half turn! They add turns to describe tricks.

quiz.q: What fraction of a full turn is 1/2 + 1/4 turn?
steps: So the turn is 3/4 of a full turn.

quiz.q: What fraction of a full turn is 1/4 + 1/8 turn?
steps: So the turn is 3/8 of a full turn.

quiz.q: Sunil measures an angle with his turn measurer. It covers 3 of the 8 equal parts. What kind of angle is it?
quiz.explain: 3/8 is more than 2/8 (a quarter) but less than 4/8 (a half), so obtuse.
steps: A quarter is 2/8 and a half is 4/8; 3/8 is between them.
More than a right angle, less than straight → obtuse.
quiz.mistake: Thinks 3 parts is small, so acute

quiz.q: An angle covers exactly 2 of the 8 parts. What is it?
quiz.explain: 2/8 = 1/4 turn, which is a right angle.
steps: A 1/4 turn is a right angle.

quiz.q: Jaya guesses an angle is a 1/4 turn. She measures and finds it is 1/8 turn. What kind of angle is it really?
quiz.explain: 1/8 turn is less than a quarter turn, so acute.
steps: Trust the measurement, not the guess: it is 1/8 turn.
1/8 is less than 1/4 (2/8), so less than a right angle.
quiz.mistake: Keeps the guess instead of the measurement

quiz.q: How many degrees is a 3/4 turn?
Which is the best way to check your guess of an angle?
options: Count the corners of the shape
Look at the colour of the shape
Put the centre of the turn measurer on the corner and count the eighths
Measure the length of the arms
quiz.explain: Angle size is the amount of turn between the arms, not their length.
steps: Angle size is the amount of turn between the arms.
Corners, colour and arm length do not tell the turn.
So put the measurer's centre on the corner and count the eighths.
Answer: Put the centre of the turn measurer on the corner and count the eighths
quiz.mistake: Thinks longer arms mean a bigger angle

quiz.q: 1/2 + 1/8 turn is the same as how many eighths?
Meera draws a turn of 1/8 and then 1/6 more. A 1/8 turn is 45° and a 1/6 turn is 60°. How big is the whole turn?
quiz.explain: 45° + 60° = 105°. That is more than a quarter turn (90°) and less than a half turn, so it is obtuse.
quiz.mistake: Subtracts the two turns instead of adding them

teach.ask: Gappu made a paper turn measurer. How do I use it to measure the corner of a shape?
teach.praise: Centre on the corner, a crease on one arm, then count eighths. Easy!
teach.nudge: Where do I put the centre of the measurer?

revise.summary: A paper turn measurer has 8 equal parts. Estimate, then put its centre on the corner and count eighths; turns can also be added like fractions or in degrees.
focus: Measure an angle with a turn measurer
Add turns like 1/2 + 1/4
Name the angle from the number of eighths
remember: 2 eighths = 1/4 turn = right angle; fewer is acute; 3 eighths is obtuse
traps: Don't add the bottom numbers of turns.
Longer arms do not make a bigger angle.

topics.title: Angles on clocks and in shapes

learn.hook: Your wall clock is a giant angle machine. Every number is a hidden 30° jump!
points: A clock face has 12 equal gaps. 360° ÷ 12 = 30°, so each gap is 30°.
To find the angle between the hands at an o'clock time, count gaps and multiply by 30°.
In 5 minutes the minute hand moves one gap, which is 30°.
Letters and shapes have angles too: L has a right angle, V has an acute angle, a rectangle has 4 right angles.

example.q: What is the angle between the clock hands at 4 o'clock? What kind of angle is it?

learn.reallife: Clock hands, scissors, a ladder against a wall and the hands of a cricket umpire show angles every day.

items.q: Angle between the hands at 3 o'clock
Angle between the hands at 4 o'clock

games.title: Smallest to largest
games.prompt: Put these angles from smallest to largest

quiz.q: On a clock face, how many degrees is the turn from one number to the next?
quiz.explain: A full turn is 360° and there are 12 gaps. 360° ÷ 12 = 30°.
quiz.mistake: Divides by the wrong number or uses 12 as the angle

quiz.q: What is the angle between the clock hands at 2 o'clock?
quiz.explain: From 12 to 2 is 2 gaps: 2 × 30° = 60°.
quiz.mistake: Counts only one gap or multiplies by 10

quiz.q: What is the angle between the clock hands at 6 o'clock?
quiz.explain: From 12 to 6 is 6 gaps: 6 × 30° = 180°. The hands make a straight line.
quiz.mistake: Thinks the hands at 6 make a right angle

quiz.q: The minute hand turns clockwise from 12 to 9. How many degrees does it turn?
quiz.explain: 12 to 9 clockwise is 9 gaps: 9 × 30° = 270°, a three-quarter turn.
quiz.mistake: Measures the short way back (90°) instead of the clockwise turn

quiz.q: Which capital letter has a right angle?
quiz.explain: L has a straight up line meeting a flat line, making a square corner.
steps: A right angle is a square corner made by two straight lines.
O, S and C are curved letters with no corners.
L has a straight up line meeting a flat line, so L has a right angle.

quiz.q: How many right angles does a rectangle have?
quiz.explain: Every corner of a rectangle is a square corner, and it has 4 corners.
steps: Every corner of a rectangle is a square corner (right angle).
quiz.mistake: Thinks only a square has right angles

quiz.q: In 20 minutes, through how many degrees does the minute hand turn?
quiz.explain: 20 minutes is 4 gaps of 5 minutes. 4 × 30° = 120°.

quiz.q: Joseph opens a book flat so the two covers make a straight line. What is the angle between them?
quiz.explain: A straight line is a half turn, which is 180°.
steps: The two covers make a straight line.
A straight line is a half turn.
quiz.mistake: Thinks a flat open book is a right angle or a full turn

teach.ask: Gappu asks: 'How can a clock tell me about angles?'
teach.praise: Tick-tock! Each gap is 30 degrees, so I count gaps and multiply. Brilliant!
teach.nudge: How many degrees is one gap on the clock? How do I use the gaps?

revise.summary: A clock face has 12 equal gaps of 30° each. Count gaps between the hands and multiply by 30° to find the angle; letters and shapes have angles too.
focus: Find the angle between clock hands at o'clock times
Find the turn of the minute hand in some minutes
Spot right angles in letters and shapes
remember: In 5 minutes the minute hand turns 30°
traps: Don't measure the short way back when the turn is clockwise: 12 to 9 clockwise is 270°.
Don't use minutes as degrees: 20 minutes is 120°.

learn.hook: The minute hand is at 12. Give it a quarter turn — where does it land? And which way does it turn?
points: The minute hand always turns clockwise: 12 → 1 → 2 → 3 …
A quarter turn of the minute hand moves it 15 minutes: from 12 to 3, or from 3 to 6.
A half turn moves it 30 minutes: from 12 to 6, or from 2 to 8.
Clockwise is the way clock hands move. Anticlockwise is the opposite way.
A quarter turn clockwise from facing up ends facing right; anticlockwise ends facing left.

example.q: The minute hand points to 4. It makes a quarter turn. Where does it point now?

learn.reallife: Screws tighten clockwise and loosen anticlockwise. Most taps open anticlockwise.

games.title: Where does the minute hand go?

items.text: At 12, a quarter turn moves it to ___
At 3, a half turn moves it to ___
At 6, a quarter turn moves it to ___
At 9, a three-quarter turn moves it to ___

games.title: Which way?
items: That is how the word got its name.
Facing up, a quarter turn clockwise makes you face left.
Clockwise from up goes to the right.
Anticlockwise is the opposite of clockwise.
A full turn clockwise and a full turn anticlockwise end in the same place.
Both bring you back to the start.

quiz.q: The minute hand points to 2. It makes a quarter turn. Where does it point now?
quiz.explain: A quarter turn is 15 minutes, which is 3 numbers. 2 + 3 = 5.

quiz.q: The minute hand points to 1. It makes a half turn. Where does it point now?
quiz.explain: A half turn is 6 numbers. 1 + 6 = 7.
quiz.mistake: Always lands on 6 for a half turn

quiz.q: The minute hand points to 10. It makes a quarter turn. Where does it point now?
quiz.explain: 10 + 3 = 13, but the clock goes back to 1 after 12.
steps: A quarter turn = 15 minutes = 3 numbers on the clock.
After 12 the clock goes back to 1. It points to 1.
quiz.mistake: Forgets the numbers go round after 12

quiz.q: The minute hand starts at 12 and makes a three-quarter turn. Where does it point?
quiz.explain: Three-quarter turn = 45 minutes = 9 numbers. It lands on 9.

quiz.q: Which way do the hands of a clock turn?
quiz.explain: Clockwise is named after the way clock hands move.
steps: Clockwise is named after the way clock hands move.
Clock hands never move the other way.

quiz.q: A lizard faces up (north on the wall) and makes a quarter turn. Now it faces left. Which way did it turn?
quiz.explain: From up, turning to the left is opposite to clock hands, so anticlockwise.
steps: Clockwise from up goes to right; anticlockwise from up goes to left.
The lizard went from up to left.

quiz.q: A ladybird faces right and makes a quarter turn clockwise. Which way does it face now?
quiz.explain: Clockwise goes up → right → down → left. From right, the next is down.
steps: Clockwise order: up → right → down → left.
One quarter turn clockwise from right is down.

quiz.q: A bird faces down and makes a quarter turn. Now it faces right. Which way did it turn?
quiz.explain: Clockwise from down would go to left. Going to right is anticlockwise.
steps: Clockwise order: up → right → down → left.
Clockwise from down would go to left.
Going from down to right is the other way: anticlockwise.
quiz.mistake: Does not follow the clock order

teach.ask: Gappu's minute hand points to 3. If it makes a half turn, where will it point, and which way does it move?
teach.praise: A half turn is 6 numbers clockwise, so from 3 it goes to 9!
teach.nudge: How many numbers does a half turn move the hand?

revise.summary: The minute hand always turns clockwise. A quarter turn moves it 15 minutes (3 numbers) and a half turn 30 minutes (6 numbers).
focus: Find where the minute hand points after a turn
Tell whether a turn was clockwise or anticlockwise
traps: Don't forget the numbers go round after 12: 10 + 3 numbers lands on 1.
Don't always land on 6 for a half turn; from 1 it lands on 7.

learn.hook: Facing North, you make three right turns. Which way do you face? Your left hand might know the answer!
points: Clockwise order of directions: North → East → South → West → North.
A right turn is a quarter turn clockwise. A left turn is a quarter turn anticlockwise.
Count quarter turns: 2 quarter turns = half turn (face the opposite way), 4 quarter turns = back to the start.
Different turns can end the same way: 3 quarter turns clockwise = 1 quarter turn anticlockwise.
On a map, a half turn means facing the opposite direction: if you face the school (East), after a half turn you face West.

example.q: Priya faces East and makes 3 quarter turns anticlockwise. Which way does she face?
steps: Anticlockwise from East: North (1), West (2), South (3)

learn.reallife: Drivers follow 'turn right, then left' directions. Pilots and sailors use turns and directions too.

quiz.q: Ravi faces North and makes 2 quarter turns clockwise. Which way does he face?
quiz.explain: Two quarter turns make a half turn, so he faces the opposite way: South.
steps: A half turn makes you face the opposite way.

quiz.q: Meena faces West and makes 1 quarter turn clockwise. Which way does she face?
quiz.explain: Clockwise order: West → North.
steps: Clockwise order: North → East → South → West → North.
From West, one quarter turn clockwise is the next one.

quiz.q: Ali faces South and makes 3 quarter turns clockwise. Which way does he face?
quiz.explain: Clockwise from South: West (1), North (2), East (3).
steps: Clockwise order: North → East → South → West → North.
From South count 3: West (1), North (2), East (3).

quiz.q: Which turn makes you face the same way as 3 quarter turns clockwise?
quiz.explain: 3 quarter turns one way leave just 1 quarter turn to complete the circle, so it equals 1 quarter turn the other way.
steps: A full turn is 4 quarter turns.
3 quarter turns clockwise is 1 quarter turn short of a full turn.
So it ends the same as 1 quarter turn anticlockwise.
quiz.mistake: Thinks only clockwise turns can match

quiz.q: Sara faces East. She turns right, then right again. Which way does she face?
quiz.explain: Each right turn is a quarter clockwise: East → South → West.
steps: A right turn is a quarter turn clockwise.

quiz.q: Raj faces North. After some turns he faces East. Which could NOT be his turn?
quiz.explain: A half turn from North gives South, not East. The others end at East.
steps: 5 quarter clockwise = 1 quarter clockwise → East; 3 quarter anticlockwise → West, South, East.
A half turn gives South, not East. So the half turn could NOT be his turn.
quiz.mistake: Thinks a half turn is a quarter turn

quiz.q: On a map, Asha faces the market, which is to her North. She makes a half turn. What is in front of her now?
quiz.explain: A half turn makes her face the opposite direction, South.
steps: A half turn makes her face the opposite direction.
She faced North, so now she faces South.
In front of her is whatever is to her South.
Answer: Whatever is to her South
quiz.mistake: Thinks a half turn is a quarter turn

quiz.q: Dev faces West. How many quarter turns anticlockwise make him face North?
quiz.explain: Anticlockwise from West: South (1), East (2), North (3).
steps: Anticlockwise order: North → West → South → East → North.

teach.ask: Gappu faces North and turns right two times. Which way am I facing? Help me!
teach.praise: First East, then South. Two right turns make a half turn!
teach.nudge: What is the clockwise order of the directions?

revise.summary: Directions go North → East → South → West clockwise. A right turn is a quarter turn clockwise and a left turn is a quarter turn anticlockwise; different turns can end the same way.
focus: Find the direction after quarter turns
Match turns that end the same way
Use half turns on a map
remember: Clockwise order: North → East → South → West → North
2 quarter turns = half turn (opposite way); 4 = back to start
3 quarter turns clockwise = 1 quarter turn anticlockwise
traps: Don't count in the wrong direction.
A half turn is not a quarter turn: from North it gives South.

learn.hook: Two teams of number cards have different totals. One clever swap can make them equal. Can you find it?
points: First find the sum of each group.
Add both sums and halve the total. That is what each group must have.
Swapping card x from the bigger group with card y from the smaller group moves x − y across.
Choose x − y = half the difference between the two sums.
Try to use the fewest swaps. Often one good swap is enough, but sometimes no single swap works.

example.q: Group A: 9, 4, 7 (sum 20). Group B: 3, 5, 6 (sum 14). Find one swap to make the sums equal.
steps: A must lose 3, so x − y = 3
Swap 9 from A with 6 from B: 9 − 6 = 3

learn.reallife: Picking two kabaddi teams of equal strength is like making sums equal!

games.title: Swap check
items: Groups 8, 2 and 5, 1: swapping 8 and 5 makes the sums equal.
The sums become 7 and 9, not equal.
If the sums are 20 and 14, each group needs 17.
Swapping a 7 and a 5 moves 2 from one sum to the other.
One sum goes down by 2, the other goes up by 2.
Swapping two equal numbers changes the sums.

quiz.q: Group A is 8, 3, 5 and Group B is 2, 6, 4. What should each group's sum be after swapping?
quiz.explain: A = 16 and B = 12. Total 28, so each needs 28 ÷ 2 = 14.

quiz.q: Group A is 8, 3, 5 and Group B is 2, 6, 4. Which one swap makes the sums equal?
quiz.explain: A must lose 2, and 8 − 6 = 2. Now A = 6 + 3 + 5 = 14 and B = 2 + 8 + 4 = 14.
steps: Sums: A = 8 + 3 + 5 = 16, B = 2 + 6 + 4 = 12. Total 28, so each needs 14.
A must lose 2, so swap x from A and y from B with x − y = 2: 8 − 6 = 2.
quiz.mistake: Swaps without checking the new sums

quiz.q: Two groups have sums 23 and 17. A swap moves x − y from the bigger group. What should x − y be?
quiz.explain: The difference is 23 − 17 = 6. Half of 6 is 3. Moving 3 makes both 20.
quiz.mistake: Moves the whole difference instead of half

quiz.q: Group A: 10, 3. Group B: 8, 1. Which swap makes the sums equal?
quiz.explain: A = 13, B = 9, each needs 11, so A must lose 2. 10 − 8 = 2 works. (Swapping 3 and 1 also works, but it is not listed.)
steps: Sums: A = 10 + 3 = 13, B = 8 + 1 = 9. Total 22, so each needs 11.
quiz.mistake: Does not check the new sums

quiz.q: Group A: 7, 6, 5. Group B: 4, 3, 1. What is the fewest number of swaps that makes the sums equal?
quiz.explain: A = 18, B = 8, each needs 13. A must lose 5. Swap 6 with 1: 6 − 1 = 5. One swap is enough.
steps: 18 + 8 = 26, so each needs 26 ÷ 2 = 13. A must lose 5.
quiz.mistake: Thinks a big difference needs many swaps

quiz.q: Group A: 9, 2. Group B: 5, 4. Which single swap makes the sums equal?
quiz.explain: A = 11, B = 9, so A must lose 1. The swaps move 9 − 5 = 4, 9 − 4 = 5, or make A bigger. None moves exactly 1.
steps: Sums: A = 9 + 2 = 11, B = 5 + 4 = 9. Each needs 10, so A must lose 1.
Possible moves: 9 − 5 = 4, 9 − 4 = 5; swapping 2 makes A bigger.
No swap moves exactly 1, so no single swap works.
quiz.mistake: Assumes there is always a swap

quiz.q: After a swap, Group A went from 20 to 17. Group B was 14. What is Group B now?
quiz.explain: Whatever A loses, B gains. A lost 3, so B is 14 + 3 = 17.

quiz.q: Group A: 12, 5, 1 (sum 18). Group B: 7, 4, 3 (sum 14). Which swap makes the sums equal?
quiz.explain: Each group needs 16, so A must lose 2. 5 − 3 = 2. Now A = 12 + 3 + 1 = 16 and B = 7 + 4 + 5 = 16.
steps: Total 18 + 14 = 32, so each group needs 16. A must lose 2.
Need x − y = 2 with x from A, y from B: 5 − 3 = 2.
quiz.mistake: Picks a swap without working out how much must move

teach.ask: Gappu has groups 6, 5, 9 and 4, 3, 7. How do I make the sums equal with one swap?
teach.praise: Each group needs 17. I swap 6 with 3 — A loses 3 and B gains 3. Done!
teach.nudge: What total should each group have?

revise.summary: To make two groups' sums equal, find each sum, add them and halve the total. Swapping x from the bigger group with y from the smaller moves x − y across, so choose x − y = half the difference.
focus: Find the target sum for each group
Find one swap that makes the sums equal
Know when no single swap works
remember: A swap moves x − y from the bigger group to the smaller
Choose x − y = half the difference of the sums
traps: Don't move the whole difference; move half of it.
Don't swap without checking the new sums.
There is not always a single swap that works.

learn.hook: Adding 99 looks hard, but adding 100 is easy. Can you see the trick?
points: To add 99, add 100 and take away 1. To add 999, add 1,000 and take away 1.
To add 98, add 100 and take away 2. To add 198, add 200 and take away 2.
Round one number to the nearest ten, add, then adjust: 47 + 38 = 47 + 40 − 2 = 85.
When fuel is filled into a tank, add the new litres to what was already there.

example.q: A tractor tank had 136 litres of diesel. 99 litres more were filled. How much is in the tank now?

learn.reallife: Petrol pump attendants and shopkeepers add quickly in their heads using these tricks.

quiz.q: What is 456 + 99?
quiz.explain: 456 + 100 = 556, then take away 1: 555.
quiz.mistake: Adds 100 but forgets to take away 1

quiz.q: What is the easy way to work out 2,345 + 999?
quiz.explain: 999 is 1 less than 1,000, so add 1,000 and take away 1.

quiz.q: Using 68 + 30, what is 68 + 29?
A bus tank has 48 litres of diesel. The driver fills 37 litres more. How much is in the tank?
A car used 18 L of petrol on Monday, 26 L on Tuesday and 24 L on Wednesday. How much in all?

quiz.mistake: Adds the 2 instead of taking it away

quiz.q: Which is the same as 345 + 97?
steps: So adding 97 = adding 100, then taking away 3.
quiz.mistake: Adds the 3 instead of taking it away

quiz.q: One fuel tanker carries 2,500 L and another carries 1,999 L. How much do they carry together?

teach.ask: Gappu must add 527 + 99 in his head. What trick can I use?
teach.praise: Add 100 to get 627, then take away 1: 626. So quick!
teach.nudge: Which easy number is 99 close to?

revise.summary: Add numbers near a hundred or a thousand the easy way: to add 99, add 100 and take away 1; to add 98, add 100 and take away 2. Round, add, then adjust.
focus: Add 99, 98, 999 or 198 quickly
Round one number to the nearest ten, add, then adjust
Add fuel or other amounts in real problems
traps: Don't forget to take away the extra 1 after adding 100.
Don't adjust in the wrong direction: 345 + 97 = 345 + 100 − 3, not + 3.

learn.hook: If 25 + 17 = 42, you already know two subtraction facts for free! Can you find them?
points: Addition and subtraction are inverse (opposite) operations. One undoes the other.
To find a missing number, use the opposite operation: ? − 245 = 380 means ? = 380 + 245.

example.q: Find the missing number: ? − 156 = 289

learn.reallife: When a shopkeeper gives change, he often counts up from the price to the money you gave — adding to check a subtraction!

games.title: Partners
items: To find ? in ? − 50 = 20, we add 50 and 20.

quiz.q: From 345 + 128 = 473, which subtraction fact is true?
quiz.explain: Take away one part from the total to get the other part.
steps: In 345 + 128 = 473, the parts are 345 and 128; the total is 473.
Total − one part = the other part.

quiz.q: From 63 − 27 = 36, which addition fact is true?
quiz.explain: Add back what was taken away to get the start number.
steps: Add back what was taken away to get the start.

quiz.q: ? − 245 = 380. What is the missing number?
quiz.explain: Undo the subtraction by adding: 380 + 245 = 625.

quiz.q: 512 − ? = 287. What is the missing number?
steps: Start − ? = what is left, so ? = start − what is left.

quiz.q: ? + 1,450 = 3,000. What is the missing number?
Which operation undoes addition?
quiz.explain: Subtraction takes away what was added, so it undoes addition.
steps: Subtraction takes away what was added.
quiz.mistake: Thinks multiplication is the opposite of addition

quiz.q: Which is NOT in the fact family of 56 + 44 = 100?
quiz.explain: 56 − 44 is 12, not 100. The other three use the same three numbers correctly.
steps: The fact family of 56 + 44 = 100 uses 56, 44, 100 correctly.
56 − 44 = 12, not 100. So 56 − 44 = 100 is NOT in the family.

quiz.q: Ravi had some marbles. He gave away 38 and has 47 left. How many did he have at first?

teach.ask: Gappu knows 48 + 27 = 75. Which subtraction facts can I write from it without working?
teach.praise: 75 − 27 = 48 and 75 − 48 = 27. Addition and subtraction are partners!
teach.nudge: What do I get if I take away one part from 75?

revise.summary: Addition and subtraction are inverse operations: one undoes the other. Use the opposite operation to find a missing number or to make a fact family.
focus: Write related facts from an addition or subtraction
Find a missing number in ? − a = b or a − ? = b
Solve 'how many at first' word problems
traps: Don't subtract when you must add back: ? − 38 = 47 means ? = 85.
Multiplication is not the opposite of addition.

learn.hook: Add 15 + 16 + 17 in two seconds? There is a magic shortcut using the middle number!
points: Consecutive numbers come one after another without skipping: 23, 24, 25.
The sum of 2 consecutive numbers is always odd, because one of them is odd and one is even.
The sum of 3 consecutive numbers can be odd or even. The sum of 4 consecutive numbers is always even.
Sums of 2 consecutive numbers go 3, 5, 7, 9 … (up by 2). Sums of 3 go 6, 9, 12 … (up by 3).
Shortcut: for an odd count of consecutive numbers, sum = middle number × count. 15 + 16 + 17 = 16 × 3 = 48.

example.q: Find 21 + 22 + 23 + 24 + 25 quickly.
steps: There are 5 numbers; the middle one is 23

learn.reallife: House numbers on one side of a lane are often consecutive odd numbers — patterns are everywhere!

quiz.q: Which of these are consecutive numbers?
quiz.explain: 34, 35, 36 follow one after another with nothing skipped.
steps: Consecutive means one after another, nothing skipped.
34, 35, 36 has nothing skipped, so it is consecutive.
quiz.mistake: Thinks even numbers in a row are consecutive

quiz.q: The sum of two consecutive numbers is always…
quiz.explain: One number is odd and the other is even, and odd + even = odd.
steps: Of two consecutive numbers, one is odd and one is even.
So the sum is always odd.

quiz.q: What is 15 + 16 + 17?
quiz.explain: Middle number 16 × 3 numbers = 48.
steps: 3 consecutive numbers; the middle one is 16.

quiz.q: Is the sum of 4 consecutive numbers odd or even?
quiz.explain: 4 consecutive numbers have 2 odd and 2 even numbers. Two odds make an even, so the total is even. Example: 1 + 2 + 3 + 4 = 10.
steps: 4 consecutive numbers have 2 odd and 2 even numbers.
Odd + odd = even, and adding evens keeps it even.
So the sum is always even (e.g. 1 + 2 + 3 + 4 = 10).
quiz.mistake: Tries only one example and guesses

quiz.q: Which is true about the sum of 3 consecutive numbers?
options: It can be odd or even
quiz.explain: 1 + 2 + 3 = 6 is even, but 2 + 3 + 4 = 9 is odd.
steps: So it can be odd or even.
Answer: It can be odd or even

quiz.q: 1 + 2 = 3, 2 + 3 = 5, 3 + 4 = 7, 4 + 5 = 9. By how much does each sum grow?
quiz.explain: 3, 5, 7, 9 go up by 2 each time.
The sums grow by 3 each time: 12 + 3 = 15.
steps: The sums 6, 9, 12 grow by 3 each time.

quiz.q: Find 41 + 42 + 43 + 44 + 45 + 46 + 47 using the middle number.
quiz.explain: 7 numbers, middle is 44. 44 × 7 = 308.

teach.ask: Gappu must add 32 + 33 + 34 + 35 + 36. Is there a quick way?
teach.praise: The middle number 34 times 5 numbers is 170. Magic shortcut!
teach.nudge: Which number is in the middle, and how many numbers are there?

revise.summary: Consecutive numbers come one after another. Two consecutive numbers always add to an odd number, four always add to an even number, and for an odd count, sum = middle number × count.
focus: Spot consecutive numbers
Say if sums of 2, 3 or 4 consecutive numbers are odd or even
Add consecutive numbers using the middle number
remember: Sum of 2 consecutive numbers is always odd
Sum of 3 can be odd or even; sum of 4 is always even
traps: Even numbers in a row (34, 36, 38) are not consecutive.
Don't decide from one example; try a few.

learn.hook: Two trains together travel thousands of kilometres in a month. Can you add like a station master?
points: Write the numbers one below the other: ones under ones, tens under tens, and so on.
Add from the right. If a column makes 10 or more, carry 1 to the next place on the left.
To subtract, start from the right. If the top digit is smaller, borrow 1 from the next place.
Check a subtraction by adding: answer + the number taken away = the starting number.

example.q: A train covered 24,365 km in March and 18,790 km in April. How far did it go in both months?

learn.reallife: Railway staff add up tickets sold, and families add up the cost of a holiday trip.

games.title: True or false?
items: To add big numbers, we line up the ones digits.
Ones go under ones so each place is added to the same place.
When a column adds up to 10 or more, we carry 1 to the next place on the left.

quiz.q: Riya's school collected ₹12,450 on Monday and ₹8,675 on Tuesday for a fair. How much in all?
quiz.explain: 12,450 + 8,675 = 21,125. Remember to carry in the tens, hundreds and thousands.
quiz.mistake: Forgets to carry 1 to the next place

quiz.q: A train has 1,248 passengers. 379 get off at Bhopal. How many are still on the train?
quiz.mistake: Takes the smaller digit from the bigger one in each column instead of borrowing

quiz.q: Kabir's town has 45,320 people. The next town has 38,905. How many more people live in Kabir's town?
quiz.explain: 'How many more' means subtract: 45,320 − 38,905 = 6,415.
quiz.mistake: Adds the numbers instead of subtracting, or slips while borrowing

quiz.q: What is 50,000 − 1?
quiz.explain: One less than 50,000 is 49,999. All the zeros become 9s after borrowing.
quiz.mistake: Changes only one zero, or adds 1 instead of taking away

quiz.q: 26,500 + ? = 40,000. What is the missing number?
quiz.explain: Find the missing part by subtracting: 40,000 − 26,500 = 13,500.
quiz.mistake: Adds 40,000 and 26,500 instead of finding the difference

quiz.q: Meena's family drove 1,285 km to Jaipur, then 642 km to Agra, then 1,073 km back home. How far did they drive in all?
quiz.mistake: Drops a carry when adding three numbers

quiz.q: Arjun had ₹5,000. He spent ₹1,750 on books and ₹865 on shoes. How much money is left?
quiz.mistake: Gives the amount spent (₹2,615) instead of the amount left

quiz.q: Aisha worked out 63,210 − 27,480 = 35,730. What is the best way to check her answer?
options: Add 35,730 + 27,480 and see if you get 63,210
quiz.explain: Adding the answer to the number taken away should give back the starting number. 35,730 + 27,480 = 63,210, so she is right.
steps: Answer + number taken away should give the start: 35,730 + 27,480.
35,730 + 27,480 = 63,210, so add them and see if you get 63,210.
Answer: Add 35,730 + 27,480 and see if you get 63,210
quiz.mistake: Does not know that adding undoes subtracting

quiz.q: Riya had ₹3,500. She spent ₹1,280 on a school bag and then got ₹750 from her nani on Raksha Bandhan. How much does she have now?
quiz.explain: Spending takes money away and receiving adds it: 3,500 − 1,280 = 2,220, then 2,220 + 750 = 2,970.
quiz.mistake: Subtracts the money received instead of adding it

teach.ask: Gappu flaps: 'How do I add two really big numbers without getting muddled?'
teach.praise: Hooray! Line up the places, add from the right and carry when it is 10 or more!
teach.nudge: Where do I write each digit? And what do I do when a column makes 10 or more?

revise.summary: To add or subtract large numbers, line up the places, work from the right, carry when a column makes 10 or more, and borrow when the top digit is smaller.
focus: Add and subtract 5-digit numbers with carrying and borrowing
Solve money and distance word problems
Check a subtraction by adding
remember: Ones under ones, tens under tens
Carry 1 when a column makes 10 or more
Check: answer + number taken away = starting number
traps: Don't take the smaller digit from the bigger one in each column; borrow instead.
Don't forget to add money received in a mixed problem.
Don't give the amount spent when asked for the amount left.

learn.hook: A truck can carry 10,000 kg. It already has 6,450 kg on it. Can it take your 4,000 kg of mangoes?
points: To find two numbers whose sum is closest to a target, try the pairs and see how far each sum is from the target.
Rounding first helps you find good pairs quickly, then check with exact sums.
Space left = capacity − load already carried.
For many loads, add them first or subtract them one by one.
If the new load is more than the space left, it cannot be carried.

example.q: A truck can carry 10,000 kg. It has 6,450 kg. How much more can it carry?

learn.reallife: Lift signs say 'Maximum 680 kg'. Drivers and lift operators always check the load.

games.title: Load check
items: A boat for 1,500 kg can carry 980 kg of people and 365 kg of bags.
A lift for 680 kg can carry 545 kg of people and a 150 kg trolley.
If a truck holds 8,000 kg and has 5,250 kg, it can take 2,750 kg more.

quiz.q: Which two numbers from 2,345; 4,780; 5,620; 3,150 have a sum closest to 8,000?
steps: Add each pair and see how far it is from 8,000.
quiz.mistake: Stops at the first pair that is near

quiz.q: Which two numbers from 6,250; 3,480; 4,100; 5,890 have a sum closest to 10,000?
steps: Add each pair and see how far it is from 10,000.
quiz.mistake: Picks the biggest number first without checking

quiz.q: A truck can carry 10,000 kg. It already has 6,450 kg. How much more can it carry?
A lorry carries 8,500 kg of cement. It drops 2,750 kg at one site and 3,125 kg at another. How much is left?
A boat can carry 1,500 kg. The passengers weigh 980 kg and their bags 365 kg. How much more can it carry?
A lift can carry 680 kg. People inside weigh 545 kg. Can a 150 kg trolley go in too?
options: No, it would be 150 kg too much
No, it would be 15 kg too much
Yes, there is 15 kg to spare
quiz.explain: 545 + 150 = 695, which is 15 kg more than 680.
steps: Answer: No, it would be 15 kg too much
quiz.mistake: Does not compare the total with the limit

quiz.q: Which pair from 2,480; 2,610; 1,995; 3,050 has a sum closest to 5,000?
steps: Add each pair and see how far it is from 5,000.
quiz.mistake: Picks the two numbers closest to 2,500 without checking

quiz.q: A goods wagon can carry 25,000 kg. It has 12,600 kg of rice and 9,850 kg of wheat. How much space is left?
quiz.mistake: Forgets to subtract from the capacity

teach.ask: Gappu's cart can carry 500 kg. It has 320 kg of grain. How much more can I load?
teach.praise: 500 − 320 = 180 kg more. Thanks!
teach.nudge: Which two numbers should I subtract?

revise.summary: To find the pair closest to a target, try pairs and see how far each sum is. Space left = capacity − load already carried; a new load must fit in that space.
focus: Pick two numbers whose sum is closest to a target
Find space left after one or more loads
Decide whether a new load can be carried
remember: Round first to find good pairs, then check exact sums
If the new load is more than the space left, it cannot go
traps: Don't stop at the first pair that looks near; check them all.
Don't forget any part of the load, like the bags.

learn.hook: Do you need the exact answer to know if ₹1,000 is enough for a trip snack? Often a smart guess is enough!
points: Estimating means finding a quick answer that is close to the real one.
To round to the nearest hundred, look at the tens digit. 5 or more: round up. Less than 5: round down.
To round to the nearest thousand, look at the hundreds digit in the same way.
Round the numbers first, then add or subtract. 4,872 + 3,195 is about 5,000 + 3,000 = 8,000.
An estimate helps us check if an exact answer makes sense.

example.q: Estimate 4,872 + 3,195 by rounding each number to the nearest thousand.
steps: 4,872: hundreds digit is 8, round up to 5,000
3,195: hundreds digit is 1, round down to 3,000

learn.reallife: News reports say 'about 2 lakh people came to the mela'. Shoppers round prices to see if they have enough money.

games.title: True or false?
items: 47 rounded to the nearest ten is 50.
The ones digit is 7, which is 5 or more, so we round up.
349 rounded to the nearest hundred is 400.
The tens digit is 4, less than 5, so it rounds down to 300.
650 rounded to the nearest hundred is 700.
The tens digit is 5, so we round up.
An estimate is always exactly the same as the real answer.
An estimate is close, not exact.

quiz.q: Round 3,462 to the nearest hundred.
quiz.explain: The tens digit is 6, which is 5 or more, so round up to 3,500.
steps: Hundreds digit is 4, tens digit is 6
quiz.mistake: Looks at the wrong digit or always rounds down

quiz.q: Round 67,280 to the nearest thousand.
quiz.explain: The hundreds digit is 2, less than 5, so round down to 67,000.
steps: Thousands digit is 7, hundreds digit is 2
quiz.mistake: Rounds up every time, or rounds to the nearest hundred instead

quiz.q: Estimate 498 + 307 by rounding each number to the nearest hundred.
quiz.explain: 498 is about 500 and 307 is about 300. 500 + 300 = 800.
quiz.mistake: Works out the exact answer (805) instead of estimating

quiz.q: A train carried 3,890 people on Monday and 5,120 on Tuesday. Rounding to the nearest thousand, about how many in all?
quiz.mistake: Gives the exact total (9,010) or rounds 3,890 down

quiz.q: Riya has ₹1,000. She wants toys costing ₹212, ₹395 and ₹289. Round each to the nearest hundred. Does she have enough?
Which number rounds to 5,000 when rounded to the nearest thousand?
quiz.explain: 4,725 has hundreds digit 7, so it rounds up to 5,000. 4,450 rounds to 4,000; 5,620 and 5,501 round to 6,000.
steps: Nearest thousand: look at the hundreds digit.
quiz.mistake: Thinks any number that starts with 5 rounds to 5,000

quiz.q: Estimate 612 − 289 by rounding each number to the nearest hundred.
quiz.explain: 612 is about 600 and 289 is about 300. 600 − 300 = 300.
quiz.mistake: Rounds 289 down to 200, or gives the exact answer

quiz.q: A school needs 28 buses with 52 seats each. Round both to the nearest ten to estimate the seats.
quiz.explain: 28 is about 30 and 52 is about 50. 30 × 50 = 1,500.
quiz.mistake: Rounds 28 down to 20, or works out the exact answer (1,456)

quiz.q: Riya's estimate said ₹1,000 is enough for toys of ₹212, ₹395 and ₹289. She now adds exactly. How much money will be left?
quiz.explain: Exact total: 212 + 395 + 289 = 896. ₹1,000 is enough, and 1,000 − 896 = ₹104 is left.
quiz.mistake: Gives the total cost instead of the money left

teach.ask: Gappu asks: 'How do I round 3,462 to the nearest hundred?'
teach.praise: Yay! Look at the tens digit: 6 is 5 or more, so it goes up to 3,500!
teach.nudge: Which digit should I look at? And when do I go up or down?

revise.summary: Estimating gives a quick answer close to the real one. Round each number first, then add or subtract; an estimate helps check whether an exact answer makes sense.
focus: Round to the nearest hundred or thousand
Estimate sums, differences and products by rounding
Use an estimate to decide if money is enough
remember: Nearest hundred: look at the tens digit
Nearest thousand: look at the hundreds digit
5 or more: round up; less than 5: round down
traps: Don't give the exact answer when asked to estimate.
Don't think every number starting with 5 rounds to 5,000: 5,620 → 6,000.

learn.hook: 638 + ? = 1,000. Can you find the missing number in a flash?
points: Numbers that add up to 100, 1,000 or 10,000 are complements: 73 + 27 = 100.
To reach 1,000 from 638: count up to 640 (2), then to 700 (60), then to 1,000 (300). 2 + 60 + 300 = 362.
To subtract 9, subtract 10 and add 1. To subtract 99, subtract 100 and add 1.
To find what to subtract from 457 to leave 99, work out 457 − 99 = 358.

example.q: What is 562 − 99?

learn.reallife: Counting change from ₹1,000 or ₹500 uses complements every day in shops.

quiz.q: What must be added to 638 to make 1,000?
quiz.mistake: Makes a borrowing error across zeros

quiz.q: 4,725 + ? = 10,000. What is the missing number?
quiz.mistake: Takes each digit away from 9 or 10 wrongly

quiz.q: 73 + ? = 100. What is the missing number?
What is 562 − 99?
quiz.mistake: Subtracts 1 instead of adding it back

quiz.q: What is 845 − 9?
What is the easy way to work out 1,234 − 99?
quiz.explain: 99 is 1 less than 100. Taking away 100 takes away 1 too many, so add 1 back.
steps: Taking away 100 takes away 1 too many.

quiz.q: 457 − ? = 99. What number must be taken away?
503 − ? = 9. What is the missing number?

teach.ask: Gappu has to work out 734 − 99 quickly. What should I do?
teach.praise: Take away 100 to get 634, then add 1 back: 635!
teach.nudge: Which round number is 99 close to?

revise.summary: Complements add up to 100, 1,000 or 10,000; count up in jumps to find them. To subtract 9 or 99, subtract 10 or 100 and add 1 back.
focus: Find what to add to reach 100, 1,000 or 10,000
Subtract 9 and 99 quickly
Find a missing number that is taken away
traps: Don't subtract 1 after taking away 100; add it back.
Don't add 99 when finding 457 − ? = 99; work out 457 − 99.

learn.hook: Read 12321 backwards. Same! Numbers like this are called palindromes.
points: A palindrome number reads the same forwards and backwards: 121, 4,554.
Two-digit palindromes are 11, 22, 33 … 99. There are 9 of them.
Three-digit palindromes between 100 and 200 are 101, 111, 121 … 191. There are 10.
Grid puzzle: put 1 to 9 in a 3 × 3 grid so that each row grows left to right and each column grows top to bottom.
In such a grid, 1 must be in the top-left corner and 9 in the bottom-right corner.

example.q: List the palindromes between 300 and 350.

learn.reallife: Some dates are palindromes too, like 12-02-2021 written as 12022021!

games.title: Grid and palindrome facts
items: In the growing grid, 9 can go in the top-left corner.
9 is the biggest, so it must be at the end of its row and column: bottom-right.

quiz.q: Which number is a palindrome?
quiz.explain: 4,554 reads 4-5-5-4 both ways.
steps: A palindrome reads the same forwards and backwards.
Read 4,554 backwards: 4-5-5-4, the same as forwards.
4,545 → 5,454, 5,454 → 4,545 and 4,455 → 5,544: these change, so they are not palindromes.
quiz.mistake: Checks only the first and last digits

quiz.q: How many palindromes are there between 10 and 100?
steps: 2-digit palindromes have both digits the same.

quiz.q: How many palindromes are there between 100 and 200?
steps: The middle digit can be 0 to 9: 101, 111, … 191.

quiz.q: What is the smallest 3-digit palindrome?
quiz.explain: 100 backwards is 001, so it is not a palindrome. 101 is.
steps: 100 backwards is 001, so 100 is not a palindrome.
The next number of the form 1_1 is 101.

quiz.q: What is the next palindrome after 1,221?
quiz.explain: 4-digit palindromes look like abba. After 1,221 comes 1,331.
steps: After 1,221 (a = 1, b = 2) the next has b = 3: 1,331.

quiz.q: In a 3 × 3 grid of 1 to 9 where rows grow left to right and columns grow top to bottom, where must 1 go?
quiz.explain: 1 is the smallest, so nothing can be to its left or above it.
steps: Rows grow left to right and columns grow top to bottom.
1 is the smallest, so nothing can be to its left or above it.
So 1 must go in the top-left corner.

quiz.q: In the same growing grid, where must 9 go?
quiz.explain: 9 is the biggest, so it must be last in its row and its column.
steps: It must be last in its row (right) and last in its column (bottom).
So 9 must go in the bottom-right corner.
quiz.mistake: Thinks 9 can go anywhere at the edge

quiz.q: Which number is NOT a palindrome?
quiz.explain: 1,231 backwards is 1,321, which is different.
steps: 1,231 → 1,321, which is different. So 1,231 is NOT a palindrome.

teach.ask: Gappu found the number 2,442. Is it a palindrome? How do I check?
teach.praise: 2,442 backwards is 2,442. It is a palindrome!
teach.nudge: What happens when I read it from right to left?

revise.summary: A palindrome reads the same forwards and backwards. In a 3 × 3 grid of 1 to 9 where rows and columns grow, 1 is top-left and 9 is bottom-right.
focus: Check whether a number is a palindrome
Count palindromes in a range
Place 1 and 9 in a growing grid
remember: There are 10 palindromes between 100 and 200 (101 to 191)
traps: Don't check only the first and last digits: 1,231 is not a palindrome.
100 is not a palindrome.

learn.hook: 27 children play a game in pairs. Will someone be left without a partner?
points: A number is even if its ones digit is 0, 2, 4, 6 or 8. Otherwise it is odd.
Even numbers can be put into pairs with none left over. Odd numbers always leave one over.
Even + even = even. Odd + odd = even. Odd + even = odd.
Adding 2 does not change odd or even: 7, 9, 11 stay odd; 8, 10, 12 stay even.

example.q: Without adding, is 135 + 247 odd or even?

learn.reallife: Houses on one side of many roads have odd numbers, and on the other side even numbers.

quiz.q: Is 3,457 odd or even?
quiz.explain: The ones digit is 7, which is odd.
steps: Odd or even depends on the ones digit.
quiz.mistake: Looks at the first digit instead of the ones digit

quiz.q: Which number is even?
quiz.explain: 5,678 ends in 8, an even digit.
steps: Only 5,678 ends in 8, so it is even.

quiz.q: 27 children stand in pairs. How many are left without a partner?
quiz.explain: 27 is odd. 13 pairs make 26, and 1 child is left.
quiz.mistake: Thinks every number can be paired

quiz.q: Without adding, is 135 + 247 odd or even?
quiz.explain: Both numbers are odd, and odd + odd = even.
steps: 135 ends in 5: odd. 247 ends in 7: odd.

quiz.q: Without adding, is 246 + 135 odd or even?
quiz.explain: 246 is even and 135 is odd. Even + odd = odd.
steps: 246 ends in 6: even. 135 ends in 5: odd.

quiz.q: Start at 51 and keep adding 2. Which number can you land on?
quiz.explain: 51 is odd, and adding 2 keeps it odd. 75 is the only odd choice.
steps: 51 is odd. Adding 2 does not change odd or even.
So every number you land on is odd.
88, 70, 64 are even. Only 75 is odd, so 75.
quiz.mistake: Thinks adding 2 changes odd to even

quiz.q: Which sum is odd?
quiz.explain: 23 is odd and 40 is even. Odd + even = odd.
steps: 22 + 40: even + even = even. 21 + 43 and 23 + 41: odd + odd = even.
Odd + even = odd, so 23 + 40 is odd.
quiz.mistake: Picks a sum of two odd numbers

quiz.q: Why can 36 laddoos be put into pairs with none left?
quiz.explain: Even numbers split into pairs exactly: 18 pairs.
steps: Even numbers split into pairs with none left over.
36 ends in 6, so it is even.
quiz.mistake: Gives a reason that has nothing to do with odd and even

teach.ask: Gappu wants to know if 999 + 1,001 is odd or even without adding. Can you teach me?
teach.praise: Both are odd, and odd + odd = even. So the sum is even!
teach.nudge: Are 999 and 1,001 odd or even?

revise.summary: A number is even if its ones digit is 0, 2, 4, 6 or 8, otherwise odd. Even + even and odd + odd are even; odd + even is odd.
focus: Tell odd from even by the ones digit
Say if a sum is odd or even without adding
Use pairs to explain odd and even
remember: Even numbers pair up with none left over
Even + even = even; odd + odd = even; odd + even = odd
Adding 2 does not change odd or even
traps: Don't look at the first digit; look at the ones digit.
Odd + odd is not odd.

learn.hook: A light switch is pressed 25 times. Is the light on or off? Odd and even can tell you!
points: To find coin combinations, start with the biggest coins and list the ways step by step.
A switch that starts off: after an odd number of presses it is on; after an even number it is off.
To read a table, find the right row and column. Subtract to find how much higher one value is.

example.q: Everest is 8,849 m and K2 is 8,611 m. How much higher is Everest?

learn.reallife: Mountaineers compare heights of peaks, and electricians know that two presses bring a switch back to where it was.

games.title: Switch and coins
items: A switch that starts off is on after 7 presses.
A switch that starts off is on after 10 presses.
10 is even, so it is off.
₹10 can be made with two ₹5 coins.
The fewest coins (₹1, ₹2, ₹5) to make ₹13 is 3.

quiz.q: In how many ways can you make ₹6 using ₹1, ₹2 and ₹5 coins?
quiz.mistake: Misses the ways that use only ₹1 coins

quiz.q: What is the fewest number of coins (₹1, ₹2, ₹5) to make ₹13?
quiz.explain: 5 + 5 + 2 + 1 = 13 uses 4 coins.
quiz.mistake: Does not use the biggest coins first

quiz.q: A light starts off. Its switch is pressed 15 times. Is it on or off?
quiz.explain: Each press changes it. 15 is odd, so it ends opposite to the start: on.
steps: After an odd number of presses it is opposite to the start.
15 is odd and it started off, so it is on.
quiz.mistake: Thinks many presses always end off

quiz.q: A fan starts off. Its switch is pressed 20 times. Is it on or off?
quiz.explain: 20 is even, so it ends the way it started: off.
steps: After an even number of presses it is back to the start.
20 is even and it started off, so it is off.

quiz.q: Everest is 8,849 m and K2 is 8,611 m. How much higher is Everest?
steps: How much higher = bigger height − smaller height.

quiz.q: Kangchenjunga is 8,586 m and Nanda Devi is 7,816 m. What is the difference?
Heights: Everest 8,849 m, K2 8,611 m, Kangchenjunga 8,586 m. Which two are closest in height?
quiz.explain: 8,611 − 8,586 = 25 m, the smallest difference.

quiz.q: A climber reached a peak in 2018, after her 26th birthday that year. In which year was she born?

teach.ask: Gappu's lamp is off. If I press the switch 9 times, is it on or off? How do I know without pressing?
teach.praise: 9 is odd, so the lamp ends up on. Two presses cancel out!
teach.nudge: Is 9 odd or even, and what does each press do?

revise.summary: List coin combinations starting with the biggest coins. A switch that starts off is on after an odd number of presses and off after an even number. Subtract to compare values in a table.
focus: Count ways to make an amount with coins
Find the fewest coins for an amount
Decide if a switch is on or off
Read a table and find differences
remember: ₹6 can be made in 5 ways with ₹1, ₹2 and ₹5 coins
Starts off: odd presses → on, even presses → off
traps: Don't miss the way that uses only ₹1 coins.
Don't mix up odd and even presses.

learn.hook: The school Maths Mela printed 350 certificates, but 412 children took part. Uh oh! How many more are needed?
points: Surplus means extra. Shortage means not enough. Subtract the smaller number from the bigger one.
Line up places carefully when adding or subtracting big numbers.
For savings, add the money saved each month.
For 'how many more' or 'by how many runs', subtract.

example.q: 350 certificates were printed for 412 children. Is there a surplus or shortage, and of how many?
steps: 412 is more than 350, so there is a shortage

learn.reallife: Event planners always count chairs, plates and prizes to avoid shortages!

quiz.q: 350 certificates were printed but 412 children took part. How many more certificates are needed?
quiz.explain: 412 − 350 = 62 more are needed. This is a shortage.
steps: 412 children need certificates; only 350 were printed.

quiz.q: 600 badges were made for 548 children. How many badges are extra?
quiz.explain: 600 − 548 = 52 extra badges. This is a surplus.
steps: 600 badges for 548 children: more badges than children.

quiz.q: Asha saved ₹1,250 in January, ₹980 in February and ₹1,475 in March. How much did she save?
A factory made 12,450 toys on Monday and 9,875 on Tuesday. How many more on Monday?
Team A scored 287 runs and Team B scored 249. By how many runs did Team A win?
steps: Winning margin = winner's runs − loser's runs.

quiz.q: A factory must make 50,000 shirts. It has made 36,780. How many are still to be made?

quiz.explain: Add place by place, carrying: 74,120.
steps: Line up places and add from the right.
Tens: 7 + 5 = 12, write 2 carry 1. Hundreds: 6 + 4 + 1 = 11, write 1 carry 1. Thousands: 5 + 8 + 1 = 14, write 4 carry 1. Ten thousands: 4 + 2 + 1 = 7.

teach.ask: Gappu ordered 120 laddoos for 135 guests. Is that a surplus or a shortage? By how many?
teach.praise: 135 − 120 = 15, so I am short by 15 laddoos. I will order more!
teach.nudge: Are there more guests or more laddoos?

revise.summary: In mixed problems, decide whether to add or subtract. Shortage or surplus, 'how many more' and 'by how many runs' need subtraction; total savings need addition.
focus: Find shortage or surplus
Add savings over months
Subtract big numbers, borrowing across zeros
remember: Surplus means extra; shortage means not enough
For 'how many more', subtract the smaller from the bigger
traps: Don't add when the question asks how many more.
Take care when borrowing across zeros: 80,000 − 46,385 = 33,615.

learn.hook: A bus does 24 trips a day. Each trip is 135 km. Can you find the distance in a day without a calculator?
points: To multiply by 10, 100 or 1,000, write 1, 2 or 3 zeros at the end: 45 × 100 = 4,500.
To multiply by a 2-digit number, split it: 135 × 24 = 135 × 20 + 135 × 4.
Division shares a number into equal parts or makes equal groups.
Check a division by multiplying: 2,400 ÷ 8 = 300 because 300 × 8 = 2,400.
A remainder is what is left over. It is always smaller than the number you divide by.

example.q: A bus makes 24 trips a day. Each trip is 135 km. How far does it go in a day?

learn.reallife: Travel agents multiply ticket prices by the number of people, and teachers divide children into buses for a trip.

quiz.q: A train ticket costs ₹1,245. What is the cost of 6 tickets?
quiz.explain: 1,245 × 6 = 7,470. Multiply each place by 6 and carry.
quiz.mistake: Forgets to add the carried digits

quiz.q: What is 48 × 100?
quiz.explain: Multiplying by 100 puts two zeros at the end: 4,800.
steps: Multiplying by 100 puts two zeros at the end.
quiz.mistake: Writes one or three zeros instead of two

quiz.q: 1,350 students go on a trip in buses. Each bus takes 45 students. How many buses are needed?
A plane flies 850 km every hour. How far does it fly in 12 hours?
quiz.mistake: Multiplies only by the 2 in 12 and forgets the 10

quiz.q: Harpreet shares 2,400 packets of rangoli colours equally among 8 shops. How many packets does each shop get?
What is 236 × 25?
quiz.mistake: Multiplies by only the 20 or only the 5 and forgets to add both parts

quiz.q: Joseph packs 97 laddoos in boxes of 8. How many full boxes does he get, and how many laddoos are left?
quiz.explain: 8 × 12 = 96, so 12 full boxes. 97 − 96 = 1 laddoo is left.
quiz.mistake: Leaves a remainder that is bigger than 8, or ignores the remainder

quiz.q: A cricket stadium sold 3,250 tickets each day for 4 days. How many tickets were sold in all?
quiz.mistake: Adds 4 instead of multiplying, or forgets a carry

teach.ask: Gappu scratches his head: 'How can I multiply 135 by 24? It is too big!'
teach.praise: Super! Split 24 into 20 and 4, multiply each, then add. 3,240!
teach.nudge: How can I make 24 easier to work with? And what do I do with the two answers?

revise.summary: To multiply by 10, 100 or 1,000, add 1, 2 or 3 zeros. Split a 2-digit multiplier into tens and ones. Division makes equal groups; check it by multiplying, and the remainder is always smaller than the divisor.
focus: Multiply by 10, 100 and 1,000
Multiply by a 2-digit number by splitting
Divide and give the remainder
Check division by multiplying
remember: Remainder < the number you divide by
traps: Don't forget the tens part: 850 × 12 = 850 × 10 + 850 × 2.
Don't leave a remainder bigger than the divisor.
Don't drop or add a zero when dividing.

learn.hook: How far is your school? A few steps, a few hundred metres or a few kilometres? Let's become distance detectives!
points: We measure short lengths in millimetres (mm) and centimetres (cm), like a pencil or an eraser.
We measure longer lengths in metres (m), like a room, a saree or a cricket pitch.
We measure long distances in kilometres (km), like the road from one town to another.
When you use a ruler, start from the 0 mark. If you start at another mark, subtract.
To find the length of a route, add the lengths of its parts.

example.q: Harpreet walks 350 m from home to the shop and then 450 m from the shop to the park. How far does she walk?

learn.reallife: Road signs show kilometres to the next town. Tailors measure cloth in metres and centimetres.

games.title: Shortest to longest
games.prompt: Put these from shortest to longest

quiz.q: Which unit is best for measuring the length of a pencil?
quiz.explain: A pencil is short, so centimetres fit best.
steps: A pencil is a short length.
Short lengths are measured in cm or mm; km and m are for long ones, litres is not length.
quiz.mistake: Picks a unit for long distances, or a unit that is not for length

quiz.q: Which unit is best for the distance from Delhi to Agra?
quiz.explain: Towns are far apart, so we use kilometres.
steps: Delhi and Agra are towns far apart.
Long distances between towns are measured in kilometres.
quiz.mistake: Thinks metres are enough for long distances between towns

quiz.q: An eraser lies on a ruler. It starts at the 2 cm mark and ends at the 7 cm mark. How long is it?
quiz.explain: Length = end − start = 7 − 2 = 5 cm.
steps: End mark 7 cm, start mark 2 cm
quiz.mistake: Reads only the end mark and forgets the eraser did not start at 0

quiz.q: Which unit should Meena use to measure the length of her classroom?
quiz.explain: A classroom is a few metres long, so metres fit best.
steps: A classroom is a few metres long.
mm is too small, km is too big, grams is not a length.
quiz.mistake: Chooses a unit that is far too small or far too big

quiz.q: Kabir takes 10 steps. Each step is about 50 cm. About how far does he walk?
quiz.mistake: Forgets to change centimetres into metres

quiz.q: Meena's school is 2 km from home. She walks there and back every day. How far does she walk each day?
quiz.explain: There and back is the distance two times: 2 km + 2 km = 4 km.

quiz.q: How many millimetres make 1 centimetre?
quiz.explain: Look at a ruler: each centimetre has 10 small marks. 1 cm = 10 mm.
steps: On a ruler, each centimetre has 10 small marks.

quiz.q: Which road is the longest?
quiz.explain: 1 km = 1,000 m, which is more than 900 m. 1,500 cm is only 15 m.
steps: Write all lengths in metres: 1 km = 1,000 m; 1,500 cm = 15 m.
1,000 m is the biggest, so the road of 1 km is the longest.
quiz.mistake: Looks at the biggest number and ignores the unit

teach.ask: Gappu wants to fly to Grandma's village. He asks: 'How do people measure how far things are?'
teach.praise: Wow! Small things in cm, rooms in metres and far places in km. I'll fly 3 km!
teach.nudge: Which unit would you use for a short thing, and which for a far-away town?

revise.summary: Short lengths are measured in mm and cm, longer lengths in metres and long distances between places in kilometres. Measure from the 0 mark and add the parts of a route.
focus: Choose the best unit for a length
Read a ruler when the object does not start at 0
Find the length of a route by adding its parts
remember: If you start at another mark, subtract: 7 cm − 2 cm = 5 cm
traps: Don't look only at the biggest number; check the unit: 1 km is more than 900 m.
Don't count only one way for 'there and back'.

learn.hook: A saree is 550 cm long. Is that more or less than 6 metres? Converting units will tell you!
points: 1 m = 100 cm and 1 cm = 10 mm.
1 km = 1,000 m, so half a kilometre is 500 m.
Big unit to small unit: multiply. 3 m = 3 × 100 = 300 cm.
Small unit to big unit: divide. 4,000 m = 4,000 ÷ 1,000 = 4 km.
Mixed units: 2 m 35 cm = 200 cm + 35 cm = 235 cm.

example.q: Write 4 km 75 m in metres.

learn.reallife: Marathon runners talk about 42 km. Tailors change metres into centimetres to cut cloth.

quiz.q: How many centimetres are there in 3 m?
steps: 1 m = 100 cm. Big unit to small unit: multiply.

quiz.q: 6 km = ? m
steps: 1 km = 1,000 m. Big unit to small unit: multiply.

quiz.q: Write 4 m 8 cm in centimetres.
quiz.mistake: Writes 4 and 8 side by side and forgets that 4 m is 400 cm

quiz.q: Write 2,750 m in km and m.
quiz.mistake: Splits the digits in the wrong place

quiz.q: Riya's saree is 550 cm long. How long is it in metres and centimetres?
Aisha ran 1 km 200 m. Joseph ran 1,020 m. Who ran farther?
quiz.explain: 1 km 200 m = 1,200 m. 1,200 m is more than 1,020 m.

quiz.q: Half a kilometre is how many metres?
Kabir cuts a 3 m ribbon into pieces of 25 cm for rakhis. How many pieces does he get?
quiz.mistake: Multiplies 3 × 25 without changing metres into centimetres

teach.ask: Gappu asks: 'How do I change kilometres into metres?'
teach.praise: Easy peasy! 1 km is 1,000 m, so I multiply by 1,000!
teach.nudge: How many metres are in 1 km? What do I do with that number?

revise.summary: 1 m = 100 cm, 1 cm = 10 mm and 1 km = 1,000 m. Multiply to change a big unit to a small one and divide to change a small unit to a big one.
focus: Change km to m and m to cm
Write mixed units in one unit
Split a length into km and m or m and cm
remember: Big to small: multiply. Small to big: divide.
traps: Don't write 4 m 8 cm as 48 cm; it is 408 cm.
Don't use 100 for km to m; use 1,000.
Change metres to cm before dividing into cm pieces.

topics.title: Double number lines and comparing heights

learn.hook: The Statue of Unity in Gujarat is about 182 m tall. How many of you, standing on each other's heads, would that be?
points: A double number line has metres on top and centimetres below, lined up: 1 m sits above 100 cm, 2 m above 200 cm.
Halfway between 0 m and 1 m is 50 cm. Halfway between 1 m and 2 m is 1 m 50 cm = 150 cm.
To find the difference between two heights, write them in the same unit and subtract.
To put heights in order, compare them in the same unit.
To find which length doubled gives another, halve it: half of 3 m is 1 m 50 cm.

example.q: Which length, doubled, gives 5 m?

learn.reallife: Tailors and carpenters use measuring tapes marked in both m and cm — a double number line!

quiz.q: On a double number line, which centimetre mark sits below 4 m?
quiz.explain: Each metre is 100 cm, so 4 m lines up with 4 × 100 = 400 cm.
steps: On a double number line, each metre lines up with 100 cm.

quiz.q: On a double number line, a mark is halfway between 2 m and 3 m. What is it in cm?
quiz.explain: Halfway between 200 cm and 300 cm is 250 cm.
steps: Halfway between them is 50 cm more than 200 cm.

quiz.q: The Statue of Unity is about 182 m tall. A temple tower is 66 m tall. How much taller is the statue?
steps: How much taller = bigger height − smaller height.

quiz.q: Statue P is 45 m tall, statue Q is 4,050 cm and statue R is 42 m 60 cm. Which is the tallest?
quiz.explain: In cm: P = 4,500 cm, Q = 4,050 cm, R = 4,260 cm. P is the tallest.
steps: 4,500 is the biggest, so P is the tallest.

quiz.q: A palm tree is 9 m 40 cm tall and a neem tree is 7 m 85 cm. What is the difference?
quiz.mistake: Subtracts metres and centimetres separately without borrowing

quiz.q: Which length, doubled, gives 3 m?
quiz.explain: 3 m = 300 cm. Half of 300 cm is 150 cm = 1 m 50 cm.
steps: To find what doubled gives 3 m, halve 3 m.

quiz.q: Rani's height is 1 m 20 cm. Her father is double her height. How tall is he?
Which length doubled gives 1 m 70 cm?
steps: To find what doubled gives 1 m 70 cm, halve it.

teach.ask: Gappu wants to know which is taller: a pole of 3 m 5 cm or one of 350 cm. How do I compare?
teach.praise: 3 m 5 cm is 305 cm, so the 350 cm pole is taller!
teach.nudge: What should I change both lengths into first?

revise.summary: A double number line lines up metres with centimetres. To compare or subtract heights, write them in the same unit; to find what doubles to a length, halve it.
focus: Read cm marks on a double number line
Find differences between heights
Order heights in mixed units
Halve or double lengths in m and cm
remember: 1 m sits above 100 cm, 2 m above 200 cm
Halfway between 2 m and 3 m is 250 cm
Half of 3 m is 1 m 50 cm
traps: Don't compare 45 m with 4,050 cm without changing units.
Don't halve or double only the metres.

topics.title: Steps, metres and distances from school

learn.hook: How many steps do you take to walk 100 m? Count them and you will have your own 'step ruler'!
points: Measure 100 m on the ground with a tape, then walk it and count your steps.
If you take 200 steps in 100 m, each step is about 50 cm, and 2 steps make about 1 m.
Use your steps to estimate other distances: 600 steps is about 300 m.
To order places by distance from school, write all distances in the same unit first.

example.q: Neel takes 160 steps for 100 m. The park is 480 steps away. About how far is it?
steps: So it is about 3 × 100 m = 300 m

learn.reallife: People used footsteps to measure land long ago. Even today, we say a shop is 'just 5 minutes' walk' away.

quiz.q: Mira takes 200 steps to walk 100 m. How many steps does she take for 300 m?
quiz.explain: 100 m takes 200 steps, so 300 m takes 3 × 200 = 600 steps.
quiz.mistake: Uses the same number of steps as metres

quiz.q: Arjun takes 200 steps in 100 m. About how long is one step?
With 2 steps for every metre, about how far is a shop that is 900 steps away?
quiz.explain: 2 steps = 1 m, so 900 steps = 900 ÷ 2 = 450 m.

quiz.q: Which place is nearest to school: library 750 m, bank 1 km 5 m, clinic 1,050 m?
quiz.explain: In metres: 750, 1,005 and 1,050. 750 is the smallest.
steps: Library 750 m, bank 1 km 5 m = 1,005 m, clinic 1,050 m.
750 m is the smallest, so the library is nearest.
quiz.mistake: Compares without changing to one unit

quiz.q: Which place is farthest: playground 1 km 200 m, lake 1,020 m, fort 1 km 80 m?
quiz.explain: In metres: 1,200, 1,020 and 1,080. The playground is farthest.
steps: Playground 1 km 200 m = 1,200 m, lake 1,020 m, fort 1 km 80 m = 1,080 m.
1,200 m is the biggest, so the playground is farthest.

quiz.q: Tina measures 200 m with a tape. Why does she count her steps over it?
options: To know about how many steps she takes for a known distance
To find the time of day
quiz.explain: Knowing steps for a known distance lets her estimate other distances.
steps: 200 m is a known distance measured with a tape.
Counting steps over it tells her how many steps make that distance.
So she knows about how many steps she takes for a known distance, to estimate others.
Answer: To know about how many steps she takes for a known distance
quiz.mistake: Does not see why a known length helps

quiz.q: Raj takes 140 steps for 100 m. His uncle takes 120 steps for 100 m. Who has the longer step?
quiz.explain: Fewer steps for the same distance means each step is longer.
steps: Fewer steps for the same distance means each step is longer: Uncle.
quiz.mistake: Thinks more steps means longer steps

quiz.q: Put in order from nearest: A 2 km, B 1,800 m, C 2 km 50 m. Which is in the middle?
quiz.explain: 1,800 m < 2,000 m < 2,050 m. A (2 km) is in the middle.
steps: Write all in metres: A = 2,000 m, B = 1,800 m, C = 2,050 m.
Order from nearest: 1,800 < 2,000 < 2,050 → B, A, C.

teach.ask: Gappu wants to know how far his nest is without a tape. How can my steps help?
teach.praise: First I count steps for 100 m, then use them to estimate any distance. Smart!
teach.nudge: How can I find out how long my step is?

revise.summary: Walk a measured 100 m and count your steps to know your step length. Then use steps to estimate other distances, and use one unit to order places by distance.
focus: Find step length from steps in a known distance
Estimate distances from steps
Order places by distance in mixed units
remember: 200 steps in 100 m means each step is about 50 cm
2 steps for every metre: metres = steps ÷ 2
Write all distances in the same unit before ordering
traps: More steps for the same distance means shorter steps, not longer.
Don't read 1 km 80 m as 1,800 m; it is 1,080 m.

learn.hook: Which is longer: 3 km 40 m or 3,400 m? They look alike, but they are not!
points: Before adding, subtracting or comparing, write both distances in the same unit.
1 km 50 m = 1,050 m, not 1,500 m. The 50 sits in the tens and ones places.
Add or subtract the numbers just like ordinary numbers.
Change the answer back to km and m if that is easier to read.

example.q: Harpreet walks 650 m to the bus stop and then rides 3 km 400 m by bus. How far does she travel?

learn.reallife: Train timetables list the distance between stations. Cyclists add up the kilometres of each ride.

games.title: Shortest to longest
games.prompt: Put these distances from shortest to longest

games.title: True or false?
items: 1 km 5 m is the same as 1,005 m.
3 m = 300 cm, and 250 cm is less than 300 cm.
To add 2 km and 300 m, first write them in the same unit.
2 km = 2,000 m, so the total is 2,300 m.

quiz.q: A train goes from Rampur to Sitapur (64 km) and then from Sitapur to Gopalpur (96 km). How far is Rampur to Gopalpur on this route?
quiz.explain: Add the two parts: 64 + 96 = 160 km.
steps: The route goes Rampur → Sitapur → Gopalpur, so add the parts.
quiz.mistake: Forgets to carry when adding, or subtracts

quiz.q: Meena walked 1 km 250 m in the morning and 850 m in the evening. How many metres did she walk in all?
Arjun's school is 2 km from home. He has cycled 1 km 350 m. How much farther must he go?
quiz.mistake: Makes a borrowing slip when subtracting from 2,000

quiz.q: Which is shorter: 3 km 40 m or 3,400 m?
quiz.explain: 3 km 40 m = 3,040 m, and 3,040 m is less than 3,400 m.

quiz.q: One lap of a running track is 400 m. How many laps make 2 km?
quiz.mistake: Divides 2 by 400 without changing km to m

quiz.q: Kabir's home is 750 m from the cycle shop. He goes to the shop and back home two times in a day. How far does he travel?
