Profit = selling price − cost price. If oil costs ₹180 to make and sells for ₹250, profit is ₹70 a litre.

example.q: A mill sold coir for ₹2,400 at ₹40 a kg. How many kg did it sell?

learn.reallife: Farmers in Kerala and Tamil Nadu sell coconuts, oil and coir ropes — every sale needs these sums.

games.title: Steps to find the earnings
items: Divide to find the litres of oil
Multiply litres by the price per litre
Subtract the cost to find the profit

quiz.q: 8 coconuts give 1 litre of oil. How many litres do 320 coconuts give?
quiz.explain: 320 ÷ 8 = 40 litres.

quiz.q: The mill sells 40 litres at ₹250 a litre. How much does it earn?
Coir sells at ₹30 a kg. The mill earned ₹1,800 from coir. How many kg were sold?
steps: Quantity sold = earnings ÷ price per kg.

quiz.q: Making 1 litre of oil costs ₹180. It sells for ₹250. What is the profit on 1 litre?
Using that profit of ₹70 a litre, what is the profit on 25 litres?
steps: Profit on 25 litres = 25 × profit on 1 litre.

quiz.q: A farmer sells 600 coconuts at ₹15 each. He spent ₹4,500 growing them. What is his profit?
quiz.mistake: Gives the earnings, not the profit

quiz.q: Oil is sold in 500 ml bottles at ₹130 each. The mill earns ₹3,900. How many bottles were sold?
steps: Bottles sold = earnings ÷ price of one bottle.

quiz.q: Which tells us whether a business made a profit?
options: Cost price is more than selling price
The number of coconuts is large
Selling price is more than cost price
quiz.explain: Profit happens when we sell for more than it cost.
steps: This is more than 0 only if selling price is more.
So selling price is more than cost price.
Answer: Selling price is more than cost price
quiz.mistake: Mixes up cost price and selling price

teach.ask: Gappu sells nest-coir at ₹20 a kg and earned ₹500. How many kg did I sell?
teach.nudge: Which operation finds the quantity from earnings and price?

revise.summary: Solve business problems one step at a time. Earnings = quantity × price, quantity = earnings ÷ price, and profit = selling price − cost price.
focus: Find litres or kg from a rule
Find earnings and quantity sold
Find profit for one and many units
traps: Don't give earnings when the question asks for profit.
Don't add cost price and selling price to find profit.

learn.hook: A farm has 4,536 coconuts to pack into 6 trucks equally. How many in each truck?
points: 4- and 5-digit numbers are divided the same way: one place at a time from the left.
If the first digit is smaller than the divisor, regroup: in 4,536 ÷ 6, 4 thousands = 40 hundreds, so take 45 hundreds.
45 hundreds ÷ 6 = 7 hundreds r 3 hundreds; 33 tens ÷ 6 = 5 tens r 3 tens; 36 ÷ 6 = 6. Answer 756.
For 2-digit divisors, use multiples: 12,480 ÷ 24 → 24 × 500 = 12,000, 480 ÷ 24 = 20, so 520.
Clue puzzles: list numbers that fit the first clue, then cross out using the others.
learn.reallife: Warehouses divide thousands of items into equal truckloads.

games.title: Regrouping
items: 2 thousands is less than 5, so regroup to 28 hundreds.
4 is less than 6, so the quotient has 3 digits: 756.

quiz.q: What is 4,536 ÷ 6?
In 2,835 ÷ 5, why do we start with 28 hundreds?
options: Because we always start with hundreds
Because 2 thousands is less than 5, so we regroup them as 20 hundreds
quiz.explain: 2 thousands cannot be shared among 5, so we change them to 20 hundreds and add the 8 hundreds.
steps: So change them to 20 hundreds and add the 8 hundreds: 28 hundreds.
We start with 28 hundreds because 2 thousands is less than 5.
Answer: Because 2 thousands is less than 5, so we regroup them as 20 hundreds
quiz.mistake: Starts with a digit smaller than the divisor

quiz.q: What is 2,835 ÷ 5?
What is 3,612 ÷ 3?
quiz.mistake: Skips the 0 in the tens place

quiz.q: A farm packs 9,750 coconuts into bags of 25. How many bags?
I am a 3-digit number less than 200. I can be divided exactly by 5 and by 9. My digits add to 9. I am even. Who am I?
quiz.explain: Divisible by 5 and 9 means a multiple of 45: 135, 180 (3-digit, under 200). Both have digit sum 9. Even: 180.
steps: Divisible by 5 and 9 means a multiple of 45: 135, 180 are 3-digit and under 200.

quiz.q: A 3-digit number is 4 × 125 and ends in 0. What is it?

teach.ask: Gappu must divide 2,412 seeds into 4 equal piles. What do I do first?
teach.praise: 2 thousands is less than 4, so I use 24 hundreds. The answer is 603!
teach.nudge: Can I share 2 thousands among 4 piles?

revise.summary: Large numbers are divided one place at a time from the left. If the first digit is smaller than the divisor, regroup it into the next place.
focus: Divide 4- and 5-digit numbers
Explain regrouping when the first digit is small
Use multiples for 2-digit divisors
Solve clue puzzles with division
traps: Don't skip a 0 in the quotient: 3,612 ÷ 3 = 1,204, not 124.
Don't drop a zero in big divisions.

topics.title: Using division: shows, shares and patterns

learn.hook: A hall seats 250 people. 1,800 people want to watch a puppet show. How many shows are needed?
points: Number of shows = audience ÷ seats per show. If there is a remainder, one more show is needed.
If shows happen 3 a day, days needed = shows ÷ 3 (round up if there are shows left over).
To find each person's share per day: total ÷ people, then ÷ days.
Patterns: when the dividend and divisor are both multiplied by the same number, the quotient stays the same: 12 ÷ 3 = 120 ÷ 30 = 4.

example.q: 1,800 people, 250 seats per show. How many shows?

learn.reallife: Cinemas, buses and trains plan the number of shows or trips with division.

items.q: ₹840 shared by 4 for 7 days: per day?
120 laddoos, 5 kids, 3 days: per kid per day?

quiz.q: A hall seats 250. 1,800 people want to see a show. How many shows are needed?
quiz.explain: 1,800 ÷ 250 = 7 r 50. The 50 people need one more show: 8 shows.

quiz.q: The puppet group can do 3 shows a day. How many days for 8 shows?
quiz.explain: 8 ÷ 3 = 2 r 2. Two shows are left for a third day.

quiz.q: ₹840 is shared equally among 4 children to spend over 7 days. How much can each child spend a day?
quiz.explain: Each child gets ₹840 ÷ 4 = ₹210. Per day: ₹210 ÷ 7 = ₹30.

quiz.q: 120 bananas are shared by 5 monkeys over 3 days, equally. How many does each monkey eat a day?
quiz.explain: Each monkey gets 120 ÷ 5 = 24. Per day 24 ÷ 3 = 8.
Both numbers are 10 times bigger, so the quotient stays 4.
steps: Multiplying both by the same number keeps the quotient.

quiz.q: Which division has the same answer as 56 ÷ 7?
quiz.explain: Multiplying both numbers by 10 keeps the quotient: 8.

quiz.q: 36 ÷ 4 = 9 and 36 ÷ 2 = 18. What happens to the quotient when the divisor is halved?
quiz.explain: Smaller groups mean more groups: 9 → 18.
quiz.mistake: Thinks a smaller divisor gives a smaller answer

quiz.q: A bus seats 45. How many trips to carry 200 pilgrims?
quiz.explain: 200 ÷ 45 = 4 r 20. The last 20 need one more trip: 5.

teach.ask: Gappu's hall seats 40 birds. 130 birds want to watch. How many shows do I need?
teach.praise: 130 ÷ 40 = 3 remainder 10, and those 10 need a show too, so 4 shows!
teach.nudge: What do I do with the birds left over?

revise.summary: Number of shows = audience ÷ seats; if there is a remainder, one more show is needed. Multiplying dividend and divisor by the same number keeps the quotient the same.
focus: Round up for shows, trips and days
Divide twice for shares per person per day
Use division patterns
remember: Halving the divisor doubles the quotient
traps: Don't ignore the remainder when everyone must be served.
Don't multiply only one number and expect the same quotient.

topics.title: Missing facts, making the most and sales records

learn.hook: 'Raju bought some pens for ₹60. How much did one pen cost?' Can you solve it? Something is missing!
points: Some word problems cannot be solved because information is missing. Spot what you need.
To find the most items you can make from limited stock, divide each stock by what one item needs, then take the smallest answer.
Example: a sandwich needs 2 slices of bread and 1 slice of cheese. With 20 bread and 8 cheese, bread allows 10 and cheese allows 8, so only 8 sandwiches.
A sales record table: amount = quantity × rate. Add the amounts for the total.

example.q: Brinjal: 4 kg at ₹30/kg, Tomato: 5 kg at ₹24/kg. Find the total sales.

learn.reallife: Vegetable vendors write daily sales records, and cooks check if they have enough of every ingredient.

games.title: Can it be solved?
items: Some pens cost ₹60. Cost of 1 pen?
A bus seats 40. How many buses for 200 people?
A bus carries children. How many buses?
12 eggs in a tray. Eggs in 5 trays?
Eggs are packed in trays. Eggs in 5 trays?

quiz.q: 'Raju bought some pens for ₹60. How much did one pen cost?' What is missing?
quiz.explain: To find the cost of one pen we must know how many pens he bought.
steps: Cost of one pen = total cost ÷ number of pens.
We know ₹60 but not how many pens.
So the number of pens is missing.
quiz.mistake: Thinks every problem can be solved

quiz.q: 'A tank fills buckets. How many buckets can it fill?' Which fact is needed?
options: How much the tank and one bucket hold
quiz.explain: We need the tank's capacity and a bucket's capacity to divide.
steps: Buckets = tank's capacity ÷ one bucket's capacity.
So we need how much the tank and one bucket hold.
Answer: How much the tank and one bucket hold
quiz.mistake: Picks a fact that does not help

quiz.q: A sandwich needs 2 slices of bread and 1 cheese slice. You have 20 bread slices and 8 cheese slices. How many sandwiches can you make?
quiz.explain: Bread allows 20 ÷ 2 = 10, cheese allows 8. The smaller is 8.

quiz.q: A garland needs 12 marigolds and 4 roses. There are 120 marigolds and 32 roses. How many garlands?
quiz.explain: Marigolds allow 120 ÷ 12 = 10, roses allow 32 ÷ 4 = 8. Only 8 garlands.

quiz.q: A kite needs 3 sticks and 1 sheet of paper. There are 25 sticks and 10 sheets. How many kites?
quiz.explain: Sticks allow 25 ÷ 3 = 8 r 1, sheets allow 10. Only 8 kites.
quiz.mistake: Forgets that the sticks run out first

quiz.q: A vegetable seller sold 4 kg of brinjal at ₹30 a kg. What amount goes in the sales record?
quiz.explain: Amount = quantity × rate = 4 × ₹30 = ₹120.

quiz.q: Sales: brinjal ₹120, tomato 5 kg at ₹24/kg, beans 3 kg at ₹45/kg. What is the total?
The record shows ₹180 for onions at ₹36 a kg. How many kg were sold?
quiz.explain: Quantity = amount ÷ rate = 180 ÷ 36 = 5 kg.

teach.ask: Gappu read: 'Some birds share 60 worms equally. How many does each get?' Can I solve it?
teach.praise: I cannot solve it yet — I need to know how many birds there are!
teach.nudge: What fact do I need before I can divide?

revise.summary: Some problems cannot be solved because information is missing. To find the most items from limited stock, divide each stock by what one item needs and take the smallest answer.
focus: Spot missing information
Find the most items that can be made
Fill and read a sales record
traps: Don't use only one ingredient; the one that runs out first decides.
Don't take the larger answer; take the smallest.

topics.title: True or false? Testing number statements

learn.hook: 'Doubling a number always makes it even.' Is that always true, sometimes true or never true? Be a maths judge!
points: A number statement can be true (12 ÷ 4 = 3) or false (12 ÷ 4 = 4).
We can complete a statement to make it true: 7 × ☐ = 56 is true when ☐ = 8.
To test a general claim, try many examples. One counterexample (an example that fails) shows the claim is not always true.
'Always true': odd + odd is even. 'Sometimes true': half of an even number is even (true for 8, false for 6). 'Never true': odd × odd is even.

example.q: Is 'half of an even number is even' always, sometimes or never true?
steps: One example works and one fails

learn.reallife: Scientists and judges test claims with evidence — maths does the same with examples!

games.title: Always, sometimes or never?
items: Doubling a number gives an even number
Half of an even number is even
A number ending in 0 is odd

quiz.q: Which division or multiplication fact is true?
Which number makes '7 × ☐ = 56' true?
Which number makes '☐ ÷ 6 = 12' true?
Is 'the sum of two odd numbers is even' always, sometimes or never true?
quiz.explain: The two left-over ones of the odd numbers pair up, so the sum is always even: 3 + 5 = 8, 7 + 9 = 16.
steps: Each odd number has one left over; the two left-overs pair up.

quiz.q: Is 'half of an even number is even' always, sometimes or never true?
quiz.explain: Half of 8 is 4 (even) but half of 10 is 5 (odd).
steps: One works and one fails, so it is sometimes true.

quiz.q: Is 'the product of two odd numbers is even' always, sometimes or never true?
quiz.explain: Odd × odd is always odd: 3 × 5 = 15, 7 × 9 = 63.
steps: So 'odd × odd is even' is never true.
quiz.mistake: Confuses the rule for adding with the rule for multiplying

quiz.q: Which is a counterexample to 'all multiples of 3 are odd'?
quiz.explain: 6 is a multiple of 3 but it is even, so the claim is false.
steps: A counterexample is a multiple of 3 that is NOT odd.
15, 21 and 9 are odd, so they agree with the claim.
6 = 3 × 2 is even, so 6 is the counterexample.
quiz.mistake: Picks an example that agrees with the claim

quiz.q: Riya claims 'doubling any number gives an even number'. Which is true?
options: Always true, because double means 2 groups, which pair up
quiz.explain: Any number × 2 can be split into pairs, so it is always even.
steps: Double a number = 2 equal groups of it.
2 groups can always be paired up, one from each group.
So it is always true (double 3 = 6, double 7 = 14).
Answer: Always true, because double means 2 groups, which pair up
quiz.mistake: Thinks odd numbers stay odd when doubled

teach.ask: Gappu says 'every number ending in 5 is odd'. Is that always, sometimes or never true? How can I check?
teach.praise: 15, 25, 135 — they all end in 5 and are odd. Always true!
teach.nudge: What do numbers ending in 5 have in their ones place?

revise.summary: A number statement can be true or false. To test a general claim, try many examples; one counterexample shows it is not always true.
focus: Decide if a fact is true
Complete a statement to make it true
Say if a claim is always, sometimes or never true
Find a counterexample
remember: Half of an even number is sometimes even
traps: Don't decide from only one example.
Don't confuse the adding rule with the multiplying rule.

learn.hook: Can 16 coconuts be shared equally among 3 friends? Among 4? Factors tell you instantly!
points: A factor divides a number exactly, with nothing left over. 4 is a factor of 12 because 12 ÷ 4 = 3.
Factors come in pairs: 12 = 1 × 12 = 2 × 6 = 3 × 4. So the factors of 12 are 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 12.
1 is a factor of every number, and every number is a factor of itself.
A number with exactly two factors, 1 and itself, is called a prime number. 7 is prime.

example.q: Find all the factors of 18.
steps: 4 and 5 do not divide 18 exactly; after 3 × 6 the pairs repeat

learn.reallife: Factors help us share sweets equally or arrange chairs in neat rows.

items.text: Every number has ___ as a factor

quiz.q: Which of these is a factor of 20?
quiz.explain: 20 ÷ 5 = 4 with nothing left over.
steps: A factor divides exactly: test 20 ÷ each.
quiz.mistake: Picks a number that is close to a factor but does not divide exactly

quiz.q: How many factors does 12 have?
quiz.explain: The factors are 1, 2, 3, 4, 6 and 12. That is 6 factors.

quiz.q: Which of these is NOT a factor of 24?
quiz.explain: 24 ÷ 5 = 4 with 4 left over, so 5 is not a factor.
steps: So 5 is NOT a factor of 24.
quiz.mistake: Thinks every small number is a factor

quiz.q: Which list shows all the factors of 15?
quiz.explain: 15 = 1 × 15 = 3 × 5. So the factors are 1, 3, 5 and 15.
steps: 2 and 4 do not divide 15; after 3 × 5 the pairs repeat.
quiz.mistake: Forgets 1 and the number itself, or lists a multiple like 30

quiz.q: Arjun wants to share 16 coconuts equally among friends with none left. How many friends could he share with?
quiz.explain: 16 ÷ 8 = 2 exactly. 3, 5 and 6 leave some over.
steps: He can share among a number of friends that is a factor of 16.
quiz.mistake: Does not check if the division is exact

quiz.q: Which number has only two factors, 1 and itself?
quiz.explain: 11 can only be 1 × 11, so it is a prime number. 9 = 3 × 3, 15 = 3 × 5, 21 = 3 × 7.
steps: A prime number has only the factors 1 and itself.
quiz.mistake: Thinks every odd number is prime

quiz.q: What is the biggest factor of 30 that is smaller than 30?
quiz.explain: 30 = 2 × 15, so 15 is a factor. No number between 15 and 30 divides 30 exactly.
steps: The biggest factor below 30 pairs with the smallest factor above 1, which is 2.
quiz.mistake: Thinks the number just before 30 must be a factor

teach.ask: Gappu asks: 'What is a factor? Is 4 a factor of 12?'
teach.praise: Yes! 4 goes into 12 exactly, 3 times, with nothing left over. So it is a factor!
teach.nudge: What must happen when I divide by a factor? Is anything left over?

revise.summary: A factor divides a number exactly with nothing left over, and factors come in pairs. A number with exactly two factors, 1 and itself, is a prime number.
focus: Test whether a number is a factor
List all factors using pairs
Spot prime numbers
remember: 1 is a factor of every number; every number is a factor of itself
traps: Don't forget 1 and the number itself.
Not every odd number is prime: 9 = 3 × 3.
Don't list multiples like 30 as factors of 15.

learn.hook: Coconuts are sold in bundles of 6. Can a shop sell exactly 40? Multiples will tell you!
points: Multiples of a number are the answers in its times table: multiples of 6 are 6, 12, 18, 24, …
Multiples go on forever. The first multiple of a number is the number itself.
If 3 is a factor of 12, then 12 is a multiple of 3.
Skip counting gives multiples: counting in 5s gives 5, 10, 15, 20, …

example.q: Write the first 5 multiples of 6.

learn.reallife: Packets of 6 bananas, boxes of 12 eggs and weeks of 7 days all give multiples.

games.title: True or false?
items: Every number is a multiple of itself.
4 × 3 = 12 and 4 × 4 = 16. 15 is not in the 4 times table.
A number has only a few multiples.
1 is a factor of every number.

quiz.q: Which of these is a multiple of 7?
steps: 27, 47 and 17 are not in the list.
quiz.mistake: Picks numbers with a 7 in them

quiz.q: What is the 5th multiple of 8?
quiz.mistake: Adds 8 + 5, or counts one multiple too many

quiz.q: Which list shows multiples of 4?
quiz.mistake: Mixes up factors and multiples, or picks numbers ending in 4

quiz.q: Coconuts are sold in bundles of 6. Which could be the total number of coconuts sold?
quiz.explain: 42 = 6 × 7. 34, 40 and 50 are not in the 6 times table.
steps: The total must be in the 6 times table.
quiz.mistake: Picks an even number without checking the 6 times table

quiz.q: 9 is a factor of 54. So 54 is a ___ of 9.
quiz.explain: 54 = 9 × 6, so 54 is in the 9 times table. It is a multiple of 9.
steps: If 9 is a factor of 54, then 54 = 9 × 6.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up the words factor and multiple

quiz.q: How many multiples of 5 are there from 1 to 50 (including 50)?
quiz.explain: 5, 10, 15, … 50. That is 50 ÷ 5 = 10 multiples.
quiz.mistake: Forgets to count 50, or counts the 5s in 50 wrongly

quiz.q: Meena counts in 3s starting from 3. Which number will she NOT say?
quiz.explain: 32 is not in the 3 times table: 3 × 10 = 30 and 3 × 11 = 33.
steps: 32 is not a multiple of 3, so she will not say 32.

quiz.q: What is the smallest multiple of 9 that is bigger than 50?
quiz.explain: 9 × 5 = 45 is too small. 9 × 6 = 54 is the first one bigger than 50.
quiz.mistake: Picks 63 by skipping a multiple, or 45 which is smaller than 50

teach.ask: Gappu asks: 'What is the difference between a factor and a multiple?'
teach.praise: Hurray! A factor goes into a number. A multiple is in its times table and they go on forever!
teach.nudge: Which one goes into a number? Which one do I get from the times table?

revise.summary: Multiples of a number are the answers in its times table and go on forever. If 3 is a factor of 12, then 12 is a multiple of 3.
focus: Spot multiples of a number
Find the nth multiple
Count multiples in a range
Use the words factor and multiple correctly
remember: The first multiple of a number is the number itself
traps: Numbers with a 7 in them are not always multiples of 7.
Don't mix up factor and multiple.

learn.hook: Fold a paper butterfly down the middle. Both wings match perfectly! That fold is magic: it is a line of symmetry.
points: A line of symmetry cuts a shape into two halves that match exactly, like mirror images.
If you fold along the line, one half sits exactly on the other.
Some shapes have many lines: a square has 4, an equilateral triangle has 3, a rectangle that is not a square has 2.
A circle has endless lines of symmetry: every line through its centre works.
Some shapes and letters have no line of symmetry, like the letters F and S.

example.q: How many lines of symmetry does a square have?
steps: Fold it down the middle (up and down): halves match
Fold it across the middle: halves match
Fold along each of the 2 corner-to-corner lines: halves match

learn.reallife: Rangolis, the Taj Mahal, leaves and butterflies all show lines of symmetry.

games.title: True or false?
items: A square has 4 lines of symmetry.
2 through the middles of the sides and 2 through the corners.
Every rectangle has 4 lines of symmetry.
A rectangle that is not a square has only 2.
The capital letter H has 2 lines of symmetry.
One up-down line and one across line.
A line of symmetry splits a shape into two matching halves.
Fold along it and the halves sit exactly on each other.
The capital letter F has a line of symmetry.
No fold of F makes the two halves match.

quiz.q: How many lines of symmetry does a square have?
quiz.explain: A square has 2 lines through the middles of its sides and 2 through its corners: 4 in all.
steps: Fold a square up-down and across through the middles of its sides: both match (2 lines).
Fold along each corner-to-corner line: both match (2 more lines).

quiz.q: How many lines of symmetry does a rectangle that is not a square have?
quiz.explain: Only the up-down and across lines through the middle. The corner-to-corner lines do not work.
steps: Up-down and across folds through the middle make matching halves: 2 lines.
Corner-to-corner folds do not match because the sides are of different lengths.
So a non-square rectangle has 2 lines.
quiz.mistake: Thinks a rectangle has the same lines as a square

quiz.q: Which capital letter has a line of symmetry?
quiz.explain: A has an up-down line of symmetry through its middle.
steps: A line of symmetry makes two matching halves.
F, G and J have no fold that makes their halves match.
A has an up-down line through its middle, so A.
quiz.mistake: Picks a letter that only looks balanced

quiz.q: Which capital letter has NO line of symmetry?
quiz.explain: No fold of S makes the halves match. T, M and U each have an up-down line.
steps: T, M and U each have an up-down line of symmetry.
No fold of S makes its halves match (S only matches after a half turn).
So S has NO line of symmetry.
quiz.mistake: Thinks a letter that looks the same after a turn must have a line of symmetry

quiz.q: How many lines of symmetry does an equilateral triangle (all sides equal) have?
quiz.explain: One line from each corner to the middle of the opposite side: 3 lines.
steps: Fold from each corner to the middle of the opposite side: the halves match.
So it has 3 lines of symmetry.

quiz.q: Riya folds a paper along a line and the two halves match exactly. What is the fold line called?
quiz.explain: A line that splits a shape into two matching halves is a line of symmetry.
steps: The two halves match exactly when folded.
A line that splits a shape into matching halves has a name.
It is a line of symmetry.

quiz.q: How many lines of symmetry does a circle have?
options: Endless, any line through the centre
quiz.explain: Every line through the centre of a circle cuts it into two matching halves.
steps: Any line through the centre of a circle cuts it into two matching halves.
There is no limit to how many such lines we can draw.
So a circle has endless lines of symmetry.
Answer: Endless, any line through the centre
quiz.mistake: Thinks a circle has only an up-down and an across line

quiz.q: Which capital letter has exactly 2 lines of symmetry?
quiz.explain: H has an up-down line and an across line. A has only an up-down line, E only an across line, and F has none.
steps: H matches on an up-down fold and on an across fold: 2 lines.
A has only an up-down line, E only an across line, F none.

teach.ask: Gappu asks: 'What is a line of symmetry? How do I find one?'
teach.praise: Flappy flap! Fold along the line and the two halves match. Like my wings!
teach.nudge: What do I do with the paper to test it? What happens to the two halves?

revise.summary: A line of symmetry cuts a shape into two halves that match like mirror images when folded. A square has 4, an equilateral triangle 3, a rectangle 2 and a circle endless lines.
focus: Count lines of symmetry of common shapes
Find letters with and without lines of symmetry
Explain what a line of symmetry is
remember: Square: 4 lines; equilateral triangle: 3; non-square rectangle: 2
A circle has endless lines: every line through its centre
F and S have no line of symmetry
traps: Don't forget the corner-to-corner lines of a square.
A rectangle does not have the diagonal lines.
A letter that matches after a turn (S) need not have a fold line.

topics.title: Letter cut-outs: one fold or two

learn.hook: Fold a paper once, draw half of the letter A, cut, open — a whole A! Can you cut an H with two folds?
points: A letter with a vertical line of symmetry (A, M, T, U, V, W, Y) can be cut by folding once and drawing only half.
A letter with a horizontal line of symmetry (B, C, D, E, K) can be cut with a fold across the middle.
Letters with both lines (H, I, O, X) can be cut with two folds, drawing only a quarter.
Some letters (F, G, J, L, P, R) have no line of symmetry, so folding does not help.
The fold always becomes a line of symmetry of the cut-out.

example.q: Which letters can be cut with two folds, drawing just a quarter: H, A, E or X?
steps: Two folds need both a vertical and a horizontal line of symmetry
A has only vertical, E only horizontal

learn.reallife: Decorations for Diwali and school charts are often made by folding paper and cutting once.

games.title: Fold and cut
items: You can cut the letter T by folding once and drawing half.
T has a vertical line of symmetry.
You can cut F by folding.
F has no line of symmetry.
Two folds let you draw only a quarter of H.
H has a vertical and a horizontal line.
C has a vertical line of symmetry.
C has a horizontal line of symmetry.

quiz.q: Which letter can be cut out by folding once down the middle (vertical fold) and drawing half?
quiz.explain: V has a vertical line of symmetry.
steps: A vertical fold works only for a letter with a vertical line of symmetry.
B has a horizontal line; F and R have none.
V has a vertical line, so V.
quiz.mistake: Picks a letter with a horizontal line

quiz.q: Which letter has a horizontal line of symmetry only?
quiz.explain: E matches top and bottom, but not left and right.
steps: T and A have only a vertical line; H has both lines.
E matches top and bottom but not left and right.
So E has a horizontal line only.

quiz.q: Which letter has both a vertical and a horizontal line of symmetry?
quiz.explain: X matches left-right and top-bottom.
steps: K has only a horizontal line; W and Y only a vertical line.
quiz.mistake: Thinks any symmetric letter has both

quiz.q: To cut out the letter I with two folds, how much of it do you draw?
quiz.explain: Two folds make 4 layers, so you draw one quarter.
steps: Two folds make 4 layers of paper.
You draw only one of the 4 parts.
So you draw a quarter of the I.

quiz.q: Which letter cannot be made by folding and cutting, because it has no line of symmetry?
quiz.explain: G does not match itself on any fold line.
steps: O, U and D each have a line of symmetry, so folding helps.
G does not match itself on any fold line.
So G cannot be made by folding and cutting.
quiz.mistake: Thinks every curved letter is symmetric

quiz.q: Ravi folds a paper once and cuts half a letter along the fold. He opens a perfect M. Where was the fold?
options: Down the middle of the M
Across the middle of the M
quiz.explain: M has a vertical line of symmetry, so the fold ran down its middle.
steps: The fold becomes a line of symmetry of the cut-out.
M has a vertical line of symmetry.
So the fold was down the middle of the M.
Answer: Down the middle of the M

quiz.q: How many of these letters have a vertical line of symmetry: A, U, W, S?
quiz.explain: A, U and W have one. S does not.
steps: Check each letter for an up-down line: A ✔, U ✔, W ✔.
S has no line of symmetry ✘.

quiz.q: Which group has only letters with a horizontal line of symmetry?
quiz.explain: B, C and K each match top and bottom.
steps: A, M, W and H, Y, T have vertical lines; F, P, R have none.
B, C and K each match top and bottom.

teach.ask: Gappu wants to cut out the letter H with as little drawing as possible. How should I fold the paper?
teach.praise: H has both lines of symmetry, so two folds and only a quarter to draw!
teach.nudge: Which lines of symmetry does H have?

revise.summary: Letters with a vertical line of symmetry can be cut with one vertical fold, letters with a horizontal line with one fold across, and letters with both lines with two folds, drawing a quarter.
focus: Sort letters by vertical, horizontal or both lines
Decide how to fold to cut a letter
Find letters that cannot be made by folding
remember: Vertical line: A, M, T, U, V, W, Y
Horizontal line: B, C, D, E, K
Both: H, I, O, X; none: F, G, J, L, P, R
traps: Don't mix up horizontal and vertical lines.
Two folds mean drawing a quarter, not a half.

learn.hook: Can you finish half a rangoli so it looks perfect? Let's make designs like an artist!
points: To complete a design with a mirror line, copy each part to the other side of the line.
Each point and its mirror image are the same distance from the line, on opposite sides.
On grid paper, count squares from the line to place the image exactly.
Fold-and-cut paper designs always have a line of symmetry along the fold.

example.q: On grid paper, a dot is 3 squares to the left of an up-down mirror line. Where does its mirror image go?
steps: Same distance from the line: 3 squares
example.answer: 3 squares to the right of the line, in the same row

learn.reallife: Kolam and rangoli artists, tailors and kite makers all build symmetrical designs.

games.title: Symmetrical or not?
items: Front view of the Taj Mahal

quiz.q: A dot is 2 squares to the left of an up-down mirror line. Where is its mirror image?
quiz.explain: The image is the same distance away on the other side: 2 squares to the right.
steps: A mirror image is the same distance from the line, on the other side.
The dot is 2 squares to the left.
So its image is 2 squares to the right.
quiz.mistake: Puts the image on the same side, or doubles the distance

quiz.q: Meena folds a paper in half and cuts half a heart along the fold. What does she get when she opens it?
options: A full heart with a line of symmetry
quiz.explain: The fold becomes the line of symmetry, so both halves of the heart match.
steps: The fold becomes a line of symmetry.
Cutting half a heart on the fold makes the other half match it.
So she gets a full heart with a line of symmetry.
Answer: A full heart with a line of symmetry
quiz.mistake: Thinks the two halves come apart

quiz.q: Riya draws half a butterfly on one side of a mirror line. How should she finish it?
options: Draw the same half again, facing the same way
Draw the mirror image of the half on the other side
quiz.explain: The other half must be the flipped (mirror) copy, so the wings match.
steps: The two halves must match like mirror images.
Copying the half facing the same way does not match; it must be flipped.
So draw the mirror image of the half on the other side.
Answer: Draw the mirror image of the half on the other side
quiz.mistake: Copies the half without flipping it

quiz.q: Which word looks exactly the same in a mirror placed beside it?
quiz.explain: M and O each have an up-down line of symmetry, and MOM reads the same both ways. D and B do not have an up-down line.
steps: A mirror beside a word reverses the order and flips each letter.
M and O each have an up-down line, and MOM reads the same both ways.
D, B, P and N do not have an up-down line, so MOM.
quiz.mistake: Thinks a word that reads the same both ways always looks the same in a mirror

quiz.q: Half a design touches an up-down mirror line and is 3 squares wide on its left. When it is completed, how wide is the whole design?
quiz.explain: The other half is also 3 squares wide: 3 + 3 = 6 squares.
steps: The left half is 3 squares wide and touches the line.
Its mirror half on the right is also 3 squares wide.
quiz.mistake: Forgets to add the mirrored half

quiz.q: A rangoli has 8 equal petals around the centre. How many times does it look the same in one full turn?
quiz.explain: Each petal moves to the next petal's place, 8 times in a full turn.
steps: The 8 petals are equal and spaced around the centre.
Each turn that moves a petal to the next petal's place makes it look the same.
That happens 8 times in a full turn.

quiz.q: Joseph finishes a symmetrical dot design. The left half has 7 dots and no dot is on the line. How many dots are in the whole design?
quiz.explain: The right half mirrors the left: 7 + 7 = 14 dots.
steps: The right half mirrors the left half.
No dot is on the line, so none is counted twice.

quiz.q: Harpreet makes a kite shape that is symmetrical about an up-down line. The left edge is 30 cm long. How long is the matching right edge?
quiz.explain: Mirror halves match exactly, so the right edge is also 30 cm.
steps: Mirror halves match exactly in size.
So the matching right edge is 30 cm.
quiz.mistake: Thinks the mirror half is half or double the size

teach.ask: Gappu asks: 'How do I finish a design if I only have half of it?'
teach.praise: Tweet! Flip each part to the other side, the same distance from the line. Beautiful!
teach.nudge: How do I copy each part? How far from the line should it go?

revise.summary: To complete a design with a mirror line, copy each part to the other side at the same distance. Fold-and-cut designs always have a line of symmetry along the fold.
focus: Place mirror images on grid paper
Complete half designs
Find the size or count of a completed design
remember: Image is the same distance from the line, on the opposite side
Count squares from the line to place the image
Half 3 squares wide + mirror half = 6 squares
traps: Don't put the image on the same side or at double the distance.
Don't copy the half without flipping it.

learn.hook: Spin a pinwheel. It looks the same again and again before it finishes one full turn! That is turn symmetry.
points: Some designs look exactly the same after a part of a full turn. This is turn (rotational) symmetry.
Count how many times a design looks the same in one full turn.
A square looks the same 4 times in a full turn, after every 90°.
An equilateral triangle looks the same 3 times (every 120°). A rectangle that is not a square looks the same 2 times (every 180°).
Letters like S, N and Z look the same after a half turn (180°).

example.q: A ceiling fan has 3 equal blades. What is the smallest turn after which it looks the same?
steps: It looks the same 3 times in a full turn

learn.reallife: Fans, wheels, flowers, rangolis and chakra designs show turn symmetry.

games.title: Smallest turn to look the same
True or false?
items: The letter S looks the same after a half turn.
Turn S upside down and it is still S.
The letter A looks the same after a half turn.
After a half turn, A is upside down.
A square looks the same after a quarter turn.
A quarter turn is 90°, and a square looks the same every 90°.
A fan with 3 equal blades looks the same after a 90° turn.
It looks the same every 120°, not 90°.
A rectangle that is not a square looks the same after a half turn.
After 180° the long sides are back in place.

quiz.q: A ceiling fan has 3 equal blades. After what smallest turn does it look the same?
quiz.explain: It looks the same 3 times in one full turn: 360° ÷ 3 = 120°.
steps: 3 equal blades: it looks the same 3 times in a full turn.
quiz.mistake: Thinks every shape repeats after a quarter turn

quiz.q: A square looks the same after what smallest turn?
quiz.explain: A square looks the same 4 times in a full turn: 360° ÷ 4 = 90°.
steps: A square looks the same 4 times in a full turn.
quiz.mistake: Thinks a square needs a half turn

quiz.q: Which capital letter looks the same after a half turn?
quiz.explain: Turn N upside down and it is still N. A, T and V end up upside down.
steps: A half turn turns a letter upside down.
A, T and V end up upside down and look different.
N upside down is still N, so N.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up turn symmetry with a mirror line

quiz.q: How many times does a square look the same during one full turn?
steps: Turn a square: it matches after 90°, 180°, 270° and 360°.
quiz.mistake: Counts only the half turn and full turn

quiz.q: A rectangle that is not a square looks the same after what smallest turn?
quiz.explain: After a quarter turn the long sides stand up, so it looks different. After a half turn (180°) it looks the same.
steps: After a quarter turn (90°) the long sides stand up: it looks different.
After a half turn it matches: 360° ÷ 2.
quiz.mistake: Thinks a rectangle behaves like a square

quiz.q: A flower rangoli has 6 equal petals around the centre. After what smallest turn does it look the same?
quiz.explain: It looks the same 6 times in a full turn: 360° ÷ 6 = 60°.
steps: 6 equal petals: it looks the same 6 times in a full turn.

quiz.q: A star has 5 equal points. How many times does it look the same in one full turn?
quiz.explain: Each point moves to the next point's place, so it looks the same 5 times.
steps: Each turn moves one point into the next point's place.
So it looks the same 5 times.
quiz.mistake: Counts the corners inside and outside (10)

quiz.q: Which of these does NOT look the same after a quarter turn (90°)?
options: Rectangle that is not a square
quiz.explain: A long rectangle turned 90° stands on its short side, so it looks different.
steps: A square, a circle and a 4-petal flower all match after a 90° turn.
A long rectangle turned 90° stands on its short side.
So the rectangle that is not a square does NOT look the same.
Answer: Rectangle that is not a square
quiz.mistake: Thinks all four-sided shapes act like squares

teach.ask: Gappu spins round and round: 'What is turn symmetry?'
teach.praise: Wheee! If a design looks the same before a full turn ends, it has turn symmetry!
teach.nudge: What do I do to the design? What must I see before the full turn is over?

revise.summary: A design has turn (rotational) symmetry if it looks the same after part of a full turn. Count how many times it looks the same in one full turn; the smallest turn is 360° ÷ that number.
focus: Find the smallest turn that matches
Count how many times a shape matches in a full turn
Spot letters that match after a half turn
remember: Equilateral triangle: 3 times (120°); non-square rectangle: 2 times (180°)
S, N and Z match after a half turn
traps: Don't think every shape repeats after a quarter turn.
Don't confuse turn symmetry with a mirror line.

learn.hook: Spin a paper firki slowly. At which turns does it look exactly as it started?
points: To test rotational symmetry, mark the centre, then turn the design by 1/4, 1/2, 3/4 and a full turn.
A 4-blade windmill looks the same after every 1/4 turn.
Some designs match after a 1/2 turn but NOT after a 1/4 turn — like a rectangle or the letter S.
A shape can have rotational symmetry without any line of symmetry, like a windmill whose blades all bend the same way, or the letters S, N, Z.
Every shape looks the same after a full turn, so we only count smaller turns as rotational symmetry.

example.q: A rectangle (not a square) is turned. At which of 1/4, 1/2, 3/4 turn does it look the same?
steps: 1/4 turn: it is now standing up — different
example.answer: Only at the 1/2 turn (and the full turn)

learn.reallife: Fans, wheels, flowers and windmills all have rotational symmetry.

games.title: Looks the same after a 1/4 turn?
Turn facts
items: A 4-blade firki looks the same after a 1/4 turn.
Each blade moves into the next blade's place.
The letter Z looks the same after a 1/4 turn.
Z matches only after a 1/2 turn.
A shape can have rotational symmetry but no line of symmetry.
Like a firki with bent blades, or the letter S.
Every design looks the same after a full turn.
A full turn brings it back to the start.

quiz.q: A paper windmill has 4 blades. After which smallest turn does it look the same?
quiz.explain: Each 1/4 turn moves every blade into the next blade's place.
steps: Each 1/4 turn moves every blade into the next blade's place.
So the smallest turn is 1/4 turn.
quiz.mistake: Thinks only a half turn works

quiz.q: A rectangle that is not a square is turned. At which turn does it first look the same?
quiz.explain: After a 1/4 turn it stands on its short side. After a 1/2 turn it matches.
steps: After a 1/4 turn the rectangle stands on its short side: different.
After a 1/2 turn it lies the same way again: same.
So it first looks the same at a 1/2 turn.
quiz.mistake: Thinks a rectangle acts like a square

quiz.q: Which letter looks the same after a 1/2 turn but not after a 1/4 turn?
quiz.explain: N turned upside down is still N, but a 1/4 turn lays it on its side. A and T change after a 1/2 turn; + already matches after a 1/4 turn.
steps: A and T look different after a 1/2 turn; + already matches after a 1/4 turn.
N upside down is still N, but a 1/4 turn lays it on its side.
quiz.mistake: Picks a letter that matches after every 1/4 turn

quiz.q: Which shape has rotational symmetry but NO line of symmetry?
quiz.explain: S matches after a 1/2 turn, but no fold line makes its halves match.
steps: A and T have a line of symmetry but no turn symmetry; a square has both.
S matches after a 1/2 turn, but no fold makes its halves match.
quiz.mistake: Thinks rotation and reflection always go together

quiz.q: How many times does a 4-blade windmill look the same in one full turn (counting the full turn)?
quiz.explain: At 1/4, 1/2, 3/4 and the full turn: 4 times.
steps: The windmill matches at 1/4, 1/2, 3/4 and the full turn.

quiz.q: A design matches after a 1/2 turn. Must it also match after a 1/4 turn?
quiz.explain: A rectangle matches after a 1/2 turn but not after a 1/4 turn.
steps: Look for an example: a rectangle matches after a 1/2 turn.
But a rectangle does not match after a 1/4 turn.
quiz.mistake: Thinks matching at 1/2 means matching at 1/4

quiz.q: Which test checks rotational symmetry?
options: Fold it and see if the halves match
Turn it about its centre and see if it looks the same before a full turn
quiz.explain: Rotational symmetry is about turning, not folding.
steps: Rotational symmetry is about turning, not folding.
Turn the design about its centre.
See if it looks the same before a full turn.
Answer: Turn it about its centre and see if it looks the same before a full turn

quiz.q: A firki has 3 blades all bent the same way. Which is true?
options: It looks the same after a 1/3 turn but has no line of symmetry
It looks the same only after a full turn
It has a line of symmetry but no turn symmetry
quiz.explain: The bent blades spoil every fold line, but turning by 1/3 moves each blade to the next.
steps: Turning by 1/3 moves each bent blade into the next blade's place: it matches.
The bends all go the same way, so no fold makes the halves match.
So it looks the same after a 1/3 turn but has no line of symmetry.
Answer: It looks the same after a 1/3 turn but has no line of symmetry
quiz.mistake: Thinks all turn designs have fold lines

teach.ask: Gappu's firki has 4 blades bent the same way. Does it have a line of symmetry? Does it have turn symmetry?
teach.praise: No fold line works, but it looks the same after every 1/4 turn!
teach.nudge: What happens when I fold it? And when I turn it?

revise.summary: Test rotational symmetry by marking the centre and turning by 1/4, 1/2 and 3/4. Some designs match only after a 1/2 turn, and a shape can have turn symmetry without any line of symmetry.
focus: Test a design at 1/4, 1/2 and 3/4 turns
Find shapes with turn symmetry but no fold line
Count matches in a full turn
remember: A rectangle and the letter S match after a 1/2 turn, not a 1/4 turn
Every shape matches after a full turn, so we count smaller turns
traps: Matching at 1/2 turn does not mean matching at 1/4 turn.
Rotational and reflection symmetry do not always go together.

learn.hook: Turn your notebook upside down: 69 is still 69! Which other numbers can do tricks like this?
points: Digits written in a simple way: 0 and 8 have a vertical and a horizontal line of symmetry, and look the same after a 1/2 turn.
3 has a horizontal line of symmetry only. 1 written as a straight stick has both lines and a 1/2-turn symmetry.
6 turned by a 1/2 turn becomes 9, so 69 and 96 look the same after a 1/2 turn — but they have no line of symmetry.
Numbers like 11, 88, 808 and 1001 (with stick 1s) have a vertical line, a horizontal line and 1/2-turn symmetry.
To create a number with 1/2-turn symmetry, use 0, 1, 8 in matching places, or pair 6 with 9.

example.q: Does 808 look the same after a 1/2 turn? Does it have a vertical line of symmetry?
steps: A mirror down the middle gives 8-0-8 again

learn.reallife: Some digital clock times like 10:01 look the same in a mirror. Car number plates can hide symmetry too!

games.title: Digit facts
items: 8 has a horizontal line of symmetry.
Its top and bottom halves match.
3 has a vertical line of symmetry.
6 turned by a 1/2 turn looks like 9.
0 looks the same after a 1/2 turn.
Turned upside down, it is still 0.
7 does not match on any fold.

quiz.q: Which digit has a horizontal line of symmetry but no vertical one?
quiz.explain: 3's top and bottom halves match, but its left and right do not.
steps: 0 and 8 have both lines; 7 has neither.
3's top and bottom halves match, but its left and right do not.
quiz.mistake: Picks a digit with both lines

quiz.q: Which digit has both a vertical and a horizontal line of symmetry?
quiz.explain: 8 matches left-right and top-bottom.
steps: 3 has only a horizontal line; 6 and 4 have none.

quiz.q: Which number looks the same after a 1/2 turn?
quiz.explain: Turning 69 upside down: 6 becomes 9 and 9 becomes 6, and their order flips, giving 69 again.
steps: A 1/2 turn flips the order of digits and turns 6 into 9 and 9 into 6.

quiz.q: Does 69 have a line of symmetry?
quiz.explain: No fold makes 69 match itself, but a 1/2 turn does.
steps: No fold, up-down or across, makes 69 match itself.
So no line of symmetry, only 1/2-turn symmetry.
quiz.mistake: Thinks turn symmetry means a fold line too

quiz.q: Which number (with stick 1s) has a vertical line, a horizontal line and 1/2-turn symmetry?
quiz.explain: 1001 matches in a mirror, top to bottom, and upside down.
steps: Stick 1s and 0s have both lines; the number must also read the same reversed.
1001 matches in a mirror, top to bottom and upside down.
1961, 1010 and 1221 fail one of these tests, so 1001.

quiz.q: Which 3-digit number has 1/2-turn symmetry?
quiz.explain: 808 turned upside down is still 808. 880 becomes 088.
steps: A 1/2 turn reverses the order of the digits; 0 and 8 stay the same.
quiz.mistake: Forgets the order flips in a 1/2 turn

quiz.q: Which 4-digit number looks the same after a 1/2 turn?
quiz.explain: Turned upside down, 6889 becomes 6889: the 9 at the end becomes a 6 at the front.
steps: Upside down: reverse the order and swap 6 ↔ 9 (8 stays 8).
quiz.mistake: Does not flip the order of digits

quiz.q: Which number has a horizontal line of symmetry only (not vertical)?
quiz.explain: Each 3 matches top-bottom, but 33 does not match left-right in a mirror.
steps: 00, 88 and 11 (stick 1s) have both a vertical and a horizontal line.
Each 3 matches top–bottom, but 33 does not match left–right in a mirror.

teach.ask: Gappu wants a 2-digit number that looks the same upside down but has no line of symmetry. Can you help?
teach.praise: 69! A half turn changes 6 into 9 and 9 into 6, so it stays 69!
teach.nudge: What happens to 6 when it is turned upside down?

revise.summary: Digits have symmetry too: 0 and 8 have both lines and half-turn symmetry, 3 has only a horizontal line. A half turn reverses digit order and swaps 6 and 9, so 69 and 96 match after a half turn.
focus: Find lines of symmetry in digits
Check if a number looks the same after a half turn
Make numbers with half-turn symmetry
remember: 0, 8 and stick 1: both lines and half-turn symmetry
traps: 66 does not stay 66 after a half turn; it becomes 99.
Turn symmetry does not mean a fold line: 69 has none.

learn.hook: Can you colour a 3 by 3 square with just two colours so it looks the same after every quarter turn?
points: To test a design for rotational symmetry, trace it, turn the tracing about the centre, and check if it fits.
To make a design match after a 1/2 turn, every shape must have a partner exactly opposite through the centre.
For a 1/4-turn match, every shape needs partners in all four quarter positions.
Lines of reflection symmetry are drawn where folding makes the halves match. A design may have several.
In a 3 × 3 grid, colouring the 4 corners one colour and the 4 edge squares another gives a 1/4-turn match.

example.q: A design has a red dot at the top. What must you add so it matches after a 1/2 turn?
steps: A 1/2 turn moves the top to the bottom
So add a red dot at the bottom, the same distance from the centre
example.answer: A red dot at the bottom

learn.reallife: Rangolis, kolams and tile floors are planned so they match after turns and folds.

games.title: Design checks
items: If every shape has a partner opposite through the centre, the design matches after a 1/2 turn.
A design with a dot only at the top matches after a 1/4 turn.
After the turn, the dot is on the right.
Colouring a 2 × 2 grid with two colours can give a 1/4-turn match.
A 1/4 turn moves every cell to the next, so all four must be one colour.
Tracing paper helps test rotational symmetry.
Turn the tracing and see if it fits.

quiz.q: A design has one star at the top. Where must another star go so the design matches after a 1/2 turn?
quiz.explain: A 1/2 turn sends the top to the bottom.
steps: A 1/2 turn moves the top to the bottom.
For the design to match, the star must have a partner there.
So another star goes at the bottom.
quiz.mistake: Thinks a 1/2 turn goes to the side

quiz.q: A design has a dot at the top. Which dots must be added for it to match after every 1/4 turn?
quiz.explain: Each 1/4 turn moves the dot to the next side: right, bottom, left.
steps: Each 1/4 turn moves the top dot to the next side.
It visits right, then bottom, then left.
So add dots at the right, bottom and left.

quiz.q: How can you test a design for rotational symmetry?
options: Trace it and turn the tracing about the centre
quiz.explain: Turning the tracing shows whether the design fits itself before a full turn.
steps: Trace the design and turn the tracing about the centre.
If it fits before a full turn, it has rotational symmetry.
Answer: Trace it and turn the tracing about the centre
quiz.mistake: Uses a fold, which tests reflection

quiz.q: In a 3 × 3 grid, how can two colours be used so it looks the same after every 1/4 turn?
options: 4 corners one colour, 4 edge squares the other
Top row one colour, the rest the other
Left column one colour, the rest the other
quiz.explain: Corners turn into corners and edges into edges, so this matches.
steps: A 1/4 turn sends corners to corners and edge squares to edge squares.
A row turns into a column, so colouring a row or column fails.
So colour the 4 corners one colour and the 4 edge squares the other.
Answer: 4 corners one colour, 4 edge squares the other
quiz.mistake: Colours a row, which moves to a column after a turn

quiz.q: A square rangoli has the same pattern on every side. How many lines of symmetry can it have at most?
quiz.explain: A square has 4 lines: 2 through opposite corners and 2 through the middles of opposite sides.
steps: A square shape with the same pattern on every side can match on the lines of a square.
A square has 2 lines through opposite corners and 2 through the middles of opposite sides.
quiz.mistake: Counts only the up-down and across lines

quiz.q: Which change makes this design match after a 1/2 turn: a triangle on the left only?
options: Add a triangle at the top
Remove the triangle and add a circle at the top
Add a square on the left
Add the same triangle on the right, turned upside down
quiz.explain: A 1/2 turn moves the left triangle to the right and turns it upside down, so that is the partner it needs.
steps: A 1/2 turn moves the left side to the right and turns things upside down.
So the left triangle needs a partner on the right, upside down.
Add the same triangle on the right, turned upside down.
Answer: Add the same triangle on the right, turned upside down
quiz.mistake: Adds the partner in the wrong place

quiz.q: A design looks the same after a 1/4 turn. Does it also look the same after a 1/2 turn?
options: Yes, because two 1/4 turns make a 1/2 turn
Only if it is a circle
quiz.explain: If it matches after one 1/4 turn, it matches after two of them as well.
steps: If it matches after one 1/4 turn, it matches again after the second.
So yes, because two 1/4 turns make a 1/2 turn.
Answer: Yes, because two 1/4 turns make a 1/2 turn
quiz.mistake: Thinks each turn must be checked from scratch

quiz.q: A design has a line of symmetry going down the middle. What does that mean?
options: Folding along it makes the two halves match
Turning it by 1/4 makes it match
quiz.explain: A line of symmetry is a fold line where the halves match.
steps: A line of symmetry is a fold line.
Folding along it makes the two halves match.
So that is what it means.
Answer: Folding along it makes the two halves match
quiz.mistake: Confuses a fold line with a turn

teach.ask: Gappu drew a flower petal pointing up. How do I finish it so it looks the same after every quarter turn?
teach.praise: I add petals pointing right, down and left — 4 petals in all!
teach.nudge: Where does the petal go after a quarter turn?

revise.summary: To make a design match after a 1/2 turn, every shape needs a partner exactly opposite the centre; for a 1/4 turn, partners in all four quarter positions. Test by tracing and turning.
focus: Add shapes so a design matches after a 1/2 or 1/4 turn
Test a design by tracing and turning
Colour a grid with 1/4-turn symmetry
remember: 1/2 turn sends top to bottom and left to right
In a 3 × 3 grid: corners one colour, edge squares another
If it matches after 1/4 turn, it also matches after 1/2 turn
traps: Don't use folding to test turning.
Adding only the opposite dot is not enough for a 1/4 turn.

learn.hook: Take squares and equilateral triangles with the same side length. Join them to make star and flower designs!
points: Squares and equilateral triangles with equal sides fit neatly edge to edge.
A square with a triangle on each of its 4 sides makes a star with 4 lines of symmetry and 1/4-turn symmetry.
A square with a triangle on just one side has 1 line of symmetry but no rotational symmetry.
A square with triangles on two opposite sides has 2 lines of symmetry and 1/2-turn symmetry.
Sort designs: reflection only, rotation only, or both.

example.q: A square has triangles on its top and bottom sides. Which symmetries does it have?
steps: Up-down and left-right folds both match: 2 lines
A 1/2 turn swaps the top and bottom triangles: matches
A 1/4 turn puts the triangles at the sides: no match

learn.reallife: Mosaics in temples and mosques often join squares and triangles into beautiful symmetric stars.

games.title: Sort the design
items: Square + triangles on top and bottom
Square + triangles on top and right

quiz.q: A square has an equilateral triangle on each of its 4 sides. How many lines of symmetry?
quiz.explain: The star matches on both diagonal folds and both middle folds: 4 lines.
steps: The star matches on both middle folds (up-down and across).
It also matches on both corner-to-corner folds.

quiz.q: That 4-triangle star is turned. After which smallest turn does it look the same?
quiz.explain: Each 1/4 turn moves every triangle to the next side.
steps: There is a triangle on each of the 4 sides.
Each 1/4 turn moves every triangle to the next side.
So the smallest turn is 1/4 turn.

quiz.q: A square has a triangle on its top side only. What symmetry does it have?
options: 1 line of symmetry, no turn symmetry
quiz.explain: Folding down the middle matches, but any turn moves the triangle away.
steps: Folding down the middle puts the top triangle on itself: 1 line.
Any turn moves the triangle off the top: no turn symmetry.
So 1 line of symmetry, no turn symmetry.
Answer: 1 line of symmetry, no turn symmetry
quiz.mistake: Thinks every design has turn symmetry

quiz.q: A square has triangles on the top and bottom. Does it look the same after a 1/2 turn?
quiz.explain: A 1/2 turn swaps the top and bottom triangles, so it matches.
steps: A 1/2 turn moves the top to the bottom and the bottom to the top.

quiz.q: Does that same design (triangles on top and bottom) match after a 1/4 turn?
quiz.explain: After a 1/4 turn the triangles are on the left and right.
steps: A 1/4 turn moves the top and bottom triangles to the left and right.
There are no triangles there to begin with.
So no, it does not match.
quiz.mistake: Thinks matching at 1/2 means matching at 1/4

quiz.q: Six equilateral triangles meet at a point to form a hexagon. How many times does it look the same in one full turn?
quiz.explain: Every 1/6 turn moves each triangle into the next place: 6 times.
steps: The hexagon has 6 equal triangles around the centre.
Every 1/6 turn moves each triangle into the next place.
So it looks the same 6 times.
quiz.mistake: Counts the lines of the hexagon wrongly

quiz.q: A square has triangles on its top and right sides. Which is true?
options: It has 1 line of symmetry (a diagonal) and no turn symmetry
quiz.explain: The fold along the diagonal between top and right swaps the two triangles. No turn matches.
steps: The diagonal between the top and right sides swaps the two triangles: 1 line.
Any turn sends a triangle to a side that had none: no turn symmetry.
So 1 line of symmetry (a diagonal) and no turn symmetry.
Answer: It has 1 line of symmetry (a diagonal) and no turn symmetry
quiz.mistake: Thinks two triangles always give 2 lines

quiz.q: Which design has BOTH reflection and rotational symmetry?
options: Square with triangles on top and right
Square with triangles on all 4 sides
Triangle with a square on one side
quiz.explain: The 4-triangle star has 4 lines and 1/4-turn symmetry.
steps: One triangle, or triangles on top and right, give only a fold line.
The square with triangles on all 4 sides has 4 lines and 1/4-turn symmetry.
So the square with triangles on all 4 sides.
Answer: Square with triangles on all 4 sides
quiz.mistake: Picks a design with only a fold line

teach.ask: Gappu put one triangle on the top of a square. How can I change it so it looks the same after a half turn?
teach.praise: I add a triangle at the bottom — then a half turn matches!
teach.nudge: Where does the top triangle go after a half turn?

revise.summary: Squares and equilateral triangles fit edge to edge into designs. Triangles on all 4 sides give 4 lines and 1/4-turn symmetry; on two opposite sides, 2 lines and 1/2-turn symmetry; on one side, 1 line only.
focus: Find the symmetries of square-and-triangle designs
Sort designs into reflection only, rotation only or both
remember: Top and bottom triangles: 2 lines + 1/2-turn symmetry
Top and right triangles: 1 diagonal line, no turn symmetry
traps: Matching at 1/2 turn does not mean matching at 1/4 turn.
Two triangles do not always give 2 lines.

learn.hook: In Rajasthan, craftspeople carve wooden blocks and stamp them on cloth. Turn the block and stamp again — a pattern appears!
points: A block print is a mirror image of the carved block, like a stamp.
Printing a block 4 times around a centre, turning it a 1/4 turn each time, makes a design with 1/4-turn symmetry.
Printing it twice with a 1/2 turn gives a design with 1/2-turn symmetry.
Border shapes repeat along a line. Some have reflection symmetry (like ▲ or ♥), some have rotational symmetry (like S or Z), some have both (like X or ◆).
You can print your own patterns with blocks cut from vegetables like potato or lady's finger.

example.q: A block makes an L-shaped print. You print it 4 times around a point, turning 1/4 each time. What symmetry does the design have?
steps: Each print is the last one turned by 1/4
So the whole design matches after a 1/4 turn

learn.reallife: Bagru and Sanganer in Rajasthan are famous for block printing. Lady's finger cut across makes a lovely star stamp!

games.title: Block printing facts
items: A print is a mirror image of the carving.
Printing 4 times with 1/4 turns gives 1/4-turn symmetry.
Each print is the next one turned.
Printing twice with a 1/2 turn always gives 4 lines of symmetry.
It gives 1/2-turn symmetry; lines depend on the block.
Lady's finger cut across makes a star-like print.
Its cross-section has ridges around a centre.

quiz.q: A carved block shows the letter F facing right. Which way does the print face?
quiz.explain: Stamping flips the carving, so the print is its mirror image.
steps: Stamping flips the carving like a mirror.
So the print faces left (a mirror image).
quiz.mistake: Thinks the print copies the block exactly

quiz.q: A block is printed 4 times around a centre, turned by a 1/4 turn each time. What symmetry does the design have?
quiz.explain: Each print is the previous one turned by 1/4, so the whole design matches after a 1/4 turn.
steps: Each print is the previous one turned by 1/4.
So the whole design fits itself after a 1/4 turn.
quiz.mistake: Thinks turning the block spoils the symmetry

quiz.q: A block is printed twice with a 1/2 turn between prints. After which turn does the design match?
quiz.explain: The two prints swap places after a 1/2 turn.
steps: The two prints are a 1/2 turn apart.
After a 1/2 turn they swap places.
So the design matches after a 1/2 turn.
quiz.mistake: Thinks it matches after a 1/4 turn

quiz.q: How many times must you print a block, turning 1/4 each time, to complete a 1/4-turn design?
quiz.explain: Four quarter turns make a full turn, so 4 prints.
steps: Each print is turned 1/4 from the last.

quiz.q: Which border shape has rotational symmetry but no line of symmetry?
quiz.explain: Z matches after a 1/2 turn but has no fold line.
steps: ▲, A and ♥ each have a fold line.
Z matches after a 1/2 turn but has no fold line.
quiz.mistake: Picks a shape with a fold line

quiz.q: Which border shape has both reflection and rotational symmetry?
quiz.explain: X has fold lines and also matches after a 1/2 turn.
steps: S and N have only turn symmetry; ♥ has only a fold line.
X has fold lines and also matches after a 1/2 turn.
quiz.mistake: Picks a shape with only one kind

quiz.q: Which border shape has reflection symmetry only?
quiz.explain: A heart matches when folded down the middle, but not after a 1/2 turn.
steps: S, Z and N match only after a 1/2 turn.
A heart matches when folded down the middle but not after a 1/2 turn.

quiz.q: Which vegetable, cut across, gives a print with many matching parts around a centre?
options: A long bean cut along its length
quiz.explain: Bhindi cut across shows ridges all around its centre, like a star.
steps: We need a cut that shows parts arranged around a centre.
Bhindi cut across shows ridges all around its centre, like a star.
quiz.mistake: Picks a cut that has no centre pattern

teach.ask: Gappu has a potato block shaped like a leaf. How can I print a design that looks the same after every quarter turn?
teach.praise: I print the leaf 4 times around a centre, turning it a quarter each time!
teach.nudge: How many prints and how much turning do I need?

revise.summary: A block print is a mirror image of the block. Printing it 4 times with 1/4 turns gives 1/4-turn symmetry, and twice with a 1/2 turn gives 1/2-turn symmetry. Border shapes can have reflection, rotation or both.
focus: Predict how a block print faces
Find the symmetry of printed designs
Sort border shapes by symmetry
remember: Print = mirror image of the carving
▲, ♥: reflection; S, Z: rotation; X, ◆: both
traps: The print does not copy the block exactly.
Two prints are not enough for a 1/4-turn design.

learn.hook: Nani wants to sew a lace border all around her quilt. How much lace does she need? That length is the perimeter!
points: Perimeter is the total length of the boundary (the edge all around) of a shape.
To find it, add the lengths of all the sides.
Rectangle: perimeter = length + breadth + length + breadth = 2 × (length + breadth).
Square: all 4 sides are equal, so perimeter = 4 × side.
Perimeter is measured in units of length: cm, m or km.

example.q: Nani's quilt is a rectangle 3 m long and 2 m wide. How much lace goes around it?

learn.reallife: Fences around a field, frames around a photo and the boundary of a cricket ground are perimeters.

games.title: True or false?
items: Perimeter is the distance all around a shape.
It is the length of the boundary.
The perimeter of a square is 4 × side.
A rectangle 5 cm by 2 cm has a perimeter of 10 cm.
5 + 2 + 5 + 2 = 14 cm. 10 is the area in square cm.
Perimeter can be measured in cm, m or km.
Perimeter is measured in square units.
Square units are for area. Perimeter is a length.

quiz.q: What is the perimeter of a rectangle 8 cm long and 5 cm wide?
quiz.mistake: Adds only two sides (13 cm) or multiplies (40)

quiz.q: What is the perimeter of a square with side 7 cm?
quiz.explain: A square has 4 equal sides: 4 × 7 = 28 cm.
steps: Square: all 4 sides are equal, so perimeter = 4 × side.

quiz.q: A triangle has sides 5 cm, 6 cm and 7 cm. What is its perimeter?
quiz.explain: Add all three sides: 5 + 6 + 7 = 18 cm.
steps: Perimeter = sum of all the sides.
quiz.mistake: Adds only two sides, or multiplies

quiz.q: Nani's square table cloth has sides of 2 m. How much lace goes all around it?
quiz.explain: 4 sides of 2 m each: 4 × 2 = 8 m.
steps: Lace goes all around: the perimeter of the square.

quiz.q: A garden is 20 m long and 15 m wide. How long is the fence around it?
quiz.mistake: Adds only one length and one breadth

quiz.q: The perimeter of a square is 36 cm. How long is each side?
quiz.explain: A square has 4 equal sides: 36 ÷ 4 = 9 cm.
steps: Perimeter of a square = 4 × side, so side = perimeter ÷ 4.

quiz.q: A rectangle has a perimeter of 30 cm. Its length is 10 cm. What is its breadth?
quiz.explain: Length + breadth is half the perimeter: 30 ÷ 2 = 15. Breadth = 15 − 10 = 5 cm.
quiz.mistake: Takes 10 away from 30 without halving first

quiz.q: Which has the longer perimeter: a square with side 6 cm, or a rectangle 8 cm by 3 cm?
quiz.explain: Square: 4 × 6 = 24 cm. Rectangle: 2 × (8 + 3) = 22 cm. 24 > 22.
steps: 24 > 22, so the square has the longer perimeter.
quiz.mistake: Thinks the shape with the longest side has the bigger perimeter

teach.ask: Gappu asks: 'What is perimeter? How do I find it for my nest?'
teach.praise: Chirp! Perimeter is the length all around. Just add all the sides!
teach.nudge: Is perimeter inside or around a shape? What do I do with the sides?

revise.summary: Perimeter is the total length of the boundary of a shape: add all the sides. Rectangle: 2 × (length + breadth); square: 4 × side.
focus: Find the perimeter of rectangles, squares and triangles
Find a missing side from the perimeter
Compare perimeters of two shapes
remember: Perimeter is in cm, m or km
traps: Don't add only two sides.
Don't multiply side × side; that is area.
For a missing side of a rectangle, halve the perimeter first.

learn.hook: Nani wants lace around a table cloth — half in red and half in gold. How much of each should she buy?
points: The lace needed for a border is the perimeter of the cloth.
A cloth 2 m by 1 m 50 cm needs 2 m + 1 m 50 cm + 2 m + 1 m 50 cm = 7 m of lace.
To split the lace equally between two colours, halve the perimeter: 7 m ÷ 2 = 3 m 50 cm.
Different rectangles can have the same perimeter. Perimeter 20 cm: 1 × 9, 2 × 8, 3 × 7, 4 × 6 and 5 × 5.
Tip: length + breadth = half the perimeter.

example.q: Draw rectangles with whole-number sides and a perimeter of 16 cm.

learn.reallife: Tailors measure the edge of a dupatta to buy lace, and gardeners fence beds of the same length in different shapes.

games.title: Perimeter 20 cm: find the other side

quiz.q: A table cloth is 2 m long and 1 m 50 cm wide. How much lace goes all around it?
Nani uses red lace for half of that 7 m border and gold for the other half. How much red lace?
quiz.explain: 7 m = 700 cm. Half is 350 cm = 3 m 50 cm.
quiz.mistake: Writes half of 7 m as 3 m 5 cm

quiz.q: A square cushion has sides of 40 cm. How much lace is needed around it?
steps: Lace around a square = perimeter = 4 × side.

quiz.q: Which rectangle has a perimeter of 20 cm?
A rectangle has a perimeter of 24 cm and length 9 cm. What is its breadth?
quiz.explain: Length + breadth = 24 ÷ 2 = 12. 12 − 9 = 3 cm.

quiz.q: How many rectangles with whole-number sides have a perimeter of 16 cm? (2 by 6 and 6 by 2 count as one.)
quiz.explain: Length + breadth = 8: 1 + 7, 2 + 6, 3 + 5, 4 + 4. That is 4 rectangles.

quiz.q: Which two rectangles have the same perimeter?
quiz.explain: Both have length + breadth = 10, so perimeter 20 cm.
steps: Perimeter = 2 × (length + breadth), so compare length + breadth.
Only 2 cm × 8 cm and 4 cm × 6 cm both give 10, so both have perimeter 20 cm.
Answer: 2 cm × 8 cm and 4 cm × 6 cm

quiz.q: A dupatta is 2 m 20 cm long and 80 cm wide. How much lace goes around it?
quiz.mistake: Adds only one length and one breadth

teach.ask: Gappu wants to build 3 different rectangular nests, each with a border of 12 sticks of 1 cm. Which sizes can I make?
teach.praise: Length + breadth = 6, so 1 × 5, 2 × 4 and 3 × 3!
teach.nudge: What must length + breadth add up to?

revise.summary: The lace for a border is the perimeter of the cloth. Different rectangles can have the same perimeter, because only length + breadth (half the perimeter) matters.
focus: Find lace needed for a border in m and cm
Halve a length in m and cm
List rectangles with a given perimeter
remember: 2 m by 1 m 50 cm needs 7 m of lace
traps: Half of 7 m is 3 m 50 cm, not 3 m 5 cm.
Don't count 2 by 6 and 6 by 2 as different rectangles.

learn.hook: Nani's quilt is made of little square patches. Count the patches and you know how much the quilt covers!
points: Area is the amount of surface a shape covers.
We measure area by counting unit squares. A 1 cm by 1 cm square has an area of 1 square cm (1 sq cm).
For a rectangle, area = length × breadth. 5 rows of 3 squares = 15 square units.
Two half squares make one full square.
Area uses square units: sq cm, sq m.

example.q: Nani's quilt has 6 patches along its length and 4 along its width. Each patch is 1 square unit. What is its area?

learn.reallife: Painters, carpet sellers and farmers all think about area.

games.title: Area or perimeter?
items: Border tape around a notice board

quiz.q: What is the area of a rectangle 5 cm long and 3 cm wide?
quiz.explain: Area = 5 × 3 = 15 sq cm.
steps: Area of a rectangle = length × breadth.
quiz.mistake: Finds the perimeter (16 cm) instead of the area

quiz.q: What is the area of a square with side 6 cm?
quiz.explain: Area = 6 × 6 = 36 sq cm.
steps: Area of a square = side × side.

quiz.q: A shape covers 8 full squares and 4 half squares. What is its area?
quiz.explain: 4 half squares make 2 full squares. 8 + 2 = 10 square units.
quiz.mistake: Counts each half square as a full square

quiz.q: Nani's quilt has 7 rows of 5 patches. How many patches are there?
quiz.explain: 7 rows × 5 patches = 35.
steps: 7 rows with 5 patches in each row: multiply.
quiz.mistake: Adds rows and patches instead of multiplying

quiz.q: Which unit should we use for the area of a notebook cover?
quiz.explain: Area is measured in square units. A notebook is small, so square centimetres fit.
steps: Area is measured in square units, not cm, kg or litres.
quiz.mistake: Uses a unit of length for area

quiz.q: A room floor is 4 m by 3 m. Each tile covers 1 sq m. How many tiles cover the floor?
quiz.explain: Area = 4 × 3 = 12 sq m, so 12 tiles.
steps: Area of the floor = 4 × 3 sq m.
Each tile covers 1 sq m, so 12 tiles.
quiz.mistake: Adds length and breadth, or finds the perimeter

quiz.q: A rectangle has an area of 24 sq cm. Its length is 6 cm. What is its breadth?
quiz.explain: Length × breadth = area, so breadth = 24 ÷ 6 = 4 cm.
steps: Area = length × breadth, so breadth = area ÷ length.

quiz.q: Arjun says the area of a square with side 3 cm is 12 sq cm. What went wrong?
options: He found the perimeter, not the area
quiz.explain: 4 × 3 = 12 is the perimeter. The area is 3 × 3 = 9 sq cm.
steps: Arjun's 12 = 4 × 3, which adds the 4 sides: that is the perimeter.
So he found the perimeter, not the area.
Answer: He found the perimeter, not the area

teach.ask: Gappu asks: 'What is area? How is it different from the border?'
teach.praise: Wow! Area is how much space a shape covers, counted in squares!
teach.nudge: Is area the edge or the inside? How do we count it?

revise.summary: Area is the amount of surface a shape covers, measured by counting unit squares. For a rectangle, area = length × breadth, in square units.
focus: Find area of rectangles and squares
Count half squares in an area
Find a missing side from the area
Choose square units
remember: Two half squares make one full square

topics.title: Covering surfaces and choosing area units

learn.hook: Try to cover your desk with bangles. Now try with notebooks. Which one leaves gaps?
points: Shapes that cover a surface with no gaps and no overlaps tile it. Squares, rectangles and triangles can; circles always leave gaps.
We can measure a table's area using any tile as the unit: squares, rectangles or triangles.
Two matching triangles (half squares) make one square. So 12 squares = 24 triangles.
A rectangle made of 2 squares is a bigger unit: 12 squares = 6 such rectangles.
Everyday objects like notebooks, postcards or tiles cover a desk fully; coins and bangles leave gaps.

example.q: A table top is covered by 15 squares. How many half-square triangles would cover it?

learn.reallife: Tilers choose square or rectangular tiles because they cover floors fully. Round tiles would leave gaps!

quiz.q: Which shape leaves gaps when covering a table?
quiz.explain: Circles touch only at points, so gaps are left between them.
steps: Squares, rectangles and triangles fit edge to edge with no gaps.
Circles touch only at points, so gaps are left.

quiz.q: A table top is covered by 12 square tiles. How many half-square triangles would cover it?
quiz.explain: Each square is 2 triangles: 12 × 2 = 24.
steps: Each square is made of 2 half-square triangles.

quiz.q: The same table (12 squares) is covered with rectangles each made of 2 squares. How many rectangles?
quiz.explain: 12 ÷ 2 = 6 rectangles.
steps: Each rectangle is made of 2 squares.

quiz.q: A region needs 18 triangles (each half a square). What is its area in squares?
quiz.explain: 2 triangles make 1 square: 18 ÷ 2 = 9.

quiz.q: Which everyday objects would cover a desk fully, with no gaps?
quiz.explain: Notebooks are rectangles, which fit edge to edge.
steps: To cover with no gaps, the objects must fit edge to edge.
Bangles, coins and marbles are round and leave gaps.
Notebooks of the same size are rectangles, so they cover fully.
Answer: Notebooks of the same size

quiz.q: Why do we say area is measured by counting units?
options: Area is the number of corners
Area tells how many units cover the surface
Area is the length of the edge
Area is the weight of the surface
quiz.explain: Area is the amount of surface, counted in units like squares.
steps: Area is the amount of surface.
We find it by counting how many units (like squares) cover it.
So area tells how many units cover the surface.
Answer: Area tells how many units cover the surface

quiz.q: A desk is covered by 10 squares and 4 half-square triangles. What is the area in squares?
quiz.explain: 4 triangles = 2 squares. 10 + 2 = 12 squares.
quiz.mistake: Counts each triangle as a full square

quiz.q: Raju measured his table as 8 big rectangles. Each big rectangle is 3 squares. What is the area in squares?
quiz.explain: 8 × 3 = 24 squares.

teach.ask: Gappu covered his table with 14 square tiles. How many triangle tiles (half a square each) would cover it?
teach.praise: Two triangles make one square, so 14 squares = 28 triangles!
teach.nudge: How many triangles make one square?

revise.summary: Shapes that cover a surface with no gaps or overlaps can be area units. Two half-square triangles make one square, and a 2-square rectangle is a bigger unit.

Know which shapes or objects cover without gaps
remember: Circles, coins and bangles leave gaps

Don't count a half-square triangle as a whole square.

topics.title: Comparing and estimating areas on a grid

learn.hook: Trace your palm on squared paper. How many squares does it cover? Count the full ones and the half ones!
points: To compare areas, count the unit squares each shape covers. More squares means more area.
For an irregular shape like a leaf or a palm, count the full squares, then the half-or-more squares. Ignore squares less than half covered.
Estimate: area ≈ full squares + half-or-more squares.
A cut-out unit square can be moved around a shape to measure its area too.
Two halves make about one whole square.

example.q: A leaf traced on a grid covers 18 full squares and 10 squares that are about half covered. Estimate its area.

games.title: Smallest area first
items: A shape of 10 full and 4 half squares

games.title: Grid counting
items: Squares less than half covered are ignored when estimating.
