Two half squares make about one full square.
A 3 by 3 square has more area than a 2 by 4 rectangle.
A shape that looks longer always has more area.
Count the squares to be sure.

quiz.q: Shape A covers 14 unit squares and shape B covers 12. Which has the bigger area?
quiz.explain: 14 squares is more than 12 squares.
steps: More unit squares means more area.
So shape A has the bigger area.
quiz.mistake: Judges by how the shape looks

quiz.q: A 3 by 3 square and a 2 by 5 rectangle are on a grid. Which has more area?
quiz.explain: 3 × 3 = 9 squares and 2 × 5 = 10 squares.
steps: 10 > 9, so the rectangle has more area.

quiz.q: A palm tracing covers 30 full squares and 12 half squares. Estimate the area.
quiz.explain: 12 halves ≈ 6 full squares. 30 + 6 = 36.
quiz.mistake: Counts half squares as full ones

quiz.q: When estimating the area of a leaf on a grid, which squares do we ignore?
quiz.explain: Tiny bits of squares are too small to count.
steps: Count full squares and half-or-more squares.
Squares less than half covered are too small to count.
So we ignore squares less than half covered.
Answer: Squares less than half covered

quiz.q: A leaf covers 22 full squares and 8 squares about half covered. About how many square units is its area?
quiz.explain: 8 halves ≈ 4 squares. 22 + 4 = 26.

quiz.q: Riya moves a 1 cm cut-out square across her book cover and fits it 24 times without overlap. What is the area?
quiz.explain: Each fit is 1 sq cm, so 24 sq cm.
steps: Each fit of the cut-out is 1 sq cm.

Its curved edges cut squares into odd parts

teach.ask: Gappu traced his wing on a grid: 16 full squares and 6 half squares. What is its area, roughly?

teach.nudge: How many full squares do 6 half squares make?

revise.summary: Compare areas by counting unit squares. For an irregular shape, count full squares and half-or-more squares, ignoring tiny bits; the result is an estimate.
focus: Compare areas on a grid
Estimate the area of a leaf or palm
Use a cut-out unit square to measure
remember: Two halves make about one whole square
traps: Don't count half squares as full ones.
Don't count squares that are less than half covered.

learn.hook: Trisha says, 'If a shape has more area, it must have more perimeter.' Is she right? Let us test it!

learn.hook: Railway tickets say 14:30, not 2:30 p.m. Why? Because trains run day and night!
points: Read a clock: the short hand shows the hour, the long hand the minutes (each number = 5 minutes).

topics.title: Working backwards to find start times

points: End time = start time + duration. Start time = end time − duration.

quiz.explain: 24 ÷ 4 = 6 jumps.
steps: The frog jumps 4 at a time.

quiz.q: A deer jumps 5 and a hare jumps 3 from 0. Which spot do they both land on?
quiz.explain: 45 is a multiple of both 5 and 3.
steps: They both land on common multiples of 5 and 3 (multiples of 15).
50 and 25 are not multiples of 3; 27 is not a multiple of 5.
quiz.mistake: Picks a multiple of only one

quiz.q: Which number is NOT a common multiple of 2 and 5?
quiz.explain: 25 is not even, so it is not a multiple of 2.
steps: A common multiple of 2 and 5 must be even and end in 0.
25 is odd, so 25 is NOT a common multiple.

quiz.q: How many common multiples of 4 and 6 are there from 1 to 50?
quiz.explain: 12, 24, 36 and 48: four of them.
steps: Common multiples of 4 and 6 are multiples of 12.

teach.ask: Gappu jumps 3 and his friend jumps 5. Will we both land on 20? On 30?
teach.praise: We both land on 30 because it is a multiple of 3 and 5, but only my friend lands on 20!
teach.nudge: Is 20 a multiple of 3? Is 30?

revise.summary: Common multiples of two numbers are all multiples of the smallest one, so they go up by it each time. An animal lands on a target only if the target is a multiple of its jump size.
focus: List common multiples
Decide which animal lands on a target
Find how many jumps each animal needs
remember: Rabbit (6) lands on 30; frog (4) does not
traps: Don't include numbers that are multiples of only one.
Don't use the other animal's jump size.

learn.hook: Two temple bells ring every 4 and 6 minutes. They ring together at 7:00. When will they ring together again?
points: When two things repeat at different gaps, they happen together at common multiples of the gaps.
The next time they happen together is the smallest common multiple.
If one number is a multiple of the other, the bigger number is the smallest common multiple: for 4 and 8 it is 8.
List multiples of the bigger number and check which is also a multiple of the smaller one. That is quick!

example.q: Bell A rings every 4 minutes and bell B every 6 minutes. Both ring at 7:00 a.m. When do they next ring together?
steps: Is 6 a multiple of 4? No. Is 12? Yes

learn.reallife: Bus timings, festival lights blinking at different speeds and buying packs to get equal numbers all use common multiples.

games.title: True or false?
items: The smallest common multiple of 4 and 8 is 32.
8 is already a multiple of 4, so the answer is 8.
Two numbers have many common multiples.
For 2 and 3: 6, 12, 18, 24, … they go on forever.
Every common multiple of 2 and 3 is also a multiple of 6.
Multiplying two numbers always gives their smallest common multiple.
For 6 and 9, 6 × 9 = 54, but 18 is smaller and works.
24 is a common multiple of 6 and 8.

quiz.q: Two bells ring every 6 minutes and every 8 minutes. They ring together at 9:00 a.m. After how many minutes do they ring together again?
quiz.explain: Multiples of 8: 8, 16, 24. 24 is also a multiple of 6. So after 24 minutes.
quiz.mistake: Multiplies 6 × 8 (48), which is a common multiple but not the first

quiz.q: Riya visits the library every 4 days and Kabir every 6 days. They were both there today. In how many days will they meet there again?
quiz.explain: Multiples of 6: 6, 12. 12 is also a multiple of 4. They meet in 12 days.

quiz.q: Laddoos come in boxes of 6 and pedas in boxes of 4. Meena wants the same number of each. What is the smallest number she can buy of each?
quiz.explain: 12 is the smallest number in both the 6 and 4 times tables. 2 boxes of laddoos and 3 boxes of pedas.

quiz.q: Two strings of Diwali lights blink every 3 seconds and every 5 seconds. They blink together now. After how many seconds will they blink together again?
quiz.explain: 3 and 5 have no common multiple smaller than 15. 15 = 3 × 5.

quiz.q: A blue bus leaves the depot every 10 minutes and a red bus every 15 minutes. Both leave at 8:00 a.m. When do they next leave together?
quiz.explain: Multiples of 15: 15, 30. 30 is a multiple of 10. 8:00 + 30 minutes = 8:30 a.m.

quiz.q: Arjun waters plant A every 2 days and plant B every 5 days. He waters both today. How many days until he waters both on the same day again?
quiz.explain: Multiples of 5: 5, 10. 10 is a multiple of 2. So 10 days.

quiz.q: What is the smallest common multiple of 4 and 8?
quiz.explain: 8 is a multiple of 4 (4 × 2), so 8 is the smallest common multiple.

quiz.q: Aisha's cricket club meets every 3 days and her dance class every 9 days. Both are on Monday. After how many days are both on the same day again?
quiz.explain: 9 is a multiple of 3, so after 9 days.
steps: List multiples of the bigger number, 9: 9, 18 …
So both are on the same day again after 9 days.

teach.ask: Gappu asks: 'Two bells ring every 4 and every 6 minutes. How do I know when they ring together again?'
teach.praise: Ding dong! The first common multiple of 4 and 6 is 12. They ring together after 12 minutes!
teach.nudge: What should I list for each bell? Which number do I look for?

revise.summary: When two things repeat at different gaps, they happen together at common multiples of the gaps; the next time is the smallest common multiple. List multiples of the bigger gap and check the smaller.
focus: Solve bells, buses and meeting problems
Find the smallest common multiple quickly
remember: Every 4 and every 6 minutes → together every 12 minutes
If one number is a multiple of the other, the bigger is the answer: 4 and 8 → 8
traps: Don't add the gaps.
Multiplying the gaps (6 × 8 = 48) is not always the first time; 24 is.

learn.hook: Which jump sizes from 0 land on both 24 and 36? Those are their common factors!
points: A common factor of two numbers divides both of them exactly.
A jump size that lands on both 24 and 36 (starting at 0) is a common factor.
To find all common factors, list the factors of each number and pick the ones in both lists.
Some pairs like 12 and 13 have only 1 as a common factor.

example.q: Find the common factors of 18 and 24.

learn.reallife: Packing 24 laddoos and 36 barfis into the same number of equal boxes uses common factors.

items.text: Biggest common factor of 24 and 36 is ___

quiz.q: Which jump size from 0 lands on both 24 and 36?
quiz.explain: 6 divides 24 (4 jumps) and 36 (6 jumps).
steps: The jump size must divide both 24 and 36.
8 does not divide 36; 9 does not divide 24; 5 divides neither.
quiz.mistake: Picks a factor of only one number

quiz.q: Which list shows all the common factors of 24 and 36?
quiz.explain: These are in both factor lists. 8 is not a factor of 36.
steps: In both: 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 12 (8 is not a factor of 36).

quiz.q: What is the only common factor of 12 and 13?
quiz.explain: 13 is prime, and 13 does not divide 12. So only 1 is common.
steps: 13 is prime: its factors are 1 and 13.
So the only common factor is 1.
quiz.mistake: Thinks there must be a bigger one

quiz.q: Which is a common factor of 15 and 25?
quiz.explain: 5 divides both 15 and 25.
steps: A common factor divides both 15 and 25.
3 and 15 do not divide 25; 10 divides neither.

quiz.q: How many common factors do 16 and 24 have?
What is the biggest common factor of 18 and 27?
quiz.explain: Factors of 18: 1, 2, 3, 6, 9, 18. Of 27: 1, 3, 9, 27. Biggest common: 9.

quiz.q: Which pair has only 1 as a common factor?
quiz.explain: 8 = 2 × 2 × 2 and 9 = 3 × 3 share nothing but 1.
steps: 9 and 12 share 3; 6 and 15 share 3; 8 and 10 share 2.
quiz.mistake: Thinks odd and even numbers always share a factor

quiz.q: 24 laddoos and 36 barfis go into equal boxes, each box with only one kind and the same number in each. What is the most sweets per box?
quiz.explain: The number per box must divide both 24 and 36. The biggest is 12.
steps: The number in each box must divide both 24 and 36.
quiz.mistake: Uses a factor of just one number

teach.ask: Gappu wants to know the common factors of 10 and 20. How do I find them?
teach.praise: Factors of 10 are 1, 2, 5, 10, and all of them divide 20. So 1, 2, 5, 10!
teach.nudge: Which numbers divide both 10 and 20 exactly?

revise.summary: A common factor divides both numbers exactly. List the factors of each number and pick the ones in both lists; the biggest one solves 'most per box' problems.
focus: List common factors of two numbers
Find the biggest common factor
Spot pairs with only 1 as a common factor
traps: Don't pick a factor of only one number: 8 is not a factor of 36.
Don't forget 1.

topics.title: Patterns in common factors and choosing jumps

learn.hook: Find common factors of 8 and 9, 14 and 15, 20 and 21… do you notice something?
points: Two consecutive numbers (like 14 and 15) always have only 1 as a common factor.
If one number divides the other (like 6 and 18), the common factors are just the factors of the smaller number.
Two even numbers always have 2 as a common factor.
To reach one number but skip another, choose a jump size that is a factor of the first but not of the second.
Example: to land on 20 but not on 15, jump 2, 4, 10 or 20.

example.q: Which jump sizes land on 12 but skip 18?

learn.reallife: A watchman who checks every 4th house will visit house 12 but walk past house 18!

games.title: Spot the pattern
items: Two consecutive numbers have only 1 as a common factor.
The common factors of 6 and 18 are the factors of 6.
Two even numbers always have 2 as a common factor.
Two odd numbers always have only 1 as a common factor.
A jump of 5 lands on 20 but not on 15.

quiz.q: What are the common factors of 20 and 21?
quiz.explain: 20 and 21 are consecutive numbers, so only 1 divides both.
steps: Consecutive numbers have only 1 as a common factor (3 and 7 do not divide 20).
quiz.mistake: Finds a factor of only one number

quiz.q: What are the common factors of 6 and 18?
quiz.explain: 6 divides 18, so every factor of 6 divides 18 too.
steps: 6 divides 18, so every factor of 6 also divides 18.
quiz.mistake: Lists factors of the bigger number

quiz.q: Which number is a common factor of ANY two even numbers?
quiz.explain: Every even number divides by 2.
steps: 6, 10 and 4 do not divide every even number (e.g. 2 itself).

quiz.q: Which pair of odd numbers has a common factor other than 1?
quiz.explain: 9 and 15 both divide by 3.
quiz.mistake: Thinks odd numbers never share factors

quiz.q: Which jump size lands on 12 but NOT on 18?
quiz.explain: 4 divides 12 but not 18. 2, 3 and 6 divide both.
steps: The jump must divide 12 but not 18.

quiz.q: Which jump size lands on 20 but not on 15?
quiz.explain: 10 divides 20 but not 15.
steps: The jump must divide 20 but not 15.
3 does not divide 20; 5 and 1 divide both.

quiz.q: Which jump size lands on 15 but not on 20?
quiz.explain: 3 divides 15 but not 20.
steps: The jump must divide 15 but not 20.
1 and 5 divide both; 10 does not divide 15.

quiz.q: Which is true for every pair of consecutive numbers?
quiz.explain: Any number dividing both would also divide their difference, 1. So only 1 works.
steps: Consecutive numbers are one odd and one even, so they are not both even or both prime.
Any number dividing both would divide their difference, 1.
So their only common factor is 1.
Answer: Their only common factor is 1

teach.ask: Gappu wants a jump size that lands on 16 but never on 24. Which jumps can I use?
teach.praise: Factors of 16 are 1, 2, 4, 8, 16. Only 16 does not divide 24, so I must jump 16!
teach.nudge: Which factors of 16 are not factors of 24?

revise.summary: Consecutive numbers share only the factor 1. If one number divides the other, the common factors are the factors of the smaller. To land on one number but skip another, pick a factor of the first that is not a factor of the second.
focus: Find common factors using patterns
Choose a jump size that lands on one number but not another
remember: To land on 20 but not 15: jump 2, 4, 10 or 20
Land on 12 but skip 18: jump 4 or 12
traps: Don't pick a common factor when the jump must skip a number.
Odd numbers can share factors: 9 and 15 share 3.

learn.hook: Without dividing, can you tell whether 3,470 can be shared equally into 10 groups? Just look at the last digit!
points: A number is divisible by 2 if its ones digit is even: 0, 2, 4, 6 or 8.
A number is divisible by 5 if it ends in 0 or 5.
A number is divisible by 10 if it ends in 0.
A number ending in 0 is divisible by 2, 5 and 10 — all three!
Sort numbers by checking the ones digit only.

example.q: Is 3,475 divisible by 2, 5 or 10?
steps: Does not end in 0 → not by 10

learn.reallife: Shopkeepers know a price ending in 0 can be paid exactly with ₹10 notes!

games.title: Divisibility facts
items: A number ending in 0 is divisible by 10.
Every number divisible by 5 is divisible by 10.
35 is divisible by 5 but not by 10.
Every number divisible by 10 is divisible by 2.
It ends in 0, which is even.
It ends in 5, an odd digit.

quiz.q: Which number is divisible by 2?
quiz.explain: It ends in 8, an even digit.
steps: Divisible by 2 means the ones digit is even.
Only 4,568 ends in an even digit, so 4,568.

quiz.q: Which number is divisible by 5?
quiz.explain: It ends in 5.
steps: Divisible by 5 means ending in 0 or 5.
quiz.mistake: Thinks any odd number divides by 5

quiz.q: Which number is divisible by 10?
quiz.explain: It ends in 0.
steps: 7,809 and 7,089 have a 0 inside but end in 9; 7,895 ends in 5.
quiz.mistake: Picks a number with a 0 somewhere inside

quiz.q: Is 3,475 divisible by 10?
options: No, it does not end in 0
quiz.explain: Only numbers ending in 0 are divisible by 10.
steps: A number is divisible by 10 only if it ends in 0.
So No, it does not end in 0.
Answer: No, it does not end in 0

quiz.q: Which number is divisible by 2, 5 and 10?
quiz.explain: 560 ends in 0, so it is divisible by all three.
steps: Divisible by 2, 5 and 10 means ending in 0.
quiz.mistake: Checks only one of the rules

quiz.q: Which number is divisible by 5 but NOT by 2?
quiz.explain: 85 ends in 5: divisible by 5 but odd.
steps: Divisible by 5 but not by 2: ends in 5 (odd).
84 and 82 are not divisible by 5; 80 is also divisible by 2.

quiz.q: Which number is divisible by 2 but NOT by 5?
quiz.explain: 124 is even but does not end in 0 or 5.
steps: Divisible by 2 but not by 5: even, but not ending in 0 or 5.
124 is even and ends in 4, so 124.

quiz.q: How many of these are divisible by 10: 40, 45, 100, 305, 990?
quiz.explain: 40, 100 and 990 end in 0.
steps: 40, 100 and 990 end in 0; 45 and 305 end in 5.

teach.ask: Gappu found 1,250 seeds. Can I share them equally into 2 piles? 5 piles? 10 piles?
teach.praise: 1,250 ends in 0, so it can be shared into 2, 5 or 10 equal piles!
teach.nudge: What is the ones digit of 1,250?

revise.summary: Check divisibility by the ones digit: by 2 if it is even, by 5 if it is 0 or 5, by 10 if it is 0. A number ending in 0 is divisible by 2, 5 and 10.
focus: Test divisibility by 2, 5 and 10
Find numbers divisible by one but not another
Count numbers divisible by 10
traps: Look at the ones digit, not the first digit.
A 0 inside the number does not make it divisible by 10.

topics.title: True or false: factors and multiples

learn.hook: '0 is a factor of 10.' True or false? Let us test tricky statements like a maths detective!
points: 0 is not a factor of any number, because we cannot divide by 0 (0 × anything = 0, never 10).
Every number is a multiple of 1, and 1 is a factor of every number.
The sum of two consecutive numbers is always odd.
Multiples of 8 are always multiples of 4, but multiples of 4 are not always multiples of 8 (12).
To show a statement is false, one counterexample is enough.

example.q: Is 'every multiple of 4 is a multiple of 8' true?
steps: 12 ÷ 8 leaves 4, so 12 is not a multiple of 8
One counterexample shows it is false

learn.reallife: Detectives look for one clue that breaks a story. In maths, one counterexample breaks a false claim!

games.title: Decide
items: Every number is a multiple of 1.
The sum of two consecutive numbers is always odd.
One is odd, one is even.
Every multiple of 4 is a multiple of 8.
12 is a multiple of 4 but not 8.
Every multiple of 8 is a multiple of 4.
A prime number has exactly two factors.

games.title: Counterexample
pairs: All multiples of 4 are multiples of 8
All even numbers are multiples of 4

quiz.q: Is 0 a factor of 10?
options: Yes, 0 is a factor of every number
quiz.explain: A factor times some number must give 10. 0 times anything is 0.
steps: A factor of 10 times some number must give 10.
quiz.mistake: Thinks 0 is a factor of every number

quiz.q: Which statement about 0 and 1 is true?
options: Every even number is a multiple of 4
1 is a factor of every number
0 is a factor of every number
Every number is a multiple of 0
quiz.explain: Any number ÷ 1 leaves no remainder.
steps: 0 is not a factor of every number; not every even number is a multiple of 4 (e.g. 6).
So 1 is a factor of every number.
Answer: 1 is a factor of every number
quiz.mistake: Mixes up the roles of 0 and 1

quiz.q: 'The sum of two consecutive numbers is always odd.' True or false?
quiz.explain: One of them is odd and one is even, and odd + even = odd: 7 + 8 = 15.
steps: Of two consecutive numbers, one is odd and one is even.
quiz.mistake: Tests only one example and doubts it

quiz.q: Which number shows that 'every multiple of 4 is a multiple of 8' is false?
quiz.explain: 12 is a multiple of 4 but 12 ÷ 8 leaves 4.
steps: We need a multiple of 4 that is not a multiple of 8.
quiz.mistake: Picks a number that agrees with the claim

quiz.q: 'Every multiple of 6 is a multiple of 3.' True or false?
steps: So any multiple of 6 is 6 × n = 3 × (2 × n), a multiple of 3.
quiz.mistake: Thinks the claim works only one way

quiz.q: Which is a counterexample to 'all odd numbers are prime'?
quiz.explain: 9 is odd but 9 = 3 × 3, so it is not prime.
steps: A counterexample is an odd number that is not prime.

quiz.q: 'The product of two consecutive numbers is always even.' True or false?
quiz.explain: One of them is even, and any number times an even number is even: 4 × 5 = 20.
steps: Of two consecutive numbers, one is even.
Any number times an even number is even (e.g. 4 × 5 = 20).

quiz.q: Which statement is false?
options: Every factor of 24 is a factor of 12
Every factor of 12 is a factor of 24
Every multiple of 24 is a multiple of 12
quiz.explain: 8 is a factor of 24 but not of 12, so that statement is false.
steps: Every factor of 12 divides 24 (12 divides 24), so that is true; multiples of 24 are multiples of 12; 12 is a factor of 24.
But 8 is a factor of 24 and not of 12.
So 'Every factor of 24 is a factor of 12' is false.
Answer: Every factor of 24 is a factor of 12

teach.ask: Gappu says 'all even numbers are multiples of 4'. Is he right? Can you find a counterexample?
teach.praise: 6 is even but not a multiple of 4. So I was wrong!
teach.nudge: Can you find an even number that 4 does not divide?

revise.summary: Test statements about factors and multiples with examples; one counterexample shows a statement is false. 0 is not a factor of any number, and 1 is a factor of every number.
focus: Decide if statements about factors and multiples are true
Find counterexamples
Know the roles of 0 and 1
remember: 0 is not a factor of any number
Every multiple of 8 is a multiple of 4, but 12 is a multiple of 4 and not of 8
The product of two consecutive numbers is always even
traps: Don't think 0 is a factor of every number.
A claim that works one way may not work the other way.

learn.hook: The sun rises in the East every morning. Can you use it to find North, South and West? Let's become explorers!
points: The four main directions are North, South, East and West.
If you face North, East is on your right, West is on your left and South is behind you.
The sun rises in the East and sets in the West.
Between the main directions are North-East, North-West, South-East and South-West.
A right turn is a quarter turn clockwise. A left turn is a quarter turn anticlockwise.

example.q: Meena faces North. She turns right, and then turns right again. Which way is she facing now?

learn.reallife: Taxi drivers, pilots, ship captains and scouts all use directions.

items.text: Facing North, your left hand points ___

games.title: True or false?
items: If you face East, North is on your left.
Facing East, turning left (anticlockwise) takes you to North.
If you face South, East is on your right.
Facing South, West is on your right and East is on your left.
Turning right two times from North makes you face South.
North-West is between North and West.
Its name tells you: North + West.
Turning from East to South is a left turn.
East to South is clockwise, so it is a right turn.

quiz.q: You are facing North. Which direction is on your right?
quiz.explain: Facing North, East is on your right.
steps: East is on your right, West on your left, South behind you.
So East is on your right.

quiz.q: Kabir faces East and turns left. Which way does he face now?
quiz.explain: A left turn is anticlockwise. From East, anticlockwise goes to North.
steps: A left turn is a quarter turn anticlockwise.
Anticlockwise order: North → West → South → East → North.
From East, the next anticlockwise is North.

quiz.q: In which direction does the sun rise?
quiz.explain: The sun rises in the East every morning.
steps: The sun rises in the East and sets in the West.
So it rises in the East.

quiz.q: Arjun walks 3 blocks North, then 2 blocks East, then 3 blocks South. Where is he now compared with his start?
quiz.explain: The 3 blocks North and 3 blocks South cancel out. He is 2 blocks East of his start.
steps: Only the 2 blocks East are left.
So he is 2 blocks East of his start.

quiz.q: Harpreet faces West and turns right. Which way does she face now?
quiz.explain: A right turn is clockwise. From West, clockwise goes to North.
steps: A right turn is a quarter turn clockwise.
Clockwise order: North → East → South → West → North.
From West, the next clockwise is North.
quiz.mistake: Thinks a right turn always leads to East

quiz.q: Which direction is halfway between North and East?
quiz.explain: Halfway between North and East is North-East.
steps: In-between directions are named from the two main directions.
Between North and East is North-East.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up the names of the in-between directions

quiz.q: Riya walks 4 blocks East and then 4 blocks West. How many blocks is she from where she started?
quiz.explain: East and West are opposite. 4 − 4 = 0, so she is back at the start.
quiz.mistake: Adds the blocks instead of seeing the walks cancel

quiz.q: Joseph faces North and turns until he faces South. How many degrees did he turn?
quiz.explain: North to South is a half turn, which is 180°.
quiz.mistake: Thinks it is a quarter turn

quiz.q: Early in the morning Kabir stands facing the rising Sun. Which direction is on his left?
quiz.explain: The Sun rises in the East, so he faces East. With East in front, North is on the left, South on the right and West behind.
steps: Facing the rising Sun = facing East
quiz.mistake: Mixes up left and right when facing East

teach.ask: Gappu asks: 'I am facing North. Where are East, West and South?'
teach.praise: Hooray! East on my right, West on my left and South behind me. Now I won't get lost!
teach.nudge: Which direction is on my right hand? Which one is behind me?

revise.summary: The four main directions are North, South, East and West; facing North, East is on your right. The sun rises in the East. A right turn is a quarter turn clockwise and a left turn a quarter turn anticlockwise.
focus: Name directions on your left, right and behind
Find the direction after turning
Find position after walking blocks
Name in-between directions
remember: Facing North: East right, West left, South behind
Sun rises in the East and sets in the West
North to South is a half turn: 180°
traps: Don't mix up left and right.
A right turn does not always lead to East.
Opposite walks cancel: 4 East then 4 West is back at the start.

topics.title: Bird watching: directions from a landmark

learn.hook: Kites are seen to the north of the lake, ducks to the east. Can you mark them on the map?
points: A landmark is a place everyone can find, like a lake, temple or big tree.
We describe where something is by its direction from the landmark: 'The heron is south of the lake.'
On a map with North at the top: north is up, south is down, east is right and west is left.
To draw an object 'to the west of the lake', draw it on the left side of the lake.
Read every clue and place the objects one by one.

example.q: On a map, the lake is in the middle. A peacock is to the east of the lake. Where do you draw it?
example.answer: To the right of the lake

learn.reallife: Bird watchers at Bharatpur's Keoladeo park describe sightings using directions from lakes and trees.

games.title: Where on the map? (North at top)
Bird map
items: If the kingfisher is drawn to the right of the lake, it is east of the lake.
With North at the top, right is east.
A heron south of the lake is drawn above it.
If the tree is west of the lake, the lake is east of the tree.
Directions swap when you switch the landmark.
A crane drawn above the lake is to its north.

quiz.q: On a map with North at the top, a stork is drawn above the lake. Which direction is it from the lake?
quiz.explain: Above means north on such a map.
steps: On a map with North at the top, up is north.
The stork is above the lake.
So it is North of the lake.

quiz.q: Ducks are to the west of the lake. Where should Riya draw them?
options: To the left of the lake
To the right of the lake
quiz.explain: West is to the left when North is at the top.
steps: With North at the top, west is to the left.
The ducks are west of the lake.
So draw them to the left of the lake.
Answer: To the left of the lake

quiz.q: A peacock is drawn to the right of the lake. Which direction is it from the lake?
quiz.explain: Right is east on a map with North at the top.
steps: With North at the top, east is to the right.
The peacock is to the right of the lake.
So it is East of the lake.

quiz.q: The banyan tree is east of the lake. Which direction is the lake from the tree?
quiz.explain: If A is east of B, then B is west of A.
steps: If A is east of B, then B is west of A.
The tree is east of the lake.
So the lake is West of the tree.
quiz.mistake: Keeps the same direction when switching landmarks

quiz.q: Clues: the parrot is north of the lake, and the owl is south of the parrot but north of the lake. Where is the owl?
options: Between the parrot and the lake
quiz.explain: South of the parrot and north of the lake puts it between them.
steps: The owl is north of the lake, so above it.
It is also south of the parrot, so below the parrot.
So the owl is between the parrot and the lake.
Answer: Between the parrot and the lake
quiz.mistake: Uses only one of the clues

quiz.q: A heron is below the lake on the map. Which direction is it from the lake?
quiz.explain: Below means south.
steps: With North at the top, down is south.
The heron is below the lake.
So it is South of the lake.

quiz.q: Kites are to the north-east of the lake. Where on the map?
options: Up and to the right of the lake
quiz.explain: North is up and east is right.
steps: North is up and east is right.
So up and to the right of the lake.
Answer: Up and to the right of the lake

quiz.q: Which is the best landmark to describe where a bird is?
quiz.explain: A landmark must stay in one place.
steps: A landmark must be easy to find and stay in one place.
A crow, a cloud and a boat all move.

teach.ask: Gappu saw a crane to the south of the lake. Where should I draw it on our map (North at the top)?
teach.praise: South is down, so I draw the crane below the lake!
teach.nudge: Which way is south on our map?

revise.summary: A landmark is a fixed place everyone can find. On a map with North at the top, north is up, south is down, east is right and west is left; describe objects by their direction from the landmark.
focus: Say the direction of an object from a landmark
Draw objects in the right place from clues
Reverse a direction between two places
remember: Up = north, down = south, right = east, left = west
If A is east of B, B is west of A
North-east is up and to the right
traps: Don't mix up east and west.
A landmark must not move.

learn.hook: Draw your room from above, like a bird looking down. Where is your bed? Your window? Your door?
points: We can say where things are from a person's view: 'The cupboard is to Ravi's left.'
With directions, we say: 'The window is on the north wall.'
A room map is drawn from above. Draw an arrow showing North on it.
List the objects on each side: north wall, south wall, east wall, west wall.
Use simple shapes for objects: a rectangle for a bed, a square for a table.

example.q: Ravi stands in his room facing north. The window is in front of him and the door is behind him. On which walls are they?
example.answer: Window on the north wall, door on the south wall

learn.reallife: Architects draw room plans from above with a North arrow, so builders know which way windows face.

items.text: A room map is drawn as seen from ___
A map needs an arrow to show ___
Facing north, your right hand points ___
Facing north, your left hand points ___

quiz.q: Meena faces north in her room. The bed is on her right. Which wall is the bed near?
quiz.explain: Facing north, right is east.
steps: The bed is on her right.
So it is near the East wall.

quiz.q: Facing north, the cupboard is behind Arjun. Which side of the room is it?
quiz.explain: Behind is the opposite of in front: south.
steps: Facing north, behind you is the opposite way.
The opposite of north is south.
So the cupboard is on the South side.

quiz.q: Why do we draw a North arrow on a room map?
options: To show the size of the room
So anyone can tell the directions on the map
To show where the door is
quiz.explain: The arrow lets readers know which way is north, so they can work out the other directions.
steps: The North arrow shows which way north is.
From it, readers can work out east, south and west too.
So anyone can tell the directions on the map.
Answer: So anyone can tell the directions on the map

quiz.q: From which view is a room map drawn?
quiz.explain: Maps show places as seen from above.
steps: Maps show places as seen from above.
A side view or a view from the door is a picture, not a map.
So from above, like a bird.
Answer: From above, like a bird
quiz.mistake: Draws it like a side picture

quiz.q: Sara faces east. The window is on her left. Which wall is the window on?
quiz.explain: Facing east, left is north.
steps: Facing east, turn your head left: that is a quarter turn anticlockwise.
So the window is on the North wall.
quiz.mistake: Uses the 'facing north' rule for every direction

quiz.q: On Kabir's room map, the table is near the west wall. If North is at the top of the map, where is the table drawn?
quiz.explain: West is on the left of a map with North at the top.
steps: With North at the top of the map, west is on the left.
The table is near the west wall.
So it is drawn on the left side.
quiz.mistake: Thinks west is on the right

quiz.q: In a room, the door is on the south wall and the window on the north wall. Which is true?
options: They are on the same wall
The door is on the east wall
The window is opposite the door
The window is next to the door
quiz.explain: North and south walls face each other.
steps: North and south walls face each other.
The door is on the south wall and the window on the north wall.
So the window is opposite the door.
Answer: The window is opposite the door

quiz.q: Which list correctly names objects to the east of Riya if the bed is east, the desk is west and the shelf is east?
quiz.explain: The bed and the shelf are both on the east side.
steps: Pick out the objects to the east.
Bed: east ✔. Desk: west ✘. Shelf: east ✔.

teach.ask: Gappu is drawing a map of his nest-room. What must I put on it so others can read the directions?
teach.praise: I draw it from above with a North arrow, and simple shapes for things!
teach.nudge: What helps readers know which way is north?

revise.summary: A room map is drawn from above with a North arrow. We can say where things are from a person's view or by direction, listing objects on the north, south, east and west walls.
focus: Find which wall an object is on from a person's view
Place objects on a room map
Know why a map needs a North arrow
remember: Facing north: right = east, behind = south
Map with North at top: west wall on the left
traps: Don't use the 'facing north' rule when the person faces another way.
Behind is the opposite direction, not west.

learn.hook: The school bus goes from Ravi's house to the zoo. Turn left, go straight, turn right… can you follow it?
points: Describe a route with directions, turns (left/right) and road names: 'Go north on Gandhi Road, turn right into Nehru Road.'
A right turn is a quarter turn clockwise; a left turn is a quarter turn anticlockwise.
To find places in a direction from a house, look on that side of the house on the map.
Trace a route on a map with your finger or a pencil, stop by stop.
To decide which stop is nearer, count blocks or compare distances.

example.q: Ravi walks north on Gandhi Road and turns right into Nehru Road. Which direction is he walking now?

learn.reallife: Bus drivers, delivery riders and taxi drivers follow routes with turns every day.

games.title: Follow the route
games.prompt: Ravi's route: north on Gandhi Road, right into Nehru Road past the post office, then left into Park Street to the zoo gate. Put the steps in order.
items: Leave home on Gandhi Road going north

quiz.q: Ravi walks north and turns right. Which way is he walking now?
quiz.explain: A right turn from north is a quarter turn clockwise: east.
steps: A right turn is a quarter turn clockwise.

quiz.q: The bus goes east and turns left. Which way is it going now?
quiz.explain: A left turn from east is anticlockwise: north.
steps: A left turn is a quarter turn anticlockwise.

quiz.q: A map shows the park to the north of Sita's house and the market to the south. Which is north of her house?
quiz.explain: The park lies on the north side.
steps: The park is to the north; the market to the south.
Only the park is on the north side.

quiz.q: The zoo is 3 blocks from stop A and 5 blocks from stop B. Which stop is nearer?
quiz.explain: 3 blocks is less than 5 blocks.

quiz.q: Going south on MG Road, the bus turns right into Lake Road. Which way is it going?
quiz.explain: Right from south is clockwise: west.
steps: So the bus is going West.
quiz.mistake: Uses the turn rule for facing north

quiz.q: To get from home to school, you go 2 blocks east then 3 blocks north. To come back the same way, what is the first move?
quiz.explain: Retrace the last move first, in the opposite direction.
steps: To come back, undo the moves in reverse order.
The last move was 3 blocks north; undo it with 3 blocks south.
So the first move back is 3 blocks south.
quiz.mistake: Repeats the route instead of reversing it

quiz.q: The temple is east of the bus stop and the zoo is west of it. Kiran is at the bus stop. Which way should she walk to the zoo?
quiz.explain: The zoo is to the west of the stop.
steps: The zoo is west of the bus stop.
The temple is east, the other way.

quiz.q: What does 'trace a route on a map' mean?
options: Count the colours on the map
Follow the path from start to end, marking each road and turn
quiz.explain: Tracing shows the whole path step by step.
steps: Tracing a route means following it on the map.
Go from start to end, marking each road and turn.
Answer: Follow the path from start to end, marking each road and turn
quiz.mistake: Thinks tracing means copying the map

teach.ask: Gappu flies north and then turns left. Which way am I flying now?
teach.praise: From north, a left turn is anticlockwise to west!
teach.nudge: Which way does a left turn go: clockwise or anticlockwise?

revise.summary: Describe a route with directions, left and right turns and road names. A right turn is clockwise and a left turn anticlockwise; trace the route stop by stop and count blocks to compare distances.
focus: Find the new direction after a turn
Reverse a route
Find which stop is nearer
remember: North + right turn → east; east + left turn → north
To return, undo the last move first in the opposite direction
traps: Left does not always mean west.
Don't repeat a route when you need to reverse it.

learn.hook: Imagine you are a bird flying over your town. What you see from up there is what a map shows!
points: A map is a drawing of a place as seen from above (a bird's-eye view).
A map is much smaller than the real place.
The key (legend) tells what each symbol on the map means.
Most maps have North at the top.
Grid maps use a letter for the column and a number for the row, like B4, to find places quickly.

example.q: On a grid map, columns are A to E (left to right) and rows are 1 to 5 (top to bottom). The temple is in column C, row 2. How do we name its square?
steps: Write the column letter first: C

learn.reallife: Maps help us find a shop in a mall, a platform at a railway station or a route on a phone.

games.title: True or false?
items: A map is a drawing of a place seen from above.
It is like a bird's-eye view.
A map key tells us what the symbols mean.
For example, 🌳 might stand for a park.
A map shows things bigger than they really are.
A map shrinks a place so it fits on paper.
On most maps, North is at the bottom.
On most maps, North is at the top.
Grid squares like B2 help us find places on a map.
The letter gives the column and the number gives the row.

quiz.q: On a map, what does the key (legend) tell us?
quiz.explain: The key explains the symbols, like 🏫 for a school.
steps: A map uses small symbols for places.
The key (legend) lists the symbols and their meanings.
So it tells us what each symbol means.
quiz.mistake: Ignores the key and guesses what symbols mean

quiz.q: A map shows a place as it looks from…
quiz.explain: A map is a bird's-eye view, as if looking down from above.
steps: A map is a bird's-eye view.
That means looking down on the place.
quiz.mistake: Thinks of a picture taken from the side

quiz.q: On most maps, which direction is at the top?
quiz.explain: Most maps put North at the top.
steps: Maps are drawn so that one direction is always up.
Most maps put North at the top.

quiz.q: On a grid map, the school is in column B, row 4. Which square is it in?
quiz.explain: Column letter first, then row number: B4.
steps: Grid squares are named column letter first, then row number.

quiz.q: On a grid map, Arjun's house is in A1 and the market is in A4, in the same column. How many squares down is the market from his house?
quiz.explain: From row 1 to row 4 is 4 − 1 = 3 squares.

quiz.q: A map shows a whole city on one page. Compared with the real city, the map is…
quiz.explain: A map shrinks the real place so it fits on paper.
steps: A whole city fits on one page.
So the map shrinks the real place.
quiz.mistake: Thinks a map is drawn at real size

quiz.q: Which is the best landmark to tell a friend the way to your house?
options: A big red temple at the corner
quiz.explain: A landmark should be big and stay in one place. Clouds, bicycles and dogs move!
steps: A landmark should be big and stay in one place.
Clouds, a parked bicycle and a dog can move away.
So a big red temple at the corner.
Answer: A big red temple at the corner

quiz.q: On a grid map, rows are numbered 1 at the top to 5 at the bottom. The park is in C3. Which square is just above it?
quiz.explain: Moving up one row in the same column: row 3 → row 2. So C2.
steps: Just above means the same column, one row up.
Rows go 1 at the top, so up means a smaller row number: 3 → 2.
quiz.mistake: Moves along the row instead of up, or goes down

teach.ask: Gappu asks: 'What is a map? How do I know what the little pictures mean?'
teach.praise: Wow! A map is a bird's-eye drawing, and the key tells what each symbol means. Just like my view!
teach.nudge: From where is a map drawn? What tells me the meaning of each symbol?

revise.summary: A map is a bird's-eye drawing of a place, much smaller than the real place. The key explains the symbols, most maps have North at the top, and grid maps name squares by column letter then row number.
focus: Use a map key
Name grid squares like B4
Move between grid squares
Choose good landmarks
remember: Column letter first, then row number
Most maps have North at the top
traps: Don't swap column and row.
Don't count the starting square when counting moves.

learn.hook: A metro map uses coloured lines. Where two lines meet, you can change trains — that is an interchange!
points: Each metro line has a colour and a list of stations in order.
An interchange station is where two lines meet. You change trains there.
Example map — Red Line: Anand, Bagh, City Centre, Dairy, Eastgate. Blue Line: Fort, Ganga, City Centre, Hill, Ishan.
To go from Anand to Hill: Red Line to City Centre (change), then Blue Line to Hill.
Count the stations to choose the route with the fewest stops.

example.q: Using the map above, how many stops from Anand to Hill?
steps: Change to Blue: City Centre → Hill (3)

learn.reallife: The Delhi Metro has many coloured lines like Yellow, Blue and Violet with interchange stations like Rajiv Chowk.

games.title: Our metro map
pairs: Last station listed on Red Line
Last station listed on Blue Line
First station listed on Red Line
First station listed on Blue Line

quiz.q: Red Line: Anand, Bagh, City Centre, Dairy, Eastgate. Blue Line: Fort, Ganga, City Centre, Hill, Ishan. Which is the interchange?
quiz.explain: City Centre is on both lines.
steps: An interchange is a station on both lines.
Bagh is only Red; Hill and Fort are only Blue.
City Centre is on both, so City Centre.
quiz.mistake: Picks a station on only one line

quiz.q: On that map, how many stops from Anand to Eastgate on the Red Line?
quiz.explain: Anand → Bagh → City Centre → Dairy → Eastgate: 4 stops.
steps: Count moves along the Red Line, not the starting station.
Anand → Bagh (1) → City Centre (2) → Dairy (3) → Eastgate (4).

quiz.q: To go from Bagh to Hill, where must you change trains?
quiz.explain: Bagh is on Red and Hill is on Blue; they meet at City Centre.
steps: Bagh is on the Red Line; Hill is on the Blue Line.
The two lines meet only at City Centre.
quiz.mistake: Thinks every trip needs no change

quiz.q: How many stops from Fort to Dairy?
quiz.explain: Fort → Ganga → City Centre (2), change, → Dairy (3).
steps: Blue Line: Fort → Ganga (1) → City Centre (2).
Change to Red Line: City Centre → Dairy (3).

quiz.q: Which line would you take from Ganga to Ishan?
quiz.explain: Ganga and Ishan are both on the Blue Line.
steps: Ganga and Ishan are both on the Blue Line.
No change of line is needed.

quiz.q: A legend on a metro map shows ● for a station and ◎ for an interchange. What does ◎ at City Centre tell you?
quiz.explain: The legend says ◎ means interchange.
steps: The legend says ◎ means an interchange.
At an interchange you can change trains.
So you can change lines there.
Answer: You can change lines there

quiz.q: Tina can go Anand → City Centre → Hill (3 stops) or ride to Eastgate and take a bus (6 stops' time). Which is better to reach Hill fast?
options: The metro route via City Centre
quiz.explain: Fewer stops usually means less time.
steps: Metro route via City Centre: 3 stops.
Eastgate bus route: about 6 stops' time.
Fewer stops is faster, so the metro route via City Centre.
Answer: The metro route via City Centre

quiz.q: How many different stations are on this whole map (Red and Blue lines)?
quiz.explain: 5 on Red + 5 on Blue = 10, but City Centre is counted twice: 9.
steps: Red has 5 stations and Blue has 5: 5 + 5 = 10.
City Centre is on both, so it is counted twice.

teach.ask: Gappu wants to go from Bagh to Ishan on our metro map. Which route and where do I change?
teach.praise: Red Line to City Centre, then change to the Blue Line to Ishan!
teach.nudge: Which lines are Bagh and Ishan on?

revise.summary: Each metro line has a colour and stations in order. An interchange is where two lines meet and you change trains; count stations to find the route with the fewest stops.
focus: Find the interchange
Count stops on one or two lines
Choose the best route
remember: Anand → Hill: Red to City Centre, change, Blue to Hill: 3 stops
traps: Don't count the starting station as a stop.
Don't count the interchange twice.
Don't change lines when both stations are on one line.

topics.title: Making a school map and a treasure hunt

learn.hook: Hide a treasure in your school and draw a map so your friends can find it!
points: A school map shows buildings and places from above: classrooms, playground, office, library.
Make a key: choose a simple symbol for each place (□ classroom, ✚ first aid, 🌳 tree).
Draw a North arrow and keep places in the right positions compared with each other.
For a treasure hunt, mark the hidden object with ✖ and give direction clues: '10 steps east of the tap.'
Check your map by asking a friend to follow it.

example.q: Your map key says ▲ = water tap. A ✖ is drawn just east of ▲. Where is the treasure?
steps: East is to the right on a map with North at the top
example.answer: Just to the east of the water tap

learn.reallife: Scouts and guides make maps with keys for camps and treasure hunts.

games.title: Make a treasure map
items: Walk around and list the places
Draw them from above in the right positions
Mark the treasure with ✖ and write clues

quiz.q: Why does a school map need a key?
options: To show what each symbol means
quiz.explain: The key explains the symbols used.
steps: A map uses symbols for places.
The key explains what each symbol means.
So to show what each symbol means.
Answer: To show what each symbol means

quiz.q: Which is the best symbol for the school library?
options: A big red circle with no label
quiz.explain: A symbol should remind readers of the place and be listed in the key.
steps: A good symbol reminds readers of the place.
A book goes with a library; a blank or a scribble tells nothing.

quiz.q: The treasure is '10 steps north of the big tree'. On a map with North at the top, where is it drawn?
quiz.explain: North is up.
steps: With North at the top, north is up.
The treasure is north of the tree.
So draw it above the tree.

quiz.q: Ria hid a ball west of the office. On the map (North at top), which side of the office is ✖?
quiz.explain: West is on the left.
steps: With North at the top, west is on the left.
The ball is west of the office.
quiz.mistake: Thinks west is on the right

quiz.q: Which clue is the most helpful for finding hidden treasure?
options: 5 steps east of the water tap
quiz.explain: It gives a landmark, a direction and a distance.
steps: A good clue gives a landmark, a direction and a distance.
So '5 steps east of the water tap'.
Answer: 5 steps east of the water tap

quiz.q: What must every good school map have?
options: A key and a North arrow
quiz.explain: The key explains symbols and the arrow gives direction.
steps: The North arrow gives the directions.
So a key and a North arrow.
Answer: A key and a North arrow

quiz.q: Your friend follows your map but cannot find the treasure. What is the best thing to do?
options: Check the positions and clues on the map
quiz.explain: Checking helps find the mistake in the map or clues.
steps: If the treasure is not found, the map or clues may have a mistake.
Hiding it again or throwing the map away does not fix that.
So check the positions and clues on the map.
Answer: Check the positions and clues on the map

quiz.q: The office is east of the library and the playground is east of the office. Which is farthest east?
quiz.explain: Library → office → playground going east.
steps: Going east: library, then office (east of library), then playground (east of office).
The playground is the last one going east.
So the playground is farthest east.

teach.ask: Gappu hid a worm treasure 3 hops south of the swing. How do I show it on our school map?
teach.praise: I find the swing, go down 3 hops, and mark ✖ there!
teach.nudge: Which way is south on the map?

revise.summary: A school map shows places from above, with a key of simple symbols and a North arrow. For a treasure hunt, mark the spot with ✖ and give clues with a landmark, direction and distance.
focus: Make a map key with clear symbols
Place treasure using direction clues
Write a helpful treasure clue
remember: Every good map needs a key and a North arrow
A good clue: '5 steps east of the water tap'
North at top: north up, west left
traps: Vague clues like 'near something' do not help.
Don't mix up west (left) and east (right).

learn.hook: An ant walks 2 cm north and 3 cm east to reach the sugar. Is there more than one way? Which is shortest?
points: On a grid, describe moves with distance and direction: '2 cm north, then 3 cm east'.
There can be many routes to the same point: 3 cm east then 2 cm north also works.
The shortest routes along grid lines never go backwards. For 2 north and 3 east, every shortest route is 5 cm.
A route that goes south and then north again is longer.
To return home, reverse the moves: 3 cm west, then 2 cm south.

example.q: An ant goes 4 cm east, 1 cm north, 2 cm west and 1 cm north. How far is it from the start, and in which directions?
example.answer: 2 cm east and 2 cm north of the start

learn.reallife: Delivery riders look for the shortest route through the lanes of a town, just like the ant!

games.title: Ant routes
items: 2 cm north then 3 cm east reaches the same point as 3 cm east then 2 cm north.
The shortest route along the grid to 2 north and 3 east is 5 cm.
Going 1 cm south first can still give a 5 cm route to that point.
It must come back north, adding 2 cm.
To go back home after 2 north and 3 east, go 3 west and 2 south.

quiz.q: An ant walks 2 cm north and then 3 cm east. How far does it walk?
Which route reaches the same point as '2 cm north, 3 cm east'?
quiz.explain: Both end 3 cm east and 2 cm north of the start.
steps: The end point is 3 cm east and 2 cm north of the start.
Doing the same moves in a different order ends at the same point.

quiz.q: Route A: 2 N, 3 E. Route B: 1 S, 3 N, 3 E. Which is shorter?
quiz.mistake: Thinks every route to a point is the same length

quiz.q: What is the shortest grid route length to a point 3 cm north and 4 cm east?
quiz.explain: Shortest routes never go backwards: 3 + 4 = 7 cm.
steps: Shortest routes along grid lines never go backwards.

quiz.q: An ant walks 4 cm east, 1 cm north, 2 cm west and 1 cm north. Where is it from the start?
quiz.explain: East − west = 4 − 2 = 2 cm east. North = 1 + 1 = 2 cm.
quiz.mistake: Adds east and west instead of subtracting

quiz.q: After going 2 cm north and 3 cm east, how can the ant go straight back home along the grid?
quiz.explain: Undo each move in the opposite direction.
steps: To go home, undo each move in reverse order.
Undo 3 cm east with 3 cm west, then undo 2 cm north with 2 cm south.
So 3 cm west, then 2 cm south.
Answer: 3 cm west, then 2 cm south
quiz.mistake: Repeats the moves instead of reversing them

quiz.q: Which route is NOT a shortest route to 1 cm north and 2 cm east?
options: 1 cm east, 1 cm north, 1 cm east
1 cm west, 1 cm north, 3 cm east
quiz.explain: It goes west first, so it is 5 cm long instead of 3 cm.
steps: A shortest route to 1 N and 2 E is 1 + 2 = 3 cm and never goes backwards.
1 W + 1 N + 3 E = 5 cm and goes west first.
So 1 cm west, 1 cm north, 3 cm east is NOT shortest.
Answer: 1 cm west, 1 cm north, 3 cm east

quiz.q: An anthill is 3 cm south and 2 cm west of the ant. How long is the shortest grid route?
steps: Shortest grid route = south distance + west distance.

teach.ask: Gappu's friend ant walked 1 cm east, 2 cm north, then 1 cm west. Where is it compared with the start?
teach.praise: East 1 and west 1 cancel, so it is just 2 cm north of the start!
teach.nudge: What happens when you go 1 east and then 1 west?

revise.summary: On a grid, describe moves by distance and direction. Many routes reach the same point; the shortest never go backwards, and you return home by reversing the moves.
focus: Find the length of a grid route
Find the shortest route length
Find position after several moves
Reverse a route
remember: Shortest route = north–south distance + east–west distance
4 E, 1 N, 2 W, 1 N → 2 cm east, 2 cm north
Home from 2 N, 3 E: 3 W, then 2 S
traps: Don't multiply distances; add them.
Going backwards makes a route longer.
East and west cancel; subtract them.

learn.hook: The lion is at (3, 2) and the tiger at (2, 3). Are they in the same place? No! The order matters.
points: On a grid, a pair of numbers gives a position: the first number tells how far across, the second how far up.
(3, 2) means 3 across and 2 up. (2, 3) means 2 across and 3 up — a different spot!
To find the animal at a position, start at (0, 0), called the origin, go across, then up.
To write an animal's position, count across first, then up.
To plot a point, start at 0, move across, then up, and mark a dot.

example.q: Zoo grid: Lion (3, 2), Elephant (1, 4), Zebra (4, 1). Which animal is 1 across and 4 up?

learn.reallife: Seats in a cinema (row and number) and squares on a chessboard are found with pairs of letters or numbers too.

quiz.q: What does the position (3, 2) mean?
quiz.explain: The first number is across, the second is up.
steps: In a position (a, b), the first number is across and the second is up.

quiz.q: Zoo grid: Lion (3, 2), Tiger (2, 3). Are they at the same place?
options: No, the order of numbers matters
Yes, if you turn the map
quiz.explain: 3 across 2 up is a different spot from 2 across 3 up.
steps: Lion (3, 2): 3 across, 2 up. Tiger (2, 3): 2 across, 3 up.
So No, the order of numbers matters.
Answer: No, the order of numbers matters
quiz.mistake: Thinks the order does not matter

quiz.q: Lion (3, 2), Elephant (1, 4), Zebra (4, 1). Which animal is at 4 across, 1 up?
quiz.explain: (4, 1) is the zebra.

quiz.q: A peacock is 5 squares across and 2 squares up. How do you write its position?
quiz.explain: Across first, then up: (5, 2).

quiz.q: To plot (0, 4), where do you put the dot?
options: 4 straight up from the start, no moves across
quiz.explain: 0 across means stay on the up line; then 4 up.
steps: (0, 4): 0 across, so do not move across.
So the dot is 4 straight up from the start, no moves across.
Answer: 4 straight up from the start, no moves across

quiz.q: The bear is at (2, 5). The deer is 3 squares to its right on the same row. Where is the deer?
quiz.explain: Moving right adds to the across number: 2 + 3 = 5. Up stays 5.
steps: Moving right adds to the across number: 2 + 3 = 5.
The same row keeps up at 5.

quiz.q: Which position is closest to the start (0, 0)?
quiz.explain: (1, 1) is only 2 squares of walking from the start along the lines.
steps: Count grid steps from (0, 0): across + up.
quiz.mistake: Looks only at the first number

quiz.q: Rhino at (4, 3) moves 2 squares up. What is its new position?
quiz.explain: Moving up adds to the second number: 3 + 2 = 5.
steps: Moving up adds to the second number.

teach.ask: Gappu's nest is at (2, 4) on the zoo grid. How do I find it starting from (0, 0)?
teach.praise: Go 2 across first, then 4 up — there is my nest!
teach.nudge: Which number tells me to go across?

revise.summary: On a grid, a pair of numbers gives a position: the first number is how far across and the second how far up, starting from (0, 0). The order matters.
focus: Read and write positions like (3, 2)
Find an animal at a position
Plot points and move them
remember: Moving right changes the first number; moving up changes the second
traps: Don't read up first.
0 across means do not move across at all.

learn.hook: How can a whole state fit on one page? The secret is the map scale!
points: A map scale tells how much real distance 1 cm on the map stands for.
If 1 cm = 5 km, then 4 cm on the map is 4 × 5 = 20 km in real life.
Real distance = map length × the scale distance.
Map length = real distance ÷ the scale distance.
Always write the units: cm on the map, m or km in real life.

example.q: On a map, 1 cm stands for 5 km. Two towns are 4 cm apart on the map. How far apart are they really?

learn.reallife: Road atlases, school plans and phone maps all use scales. Zooming in on a phone changes the scale!

items.q: 1 cm = 2 km. 10 km in real life = ? cm on the map

quiz.q: A map scale is 1 cm = 10 km. Two villages are 3 cm apart on the map. How far apart are they really?
On Riya's school map, 1 cm = 100 m. The playground is 7 cm from the gate on the map. How far is it really?
steps: Real distance = map length × scale distance.
quiz.mistake: Adds a zero too many or too few

quiz.q: A map scale is 1 cm = 2 km. Two towns are 12 km apart. How far apart are they on the map?
quiz.explain: Each 2 km takes 1 cm. 12 ÷ 2 = 6 cm.
steps: Map length = real distance ÷ scale distance.

quiz.q: On Aisha's map, 1 cm = 50 km. Two cities are 4 cm apart. How far apart are they really?
steps: Real distance = map length × scale distance.

quiz.q: A plan of a cricket ground uses 1 cm = 5 m. The ground is 9 cm long on the plan. How long is it really?
steps: Real length = plan length × scale distance.
quiz.mistake: Adds the numbers instead of multiplying

quiz.q: Map A uses 1 cm = 1 km. Map B uses 1 cm = 2 km. Both show the same city on the same paper. On which map does the city look bigger?
quiz.explain: On Map A each km takes 1 cm. On Map B each km takes only half a cm. So the city looks bigger on Map A.
steps: Map A: 1 km takes 1 cm. Map B: 1 km takes only 1/2 cm.
So the same city takes more paper on Map A.
The city looks bigger on Map A.
quiz.mistake: Thinks the bigger number in the scale makes things look bigger

quiz.q: A map scale is 1 cm = 25 km. A route has three parts of 2 cm, 3 cm and 1 cm on the map. How long is the real route?
quiz.explain: Total map length: 2 + 3 + 1 = 6 cm. Real: 6 × 25 = 150 km.
quiz.mistake: Gives the map length in cm, or adds 25 only once

quiz.q: A map scale is 1 cm = 20 m. A park is 80 m wide. How wide is it on the map?
steps: Map width = real width ÷ scale distance.

teach.ask: Gappu asks: 'How can a big city fit on a small map? What is a scale?'
teach.praise: Clever! Each cm on the map stands for a real distance, so I multiply to find how far!
teach.nudge: What does 1 cm on the map stand for? How do I find the real distance?

revise.summary: A map scale tells how much real distance 1 cm on the map stands for. Real distance = map length × scale distance; map length = real distance ÷ scale distance.
focus: Find real distance from a map
Find map length from real distance
Compare maps with different scales
remember: Map length = real distance ÷ scale distance
Write cm on the map and m or km in real life
traps: Don't add the map length and the scale.
Don't multiply when finding map length; divide.
A bigger number in the scale makes things look smaller.

learn.hook: Class 5 did a survey: how do you come to school? Let's be data detectives and find the story in the numbers!
points: Tally marks are drawn in bundles of 5 (four lines and one across) to count quickly.
From data we can find the most, the least, the total and the difference.
We can also find fractions of the data: 20 out of 40 is half.
Only say what the data really shows. Do not guess things it does not tell.

example.q: 40 children answered: 20 walk, 12 come by bus, 8 cycle. What fraction walk? How many more walk than cycle?
example.answer: Half walk; 12 more walk than cycle

learn.reallife: Schools, shops and doctors collect data to make good decisions.

games.title: Data: dogs 10, cats 6, fish 4
buckets: Can be answered from the data
items: How many more dogs than cats?
Which pet is the least common?

items.q: Bars of 12 and 7: how many more?

quiz.q: A tally shows two bundles of five and 3 more lines. What number is that?
40 children were asked how they come to school. 20 walk. What fraction of the children walk?
quiz.mistake: Writes the number who walk over the number who don't (20/20)

quiz.q: In the same survey, 20 children walk and 8 cycle. How many more walk than cycle?
quiz.mistake: Adds instead of finding the difference

quiz.q: Temperatures this week: Mon 30°, Tue 32°, Wed 29°, Thu 33°. Which day was the hottest?
quiz.explain: 33° is the highest, so Thursday was the hottest.
steps: The hottest day has the highest temperature.

quiz.q: Favourite part of Diwali: Sweets 15, Diyas 12, Rangoli 9, Lights 4. Which statement is TRUE?
options: Lights are more popular than Diyas
Rangoli and Diyas got the same votes
quiz.explain: 15 is the biggest number, so Sweets got the most votes.
steps: Check each statement with the numbers.
Lights 4 < Diyas 12; Rangoli 9 ≠ Diyas 12; Lights got 4 votes, not 0.
Sweets 15 is the biggest, so 'Sweets are the most popular' is true.
Answer: Sweets are the most popular

quiz.q: In that Diwali survey (15, 12, 9 and 4 votes), how many children voted in all?
Books read this month: Riya 5, Arjun 8, Meena 6, Kabir 5. How many children read more than 5 books?
quiz.explain: Arjun (8) and Meena (6) read more than 5. Riya and Kabir read exactly 5, which is not more than 5.
steps: Riya and Kabir read 5, and 5 is not more than 5.
So 2 children read more than 5 books.
quiz.mistake: Counts children who read exactly 5 as 'more than 5'

quiz.q: In a quiz, Team A scored 45 and Team B scored 60. By how many points did Team B win?
quiz.explain: 60 − 45 = 15 points.
steps: Winning margin = bigger score − smaller score.

teach.ask: Gappu asks: 'What can we learn from a table of numbers?'
teach.praise: Wow! Data tells us the most, the least, the total and how many more. I'm a data detective now!
teach.nudge: What questions can I answer from the numbers? Can I find the biggest and the total?

revise.summary: Tally marks are drawn in bundles of 5. From data we can find the most, the least, the total, the difference and fractions, but we only say what the data really shows.
focus: Read tally marks
Find most, least, total and difference
Find a fraction of the data
Pick true statements about data
traps: Don't count a tally bundle as 1.
Don't leave out the smallest number in a total.
'More than 5' does not include 5.

learn.hook: Can one little mango picture stand for 5 mangoes? In a pictograph, it can!
points: A pictograph shows data using pictures or symbols.
The key tells how many things one symbol stands for, like 🥭 = 5 mangoes.
To read it, multiply the number of symbols by the key.
Half a symbol stands for half the key number.
Choose a key that keeps the pictures easy to draw and count.

example.q: Key: 🍎 = 10 apples. A shop's row shows 🍎🍎🍎🍎 and half an 🍎. How many apples?

learn.reallife: Pictographs are used in newspapers, school charts and posters to show data in a fun way.

items.text: Half a ☀️ stands for ___ sunny day

quiz.q: Key: 🍎 = 10 apples. A shop's row shows 🍎🍎🍎🍎. How many apples does the shop have?
quiz.explain: 4 symbols × 10 = 40 apples.
quiz.mistake: Counts the symbols but forgets the key

quiz.q: Key: ⭐ = 4 children. A row shows 3 and a half ⭐. How many children is that?
quiz.explain: 3 stars = 12 children. Half a star = 2 children. 12 + 2 = 14.
quiz.mistake: Ignores the half symbol, or counts it as a full one

quiz.q: Key: 🏏 = 10 runs. Kabir has 🏏🏏🏏🏏🏏🏏 and Joseph has 🏏🏏🏏. How many more runs did Kabir score?
quiz.mistake: Gives the difference in symbols (3) and forgets the key

quiz.q: Key: 🙂 = 5 children. How many 🙂 are needed to show 35 children?
quiz.explain: 35 ÷ 5 = 7 symbols.
quiz.mistake: Draws one symbol for each child

quiz.q: Why does a pictograph have a key?
options: So we know how many each symbol stands for
quiz.explain: Without the key we cannot tell if one symbol means 1, 5 or 10 things.
steps: One symbol may stand for 1, 5, 10 or more things.
So we know how many each symbol stands for.
Answer: So we know how many each symbol stands for
quiz.mistake: Thinks the symbols always mean 1 each

quiz.q: Key: 📚 = 20 books. The library row shows 📚📚 and half a 📚. How many books?
A pictograph will show 200, 350 and 500 visitors at a mela. Which key is the best choice?
quiz.explain: With 50, the rows need 4, 7 and 10 symbols. Easy to draw and read!
steps: A good key divides the numbers and keeps symbols few.
1, 3 or 7 visitors per symbol needs too many symbols or does not divide evenly. So 1 symbol = 50 visitors.
quiz.mistake: Picks a key that needs hundreds of symbols or does not divide the numbers

quiz.q: Key: 🌸 = 6 flowers. Meena picked 24 flowers. How many 🌸 symbols show this?
quiz.explain: 24 ÷ 6 = 4 symbols.
quiz.mistake: Uses the key number as the answer

teach.ask: Gappu asks: 'In a pictograph, how do I know how many things one picture means?'
teach.praise: Yay! Read the key, then multiply the symbols by it. Easy-peasy!
teach.nudge: What part of the pictograph tells me what a symbol is worth? What do I do then?

revise.summary: A pictograph shows data with symbols, and the key tells how many each symbol stands for. Multiply the number of symbols by the key; half a symbol is half the key.
focus: Read a pictograph using the key
Find how many symbols show a number
Choose a good key
traps: Don't count symbols and forget the key.
Don't ignore half symbols or count them as full ones.

topics.title: Two-wheelers on the road: pictographs with a scale

learn.hook: Students counted two-wheelers passing their school in 15 minutes. Each 🛵 stands for 3 vehicles!
points: With the scale 🛵 = 3 vehicles, multiply the number of icons by 3.
Pictograph (🛵 = 3 vehicles): Scooters 🛵×6, Motorcycles 🛵×8, Mopeds 🛵×4, E-scooters 🛵×2.
So scooters = 6 × 3 = 18, motorcycles = 24, mopeds = 12, e-scooters = 6. The maximum is motorcycles.
Total = 18 + 24 + 12 + 6 = 60 vehicles. Difference: motorcycles − mopeds = 24 − 12 = 12.
To redraw with 🛵 = 6 vehicles, divide each value by 6: 3, 4, 2 and 1 icons.

example.q: Using the pictograph, how many more motorcycles than scooters passed?

learn.reallife: Traffic police count vehicles at busy crossings to plan signals and lanes.

quiz.q: Pictograph (🛵 = 3 vehicles): Scooters 🛵×6, Motorcycles 🛵×8, Mopeds 🛵×4, E-scooters 🛵×2. How many scooters passed?
quiz.explain: 6 icons × 3 = 18 scooters.
quiz.mistake: Counts icons instead of using the scale

quiz.q: In the two-wheeler pictograph (🛵 = 3), which type passed most often?
quiz.explain: Motorcycles have the most icons, 8, which is 24 vehicles.
steps: The row with the most icons passed most often.

quiz.q: Using 🛵 = 3, how many motorcycles passed (8 icons)?
What is the total number of two-wheelers (6, 8, 4 and 2 icons; 🛵 = 3)?
quiz.explain: 20 icons × 3 = 60 vehicles.

quiz.q: How many more motorcycles (8 icons) than mopeds (4 icons) passed, with 🛵 = 3?
quiz.mistake: Subtracts icons and forgets the scale

quiz.q: If the same data is redrawn with 🛵 = 6, how many icons show the 24 motorcycles?
quiz.explain: 24 ÷ 6 = 4 icons.
quiz.mistake: Keeps the old number of icons

quiz.q: With 🛵 = 6, how many icons show the 6 e-scooters?
quiz.explain: 6 ÷ 6 = 1 icon.

quiz.q: Why might we choose 🛵 = 6 instead of 🛵 = 3?
options: To change the real number of vehicles
To draw fewer icons for big numbers
quiz.explain: A bigger scale needs fewer icons; the data stays the same.
steps: A bigger scale means each icon stands for more vehicles.
So big numbers need fewer icons; the real data stays the same.
So we choose it to draw fewer icons for big numbers.
Answer: To draw fewer icons for big numbers
quiz.mistake: Thinks a new scale changes the data

teach.ask: Gappu drew 5 🛵 icons with the key 🛵 = 3. How many vehicles is that? And how many icons with 🛵 = 5?
teach.praise: 5 × 3 = 15 vehicles. With 🛵 = 5 I need only 3 icons!
teach.nudge: What does each icon stand for?

revise.summary: With a scale like 🛵 = 3 vehicles, multiply icons by 3 to read the data. To redraw with a bigger scale, divide each value by the new scale; the data stays the same.
focus: Read a pictograph with a scale
Find the maximum, total and difference
Redraw with a new scale
traps: Don't subtract icons and forget the scale.
A new scale does not change the real numbers.

learn.hook: Asha and Ravi both have 24 hours a day. How differently do they spend them?
points: A table or a picture record can show how much time someone spends on each activity.
Asha: sleep 9 h, school 7 h, play 2 h, study 2 h, TV 1 h, meals 1 h 30 min, other 1 h 30 min. Ravi: sleep 8 h, school 7 h, play 1 h, study 2 h, TV 4 h, meals 1 h, other 1 h.
To compare, find the difference for each activity: Ravi watches TV 4 − 1 = 3 hours more than Asha.
The times in a full day must add up to 24 hours.
A balanced routine has enough sleep, play and study, and not too much screen time.

example.q: How much more does Asha sleep than Ravi?

learn.reallife: Doctors say children your age need about 9–11 hours of sleep and some active play every day.

games.title: Compare the routines
items: Ravi watches 3 hours more TV than Asha.
The table shows 7 h for both.
Asha's activities add up to 24 hours.

quiz.q: Asha watches TV for 1 hour a day and Ravi for 4 hours. How many more hours does Ravi watch?
quiz.explain: 4 − 1 = 3 hours.
steps: How many more = Ravi's TV − Asha's TV.

quiz.q: How much more does Asha sleep than Ravi (9 h and 8 h)?
quiz.explain: 9 − 8 = 1 hour.
steps: How much more = Asha's sleep − Ravi's sleep.

quiz.q: Who plays more, and by how much (Asha 2 h, Ravi 1 h)?
quiz.explain: 2 − 1 = 1 hour more for Asha.
steps: Asha plays 2 h, Ravi 1 h, so Asha plays more.

quiz.q: Ravi's times: sleep 8, school 7, play 1, study 2, TV 4, meals 1, other 1 (hours). What is the total in hours?
On which activity do Asha and Ravi spend the same time?
quiz.explain: Both spend 7 h at school and 2 h studying.
steps: Compare row by row: TV 1 vs 4, sleep 9 vs 8, play 2 vs 1.
School 7 vs 7 and study 2 vs 2 are equal.

quiz.q: Whose routine is more balanced?
options: Asha's — more sleep and play, less TV
quiz.explain: Asha sleeps more, plays more and watches less TV.
steps: A balanced routine has enough sleep and play and not too much TV.
Asha sleeps 9 h vs 8 h, plays 2 h vs 1 h, watches TV 1 h vs 4 h.
So Asha's routine is more balanced.
Answer: Asha's — more sleep and play, less TV
quiz.mistake: Thinks more TV time is better

quiz.q: Asha spends 1 h 30 min on meals and Ravi spends 1 h. How many more minutes does Asha spend?
quiz.explain: 90 − 60 = 30 minutes.

quiz.q: If Ravi cuts his TV time by 2 hours and adds it to play, how many hours does he play?
quiz.explain: 1 + 2 = 3 hours of play.
steps: He adds the 2 hours cut from TV.
quiz.mistake: Takes the time away from play too

teach.ask: Gappu sleeps 6 hours and watches the sky-TV for 5 hours. His friend sleeps 10 hours and watches 1 hour. Whose day is more balanced?
teach.praise: My friend sleeps more and watches less TV, so my friend's day is more balanced!
teach.nudge: Who gets more sleep and less screen time?

revise.summary: A table can show how much time someone spends on each activity; a full day adds up to 24 hours. Compare routines by finding the difference for each activity.
focus: Compare time spent on activities
Check that a day adds to 24 hours
Decide which routine is more balanced
remember: Ravi watches TV 4 − 1 = 3 hours more than Asha
Times in a day add up to 24 hours
traps: Don't give one person's time when asked for the difference.
Don't leave out an activity when adding.
More TV does not mean a better routine.

topics.title: A day in my life as a bar graph

learn.hook: Turn your whole day into bars! The longest bar shows what you do most.
points: Record your 24-hour routine in hours and minutes. Check that it adds up to 24 hours.
To draw a bar graph: draw two axes, write the activities along one, mark a scale (like 1 square = 1 hour) along the other.
Draw each bar as long as its time. Keep bars the same width with equal gaps.
Strip graph: cut paper strips as long as each measured length (like index fingers) and paste them side by side — it becomes a bar graph.
Give the graph a title and label both axes.

example.q: Meena's day: sleep 10 h, school 6 h, play 2 h, homework 2 h, meals 2 h, other ? Find 'other'.

learn.reallife: Health apps show your sleep and exercise as bars every day.

games.title: Draw a bar graph
items: Collect the data in a table
Draw the two axes and mark a scale
Draw a bar of the right length for each item
Check each bar against the table

items.q: Sleep 10 h, scale 1 square = 1 h: squares?
School 6 h, scale 1 square = 2 h: squares?
Bar of 4 squares, 1 square = 30 min: minutes?

quiz.q: Meena's day: sleep 10 h, school 6 h, play 2 h, homework 2 h, meals 2 h and other. How many hours is 'other'?
In Meena's bar graph, which activity has the longest bar?
quiz.explain: Sleep, 10 hours, is the most.
steps: The longest bar shows the most time.
Sleep is 10 h; school 6 h; play, homework and meals 2 h each.
So sleep has the longest bar.

quiz.q: With the scale 1 square = 1 hour, how many squares long is the bar for 6 hours of school?
quiz.explain: 6 hours ÷ 1 hour per square = 6 squares.

quiz.q: With the scale 1 square = 2 hours, how many squares show 10 hours of sleep?
quiz.explain: 10 ÷ 2 = 5 squares.

quiz.q: Children paste paper strips as long as their index fingers: Ali 6 cm, Bina 5 cm 5 mm, Chetan 6 cm 2 mm. Whose strip is longest?
quiz.explain: 6 cm 2 mm = 62 mm is the longest.
steps: Change all to mm: Ali 60 mm, Bina 55 mm, Chetan 62 mm.

quiz.q: In that strip graph, whose finger is shortest?
quiz.explain: 5 cm 5 mm = 55 mm is the shortest.

quiz.q: What must all the bars in a bar graph have the same?
quiz.explain: Only the lengths change; widths stay equal so the graph is fair.
steps: In a bar graph only the bar lengths change with the data.
For a fair graph, all bars keep the same width.

quiz.q: A bar for homework is 3 squares long and each square is 30 minutes. How long is homework?
quiz.explain: 3 × 30 = 90 minutes = 1 hour 30 minutes.

teach.ask: Gappu wants to draw a bar graph of his day. What do I need to remember?
teach.praise: I choose a scale, keep bars the same width, and add a title and labels!
teach.nudge: What makes a bar graph easy to read?

revise.summary: To draw a bar graph, draw two axes, write the activities on one, mark a scale on the other, and draw equal-width bars as long as each value. A strip graph pastes measured strips side by side.
focus: Find a missing time in a 24-hour day
Find bar length using a scale
Compare lengths in a strip graph
Read a bar using its scale
remember: All bars the same width; add a title and axis labels
traps: Don't ignore the scale.
Compare mm too: 5 cm 5 mm is shorter than 6 cm.
Don't read squares as hours when each is 30 minutes.

learn.hook: Which fruit does your class love most? A bar graph shows the winner in one look!
points: A bar graph uses bars of different lengths to show data.
The longer or taller the bar, the bigger the number it shows.
The scale on the side tells what each line stands for, like 1 line = 2 children.
All bars should be the same width with equal gaps between them.
Bars can go up (vertical) or across (horizontal).

example.q: On a bar graph each line stands for 2 children. The Mango bar reaches 6 lines. How many children chose mango?

learn.reallife: Cricket scorecards on TV, rainfall charts and school results often use bar graphs.

games.title: Fewest to most votes
games.prompt: Favourite game votes: Kabaddi 9, Cricket 15, Football 11, Kho-kho 6. Order the bars from shortest to tallest

games.title: True or false?
items: In a bar graph, all bars should be the same width.
Only the length should change, so the graph is fair.
The longest bar shows the smallest number.
The longest bar shows the biggest number.
We need the scale to read the numbers on a bar graph.
The scale tells what each line stands for.
Bars can be drawn going across, not only up.
Horizontal bar graphs work the same way.
If 1 line = 5, a bar 4 lines tall shows 4.

quiz.q: Favourite fruits in Class 5: Mango 12, Banana 8, Apple 5, Grapes 10. Which fruit has the tallest bar?
quiz.explain: Mango has the biggest number, 12, so its bar is tallest.
steps: The tallest bar shows the biggest number.
quiz.mistake: Picks the fruit with the shortest bar

quiz.q: Using the same fruit graph (Mango 12, Banana 8), how many more children chose Mango than Banana?
In the fruit graph (Mango 12, Banana 8, Apple 5, Grapes 10), how many children voted in all?
On a bar graph, each line stands for 2 children. A bar reaches 7 lines. How many children does it show?
quiz.explain: 7 × 2 = 14 children.
quiz.mistake: Reads the number of lines and forgets the scale

quiz.q: Runs in each over: Over 1 = 6, Over 2 = 10, Over 3 = 4, Over 4 = 12. Which over had the most runs?
quiz.explain: Over 4 has the tallest bar with 12 runs.
quiz.mistake: Picks the over with the shortest bar

quiz.q: Using the runs graph (6, 10, 4 and 12 runs), how many runs were scored in all 4 overs?
quiz.mistake: Makes an adding slip or misses one over

quiz.q: Rainy days: June 8, July 15, August 12, September 6. Which month had the fewest rainy days?
quiz.explain: September has the shortest bar, 6 days.
quiz.mistake: Picks the month with the most rain
